{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/adr/0003-gx-only-for-v1.md",
  "content": "# ADR 0003 — GX-only for v1; DQX deferred to v1.1 for DLT/streaming\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-05-24\n- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771\n\n## Context\n\nDataQ v1 must run data quality checks across four datasource types: Snowflake, ADLS Gen2, AWS S3, and Unity Catalog (Databricks). Two viable DQ frameworks were considered:\n\n- **Great Expectations (GX Core v1)** — mature, multi-backend, supports Snowflake / Pandas (for flat files) / Spark via DataFrame datasources. Unified suite/expectation/result model. Batch-only.\n- **Databricks Labs DQX** — newer, native to Databricks runtime. First-class streaming and Delta Live Tables (DLT) support. Lower runtime overhead on Spark. Unity Catalog-aware. Not multi-backend.\n\nThe roadmap defers DLT / streaming functionality to v1.1.\n\n## Decision\n\n**Use Great Expectations (GX Core v1) as the sole DQ framework for v1, across all four datasource types. Defer DQX to v1.1 for the streaming / DLT use case.**\n\nTo enable the v1.1 swap cleanly:\n\n- Wrap the Unity Catalog GX execution behind a `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` interface in Week 3.\n- DQX in v1.1 will implement the same interface as a `DqxCheckRunner` alongside the existing GX runner.\n- A result-shape adapter will normalise DQX output into DataQ's existing `check_results` schema.\n- UI exposes `engine: gx | dqx` toggle on UC suites in v1.1.\n- Batch UC tables via SQL Warehouse remain on GX even after v1.1 (no migration of working code).\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- One framework → one result schema, one suite model, one check-editor UI, one MCP tool contract across all four datasources.\n- The 8-week timeline is feasible with a single framework; two would not be.\n- The interface-first approach in Week 3 makes the v1.1 DQX add additive, not migrative.\n\n**Negative**\n- GX has no streaming support — streaming/DLT DQ is impossible in v1 (acceptable; deferred to v1.1).\n- GX-on-Spark for Unity Catalog is higher-overhead than DQX on the same workload. Acceptable for v1 batch volumes.\n- GX Core v1 API has drifted across point releases — must pin the version in `environment.yml` and avoid tracking latest.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **GX for Snowflake / flat files, DQX for Unity Catalog from v1** — rejected. Mixing frameworks in v1 doubles the result-shape handling and forces a check-editor variant per framework; estimated 1 extra week of work for ~0 user-visible benefit in v1 (no streaming requirement yet).\n- **DQX-only** — rejected. DQX is Databricks-native and does not cover Snowflake / S3 / ADLS as first-class targets.\n- **Build a custom DQ framework** — rejected outright. Out of scope; both GX and DQX are mature.\n\n## Related\n\n- v1.1 streaming/DLT entry in `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` \"Deferred to v1.1\".\n- `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` interface (Week 3 deliverable).\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/adr/0004-orchestration-abstraction.md",
  "content": "# ADR 0004 — Unified `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction for ADF and Apache Airflow\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-05-24\n- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771\n\n## Context\n\nDataQ integrates with Azure Data Factory (ADF) and Apache Airflow. The original product framing listed ADF as a \"5th datasource type,\" which conflates orchestration with data storage:\n\n- **Datasources** (Snowflake, ADLS Gen2, S3, Unity Catalog) are stores against which DQ checks are written.\n- **Orchestrators** (ADF, Airflow) are workflow engines whose pipeline/DAG runs we observe and react to. We do not write DQ checks against the orchestrator itself.\n\nTreating orchestrators as datasources pollutes the suite/check editor, mixes unrelated concerns in the data model, and makes the upcoming Airflow integration look like a one-off rather than a sibling of ADF.\n\n## Decision\n\n**Treat ADF and Apache Airflow as orchestration integrations behind a single `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction. They are NOT datasources and never appear in the connection editor / check editor / suite model as a queryable target.**\n\n### Responsibilities (identical across both providers)\n\n1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table with a `provider` column (`adf` | `airflow`) and `provider_run_id`.\n2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific webhook channels (see table below).\n3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings` (composite key: `provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs (no point running checks on data that wasn't loaded).\n\n### Interface\n\n```\nclass OrchestrationProvider:\n    def parse_event(self, payload: bytes, headers: dict) -> RunUpdate: ...\n    def fetch_run_detail(self, provider_run_id: str) -> RunDetail: ...\n    def list_recent_runs(self, since: datetime) -> list[RunUpdate]: ...\n```\n\nBoth `AdfProvider` and `AirflowProvider` implement this interface. Service code routes by `provider` enum, never by provider-specific branching.\n\n### Event channels per provider\n\n| Provider | Failure / success channel | Auth | Polling fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| ADF | Azure Monitor alert rule → webhook `POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/adf` | Shared-secret header (Azure Monitor's only auth mode) | ADF REST API every 10 min |\n| Airflow | DAG `on_success_callback` / `on_failure_callback` → webhook `POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow` | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns` every 10 min |\n\n### UI surface\n\nOrchestrators appear ONLY in:\n- The orchestration status panel on the results dashboard.\n- The trigger-binding configuration UI.\n\nThey do NOT appear in the connection editor's \"pick a datasource\" list or the check editor's table picker.\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- Adding a third orchestration provider in the future (Prefect, Dagster, etc.) is a new `OrchestrationProvider` implementation — no data-model or UI churn.\n- `pipeline_runs` stays clean as a single events stream regardless of provider.\n- `trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic from day one.\n- Forces correct mental model — orchestrator is not a datasource.\n\n**Negative**\n- Slightly more abstraction upfront in Week 2 vs hardcoding ADF, then refactoring when Airflow is added. Accepted because Airflow is in-scope for v1, not a hypothetical future.\n- Airflow callback adoption is voluntary on the user side (we cannot mutate their DAGs). Mitigated by documenting the polling fallback and providing a copy-paste `dataq_airflow_callback` snippet.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **Treat ADF as a 5th datasource (original framing)** — rejected. Conflates orchestration with storage; pollutes the check editor and the data model.\n- **Hardcode ADF in v1, abstract later when Airflow is added** — rejected. Refactoring after `pipeline_runs` has data is more expensive than designing the abstraction once upfront.\n\n## Related\n\n- `pipeline_runs` and `trigger_bindings` schema lands in Week 1/2.\n- `OrchestrationProvider` interface lands in Week 2 alongside both implementations.\n- Future: ADR 0006 (ADF webhook auth) and ADR 0007 (Airflow callback model) will detail the provider-specific event channels.\n"
}
```

  "content": "# Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)\n\nEach ADR captures a single significant architecture decision: the context, the decision, the consequences, and the alternatives considered. New ADRs are append-only — supersede an old decision by adding a new ADR and marking the old one's status as `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.\n\n## Format\n\n- File name: `NNNN-short-kebab-slug.md` (zero-padded 4-digit sequence)\n- Frontmatter fields: Status, Date, Deciders\n- Sections: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, Related (optional)\n- Keep each ADR short — 1–2 pages. If it grows past that, the decision is probably two decisions.\n\n## Index\n\n| # | Title | Status |\n|---|---|---|\n| [0001](0001-trunk-based-branching.md) | Trunk-based branching with squash-merge into `main` | Accepted |\n| [0002](0002-conventional-commits.md) | Conventional commits for PR titles and commit messages | Accepted |\n| [0003](0003-gx-only-for-v1.md) | GX-only for v1; DQX deferred to v1.1 for DLT/streaming | Accepted |\n| [0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) | Unified `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction for ADF and Airflow | Accepted |\n\n## Pending (to be written in their respective weeks)\n\n| # | Topic | Target week |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0005 | Severity tier weights (warn / fail / critical → health score) | Week 3, Day 1 |\n| 0006 | ADF webhook authentication (shared secret + Key Vault rotation) | Week 2 |\n| 0007 | Airflow callback model (HMAC signing + polling fallback) | Week 2 |\n| 0008 | MCP mounted at `/mcp` with Azure AD auth | Week 7 |\n| 0009 | Repo layout — flat monorepo (`backend/` + `frontend/`) | Week 1 |\n"

# Code review — PR #1 `chore: add .gitignore`

**Overview**
Adds a 130-line `.gitignore` for the monorepo covering Python, Node, env/secrets, IDE, OS, Docker, conda, logs, and Azure creds. Single new file, no behavioural code. Aligns with PR 0 (repo governance).

## Findings

### 🔴 Bug — `.vscode/` negation patterns don't work
Lines 78, 80–81:
```
.vscode/
!.vscode/extensions.json
!.vscode/settings.shared.json
```
Per `man gitignore`: *"It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded."* Because `.vscode/` is ignored as a whole directory, the two `!` negations are silently no-ops — those files will never be tracked. Either ignore specific files instead of the whole directory, or drop the misleading negation lines.

Suggested fix:
```
# track shared VS Code recommendations; ignore personal overrides
.vscode/*
!.vscode/extensions.json
!.vscode/settings.shared.json
```

### 🟡 Suspect pattern — `*.conda-lock.cache/`
Line 32. `conda-lock` doesn't produce per-project `<name>.conda-lock.cache/` directories in normal use. Either typo (perhaps intended `.conda-lock-cache/`) or unnecessary. Recommend removing or replacing with the actual artefact name once observed.

### 🟡 Risk — `lib/` is overly broad
Line 13. `lib/` ignores any directory named `lib` at any depth (e.g., `backend/app/lib/` if it ever exists). This pattern comes from the standard Python venv gitignore but is dangerous in a monorepo where `lib/` is a common source-folder name. Recommend scoping it to known venv locations or removing.

### 🟡 Duplicates across sections
- `build/` — lines 7 (Python) and 53 (Node)
- `dist/` — lines 9 (Python) and 52 (Node)

Harmless but redundant; consolidate into a single "build artefacts" section.

### 🟢 Suggestion — add `.claude/settings.local.json`
Line 130 ignores `.claude/cache/`. Worth also adding `.claude/settings.local.json` (and any `.claude/settings.personal.json`) — per Claude Code conventions, `settings.local.json` is for individual-developer overrides and should never be committed. The shared `settings.json` stays tracked.

### 🟢 Minor cleanup
- `*$py.class` (line 4) — Jython-specific, not relevant to CPython 3.11.
- `.docker/` (line 73) — Docker doesn't write a project-local `.docker/`; it lives in `~/.docker/`. Likely a no-op.
- Consider adding `*.orig` and `*.rej` (merge conflict artefacts) for completeness.

## Correctness, security, performance
- ✅ Secret patterns are solid: `.env*` with `!.env.example` escape works, plus `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.crt`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `secrets/`, `credentials.json`. Covers most accidental-commit risks.
- ✅ Test plan in PR description is testable and small.
- ⚪ No code, no test coverage implications.
- ⚪ No performance impact.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** The `.vscode/` negation bug is the only thing that materially misleads future contributors; everything else is polish. Recommend fixing that one in a fixup commit on this branch before merge, then merging.

---

Now posting these findings to PR #1 as comments per the agreed workflow.

+# CLAUDE.md — DataQ project guide for AI assistants
+
+> Single source of truth for any Claude / AI assistant working in this repo. Read this end-to-end before touching code.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Project summary
+
+**DataQ** is the v1 evolution of SnowQ — a single-tenant data quality monitoring platform built around Great Expectations (GX Core). It runs DQ checks across **4 datasources** and integrates with **2 orchestration providers**.
+
+| Layer | Components |
+|---|---|
+| **Datasources (you can write checks against)** | Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT), ADLS Gen2, AWS S3, Unity Catalog (Databricks) |
+| **Orchestration providers (monitor + trigger only — NOT datasources)** | Azure Data Factory (ADF), Apache Airflow |
+| **Backend** | FastAPI + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL + Alembic |
+| **Frontend** | React + Vite + Ant Design + Monaco editor |
+| **Auth / secrets** | Azure AD (MSAL) + Azure Key Vault |
+| **Deploy** | Azure Container Apps + Azure Static Web App |
+| **Observability** | Azure Application Insights + structlog |
+| **AI integration** | FastMCP (8 curated tools mounted at `/mcp`) — Claude Desktop / Claude.ai / Copilot / Cursor |
+
+Timeline: **8 weeks** to v1. Scope: single tenant, suite-level access sharing, Azure-hosted.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Architecture at a glance
+
+See [docs/architecture.svg](docs/architecture.svg) for the full diagram (moved here from `context/` in PR 0).
+
+```
+Browser ──HTTPS──► React (Static Web App) ──► FastAPI (Container Apps) ──► PostgreSQL
+                                                    │  │
+AI clients ──MCP/HTTP──► FastAPI /mcp endpoint      │  └──► Celery worker ──► GX execution ──► Snowflake / ADLS / S3 / UC
+                                                    │
+                                                    ├──► Redis (task queue)
+                                                    ├──► Key Vault (secrets)
+                                                    └──► App Insights (observability)
+
+ADF ──► Azure Monitor alert rule ──► webhook ──► POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/adf
+Airflow ──► on_success/on_failure_callback ──► POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow
+FastAPI ──► MS Teams webhook (alerts)
+```
+
+---
+
+## 3. Repo layout
+
+Flat monorepo (decided in Week 1):
+
+```
+DataQ/
+├── backend/                     # FastAPI + Celery + GX (Python, conda)
+│   ├── app/
+│   │   ├── core/                # logging, errors, config (locked in PR 2)
+│   │   ├── db/                  # SQLAlchemy models, session
+│   │   ├── api/                 # FastAPI routers (versioned: /api/v1/...)
+│   │   ├── services/            # business logic per domain
+│   │   ├── orchestration/       # OrchestrationProvider abstraction (ADF, Airflow)
+│   │   ├── datasources/         # GX adapter per datasource type
+│   │   └── mcp/                 # FastMCP tools (Week 7)
+│   ├── alembic/
+│   └── tests/
+├── frontend/                    # React + Vite + Ant Design (Node, pnpm or npm)
+│   ├── src/
+│   └── tests/
+├── docs/
+│   ├── architecture.svg
+│   └── adr/                     # Architecture Decision Records
+├── scripts/
+│   └── setup.sh                 # one-command dev env bootstrap
+├── context/                     # original product/roadmap context (read-only reference)
+│   └── DataQ_platform_roadmap.md
+├── .github/
+│   ├── workflows/
+│   ├── pull_request_template.md
+│   └── ISSUE_TEMPLATE/
+├── docker-compose.yml
+├── environment.yml              # conda env definition
+├── conda-lock.yml
+├── pyproject.toml               # Black + Ruff + mypy config
+├── CONTRIBUTING.md
+├── CLAUDE.md                    # this file
+└── README.md
+```
+
+**Promotion to `apps/` + `packages/`:** only if a real shared package emerges (e.g., auto-generated OpenAPI client in Week 4–5). Default flat.
+
+---
+
+## 4. Datasources vs orchestration — critical distinction
+
+**Datasources** are stores you write DQ checks against:
+- Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT)
+- ADLS Gen2 (flat files)
+- AWS S3 (flat files)
+- Unity Catalog / Databricks
+
+**Orchestration providers** are NOT datasources. They are workflow engines whose pipelines/DAGs we observe and react to. Their *only* three responsibilities in DataQ:
+
+1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table (separate from `runs` / `results`).
+2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific event channels (webhook for both).
+3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings` (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `suite_id`, `env`). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs.
+
+Both providers implement a single `OrchestrationProvider` interface — ADF is the reference implementation, Airflow is the second. **Never hardcode ADF-only logic; always go through the abstraction.**
+
+| Provider | Event channel | Auth | Polling fallback |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| ADF | Azure Monitor alert → webhook | Shared secret header (Azure Monitor's only mode) | ADF REST API, 10 min |
+| Airflow | DAG `on_*_callback` → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns`, 10 min |
+
+Airflow callbacks require the user to add a snippet to their DAGs (we can't mutate them). Polling is the documented fallback.
+
+**Anti-pattern (do not do this):** treating ADF/Airflow as a 5th/6th datasource in the connection editor, check editor, or suite model.
+
+---
+
+## 5. Framework choice — GX-only for v1
+
+- **v1:** Great Expectations (GX Core) is the sole DQ framework across all 4 datasources. Unifies result schema, suite/check model, MCP tools, and the check editor.
+- **v1.1:** Databricks Labs **DQX** will be added for DLT / streaming use cases (GX is batch-only and runs poorly on streaming). DQX will implement the same `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` interface introduced in Week 3 — UI exposes `engine: gx | dqx` toggle on UC suites.
+- **Implication for Week 3:** keep the UC adapter thin behind `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` so v1.1 DQX swap-in doesn't ripple into the suite/check/result layer.
+
+---
+
+## 6. Working agreements (rules above feature work)
+
+Full list (30 rules across 8 categories) lives in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Highlights:
+
+### Commit & change discipline
+- **One functionality per commit** (where possible).
+- **Manually test each committed change before starting the next functionality** (required until unit tests land in Week 8).
+- **Defects → GitHub issue, never silent fixes.** Use `gh issue create`. The fixing PR must include `Fixes #N`.
+- **From Week 8 onward, every new functionality ships with tests.**
+
+### Git workflow
+- **Trunk-based** with short-lived feature branches off `main`. No long-lived `develop`.
+- Branch names: `feature/<desc>`, `fix/issue-<N>-<desc>`, `chore/<desc>`, `docs/<desc>`.
+- `main` is protected: PR + ≥1 review + passing CI + no force-push.
+- **Squash-merge only into `main`.**
+- **Conventional commits** (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`).
+
+### CI/CD quality gates (block merge)
+- Ruff (lint), Black `--check` (format), mypy (types), pytest (from W8), frontend lint/format/test.
+- `gitleaks` secret scanning (pre-commit + CI).
+- Bandit (Python SAST) + CodeQL.
+- Dependabot for npm + pip + github-actions.
+
+### Tooling (locked in Week 1, do not drift)
+- **Python:** conda env (`conda create -n dataq python=3.11`) — *not* venv, *not* poetry.
+- **Black** formatter (CI-enforced).
+- **Ruff** lint, **mypy** types, **structlog** logging, **Pydantic Settings** config (12-factor).
+- **Frontend:** Prettier + ESLint.
+
+### Observability
+- **Structured logging from Week 1.** structlog, JSON, `request_id` correlation propagated FastAPI → Celery → GX.
+- **PII redaction at logger level** (failed-check sample rows may contain sensitive data).
+- **App Insights exception tracking wired Week 1**, not Week 7.
+
+### Database
+- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** No `DROP COLUMN` + code change in same PR. Two-step deploys from W5 onward.
+- Migration PR checklist: rollback plan + "tested up + down locally."
+
+### Documentation
+- **ADRs in `docs/adr/`** — one short markdown per significant decision.
+- `scripts/setup.sh` — one command from clone to working dev env.
+
+### Security cadence
+- End-of-week quick scan from Week 2: vuln alerts, secret scan, OWASP spot check, Key Vault audit.
+- Hard security review gate before Week 7 deploy.
+
+---
+
+## 7. Required reading before coding
+
+1. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — full 30-rule working agreements + DoD + commit/branch conventions
+2. [docs/adr/](docs/adr/) — all ADRs (architecture decisions with rationale)
+3. [context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md](context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md) — the 8-week, 100-task product roadmap
+4. The current week's milestone target (see §13 below)
+
+---
+
+## 8. Local dev quickstart
+
+```bash
+git clone <repo>
+cd DataQ
+./scripts/setup.sh           # creates conda env, installs pre-commit, pulls images, runs migrations, seeds dev data
+conda activate dataq
+docker-compose up            # Postgres + Redis + FastAPI + React + Celery worker
+# Smoke test:
+curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/_probe/snowflake-suite
+# Browse Swagger: http://localhost:8000/docs
+```
+
+---
+
+## 9. Key design decisions (with ADR links)
+
+| Decision | ADR | Status |
+|---|---|---|
+| Trunk-based branching, squash-merge into `main` | [0001](docs/adr/0001-trunk-based-branching.md) | Locked W1 |
+| Conventional commits | [0002](docs/adr/0002-conventional-commits.md) | Locked W1 |
+| GX-only for v1; DQX deferred to v1.1 | [0003](docs/adr/0003-gx-only-for-v1.md) | Locked W1 |
+| Orchestration abstraction (ADF + Airflow share `OrchestrationProvider`) | [0004](docs/adr/0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) | Locked W1 |
+| Severity tier weights (warn/fail/critical → health score) | `0005` (TBD W3) | Pending stakeholder agreement before W3 starts |
+| ADF webhook auth (shared secret) + Key Vault rotation | `0006` (TBD W2) | Pending W2 |
+| Airflow callback model (HMAC-signed) + polling fallback | `0007` (TBD W2) | Pending W2 |
+| MCP mounted at `/mcp` with Azure AD auth | `0008` (TBD W7) | Pending W7 |
+| Repo layout: flat monorepo (`backend/` + `frontend/`) | `0009` (TBD W1) | Locked W1 |
+
+---
+
+## 10. Critical pointers (easy to get wrong)
+
+- **`pipeline_runs` ≠ `runs`.** Orchestrator pipeline executions live in `pipeline_runs`; DQ suite executions live in `runs`. They link via `triggered_by: '<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>'`.
+- **`trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic.** Composite key (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) → `suite_id`. Don't add an ADF-specific bindings table.
+- **PII redaction at the logger level**, not at every call site. The redactor sits in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.
+- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** Code that depends on a new column ships in a separate PR *after* the migration is deployed.
+- **Secret scanning in pre-commit AND CI.** Don't rely on one alone.
+- **Azure Monitor alert setup (Week 7) needs the deployed public API URL.** Deployment must come first; coordinate Container Apps ingress with infra/security before Week 7 to avoid a deployment-day surprise.
+- **MCP tool descriptions are LLM-facing, not REST-API-facing.** Write them for natural-language selection; test against the 4 canonical NL queries in the roadmap.
+
+---
+
+## 11. What NOT to do
+
+- ❌ Don't add ADF or Airflow as a queryable datasource in the connection editor / check editor / suite model.
+- ❌ Don't bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with provider-specific branching in service code.
+- ❌ Don't `git commit --no-verify` past hooks. If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue.
+- ❌ Don't commit `.env` files. Use `.env.example` as the template.
+- ❌ Don't drop columns in the same PR as the code change that stops using them. Two-step it.
+- ❌ Don't fix bugs silently. Raise a GitHub issue, then PR with `Fixes #N`.
+- ❌ Don't batch unrelated changes into one commit. One functionality per commit.
+- ❌ Don't track GX Core at "latest." Pin the version in `environment.yml` — GX v1 API has drifted across point releases.
+- ❌ Don't use venv or poetry for backend dev. Conda only.
+- ❌ Don't write the MCP layer before Week 7. The service layer must stabilise first.
+
+---
+
+## 12. Where things live
+
+| Artifact | Location |
+|---|---|
+| Product roadmap (100 tasks, 8 weeks) | [context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md](context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md) |
+| System architecture diagram | [docs/architecture.svg](docs/architecture.svg) |

+

+

Adds a 283-line `CLAUDE.md` as the canonical onboarding doc for AI assistants entering this repo. 13 sections + appendix covering project summary, architecture, repo layout, datasource-vs-orchestration distinction, GX-only-for-v1, working agreements, decisions, anti-patterns, and current milestone. Single new file, no behavioural code.

## Findings

### 🔴 Misalignment with applied branch protection
§6 *Git workflow* says:
> `main` is protected: PR + **≥1 review** + passing CI + no force-push.

But the ruleset we actually applied (PR-prep step) has `required_approving_review_count: 0` for the solo-dev phase. This contradicts CLAUDE.md and will confuse anyone reading the doc against the live config. Fix: say "PR + (≥1 review when a collaborator joins) + passing CI + no force-push" or note the current temporary 0-reviews setting.

### 🟡 ADR 0009 status conflict with PR #4
§9 *Key design decisions* lists:
> Repo layout: flat monorepo (`backend/` + `frontend/`) | `0009` (TBD W1) | **Locked W1**

But the ADR index in PR #4 lists 0009 as "Pending" — no ADR file exists yet. Either "Pending" or write 0009 alongside; don't mark something Locked without an ADR file behind it.

### 🟡 Plan file commit promise not fulfilled
§12 says:
> Execution plan ... will be committed to `docs/execution-plan.md` in PR 0

None of the 6 split PR-0 branches commit this. Either add a 7th branch `docs/add-execution-plan` or change the wording to "will be committed in a follow-up." Right now this is a promise the diff doesn't keep.

### 🟡 `context/` listing in §3 is incomplete
Repo-layout tree shows `context/` with only `DataQ_platform_roadmap.md`. PR #6 also commits `DataQ_Management_Presentation.pptx`. Add it.

### 🟡 `.github/` listing in §3 missing CODEOWNERS
Tree shows `.github/workflows/`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. PR #3 also adds `CODEOWNERS`. Add it.

### 🟢 Forward-reference link risk — merge-order matters
CLAUDE.md links to:
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (doesn't exist; PR 1 of the plan, not yet open)
- `docs/architecture.svg` (PR #5)
- `docs/adr/0001...0004` (PR #4)
- `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` (PR #6)

If PR #2 merges before #4, #5, #6, every link on GitHub's rendered view is a 404 until the others land. Recommend merge order: **#4 → #5 → #6 → #3 → #1 → #2** (CLAUDE.md last). Or mark this PR as blocked-by the others in the GitHub UI.

### 🟢 Frontend package manager left undecided
§3 says `(Node, pnpm or npm)`. The working agreements lock Python tooling specifically — Node should be locked too in Week 1 per agreement #17 ("don't drift"). Pick one (recommend pnpm for monorepo-friendliness) and update.

### 🟢 "PR 0" naming vs reality on GitHub
§13 references "PR 0 — Repo governance" as a singular thing. On GitHub it materialised as 6 PRs (#1–#6). Future readers won't know what "PR 0" means. Clarify: "the PR 0 governance bundle, currently split into GitHub PRs #1–#6."

### 🟢 Quickstart commands aren't runnable yet
§8 calls `./scripts/setup.sh`, `conda activate dataq`, `docker-compose up`, `curl /api/v1/_probe/snowflake-suite` — none exist until Week 1 PRs land. Acceptable for a forward-looking doc, but worth a one-line caveat: "Quickstart commands assume Week 1 scaffolding is in place."

## Correctness, conventions, security
- ✅ Datasource-vs-orchestration distinction (§4) matches ADR 0004.
- ✅ GX-only-for-v1 (§5) matches ADR 0003.
- ✅ Working-agreement highlights (§6) match `feedback_working_agreements.md` memory.
- ✅ Markdown is well-formed; tables align; emoji use is minimal and consistent.
- ⚪ Docs-only; no code-correctness, no security surface, no tests required.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** The branch-protection misstatement (§6) is the only material correctness issue — anyone reading CLAUDE.md will think `main` is stricter than it is. The status/listing fixes (§3, §9, §12) are accuracy housekeeping; nice to address before merge but not blocking. The merge-order note is process advice, not a code fix.

# Code review — PR #3 `chore: add CODEOWNERS, PR template, and issue templates`

**Overview**
Four metadata files: `CODEOWNERS`, `pull_request_template.md`, `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.md`, `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md`. Operationalises working agreements #1, #3, #5, #11, #25. 180 lines added, no behavioural code.

## Findings

### 🔴 Issue title prefixes use PR-side conventional types
Both `bug.md` and `feature.md` set:
```yaml
title: "fix: <short description>"
title: "feat: <short description>"
```
But conventional commits (`fix:`, `feat:`, …) are **PR/commit-title** prefixes — they describe a change. Issues describe a *problem* or *request*. Pre-filling issues with `fix:` conflates the two. The implementing PR uses `fix: <desc>` and references `Fixes #N`; the issue should have a plain descriptive title (or `[bug]` / `[feature]` if a prefix is wanted).

Suggested:
```yaml
# bug.md
title: "<short description of the defect>"
# feature.md
title: "<short description of the request>"
```

### 🟡 "Type of change" allows multi-select but conventional commits are singular
PR template says:
> ## Type of change
> Tick all that apply.

But squash-merge produces one commit with exactly one type prefix. Multi-tick implies multiple types — contradicts ADR 0002. Should be: "Tick **one** that matches your conventional commit prefix."

### 🟡 `Fixes #` pre-fill leaves a literal half-token
```
Fixes #
```
If the author doesn't fill or delete, GitHub doesn't parse it (no number). Recommend leaving the field blank with a comment hint, or `Fixes #N` (literal `N`) so reviewers spot an unfilled placeholder.

### 🟡 Security-severity defects shouldn't be public issues
`bug.md` severity options include:
```
- [ ] critical — production down / data loss / security
```
A public issue for an exploitable vulnerability is the wrong channel — it discloses before the fix is ready. Recommend:
1. Split "security" out of "critical."
2. Add a separate `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/security.md` that *redirects* to GitHub Security Advisories (private vulnerability reporting): `https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new`.
3. Or use `.github/SECURITY.md` with a `Reporting a Vulnerability` section pointing to the same.

### 🟢 CODEOWNERS is functionally a no-op for solo dev
Sole owner = sole admin = sole likely PR author. GitHub does not auto-request review from the PR author, so none of these entries trigger today. PR body acknowledges this.

Also: every path has identical owner, so the per-area splits are redundant — the single `* @TheurgicDuke771` line covers all of them. Two options:
- Simplify to just `*` until a second contributor joins.
- Keep the per-area scaffolding as documentation of where ownership *will* split (current choice; reasonable for a forward-looking governance file).

If keeping the scaffolding, consider adding:
- `/Makefile` (if/when it exists)
- `/.dockerignore`
- `/.env.example`

### 🟢 Schema-migration question rendered as checkboxes
```
- [ ] No schema change
- [ ] Yes — Alembic migration included, ...
```
These are mutually exclusive but rendered as multi-select. GitHub markdown doesn't support real radio buttons in templates, but the wording should make exclusivity explicit: "Tick exactly one."

### 🟢 Missing screenshots/video section in PR template
From Week 4 (frontend work) onward, screenshots/recordings materially help reviewers. Add a `## UI evidence (frontend changes only)` section now so the habit is established.

### 🟢 Minor — checklist items reference tools not yet installed
`Black + Ruff + mypy pass locally` and `Prettier + ESLint pass locally` — these aren't configured until Week 1 PR 1. Reviewers/authors can't tick them yet. Acceptable forward reference; consider adding "(from Week 1 onward)" suffix like the testing line.

## Correctness, conventions, security
- ✅ CODEOWNERS syntax correct (leading `/` for repo-root, trailing `/` for directories).
- ✅ Frontmatter on issue templates valid.
- ✅ All references to working agreements / ADRs match the agreed model.
- ✅ Datasource/orchestration distinction reinforced in feature template (good — prevents the "ADF as datasource" anti-pattern from creeping into proposals).
- ⚪ Docs/templates only; no runtime code, no test coverage required.
- ⚠️ Security: the public-issue-for-vuln gap (above) is the only security-adjacent finding.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** The issue-title prefix mistake (🔴) is small but worth fixing now so the first real bug report doesn't inherit the bad pattern. The security-disclosure path (🟡) should be in place before any public exposure (Week 7) — fine to defer if tracked. Everything else is polish.

---

Posting findings.

+# ADR 0001 — Trunk-based branching with squash-merge into `main`
+
+- **Status:** Accepted
+- **Date:** 2026-05-24
+- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
+
+## Context
+
+DataQ v1 has an 8-week timeline and a small team (starting solo, expected to grow). We need a branching model that supports frequent integration, keeps `main` history readable, and aligns with the working-agreement of one functionality per commit.
+
+## Decision
+
+Adopt **trunk-based development** with short-lived feature branches off `main`, and **squash-merge** as the only allowed merge method into `main`.
+
+- All work happens on a branch named `feature/<desc>`, `fix/issue-<N>-<desc>`, `chore/<desc>`, or `docs/<desc>`.
+- Branches are short-lived (ideally hours to a couple of days), opened as PRs against `main`.
+- PRs are squash-merged — the PR title becomes the single commit on `main` (so PR titles MUST follow conventional commits — see ADR 0002).
+- No long-lived `develop` branch.
+- `main` is protected via a GitHub ruleset (deletion blocked, force-push blocked, linear history required, PR required, squash-only merge, dismiss stale reviews on new push). Admin (sole maintainer) can bypass in emergencies.
+- Auto-delete head branches on merge.
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive**
+- `main` history reads as one commit per delivered functionality — matches working-agreement #1.
+- Short-lived branches force small, reviewable changes.
+- No long-lived branches to keep in sync.
+- Linear history makes `git bisect` reliable.
+
+**Negative**
+- Loses individual WIP commits inside a PR. Mitigated: those commits remain visible in the PR view on GitHub.
+- Solo dev currently has `required_approving_review_count: 0` — must bump to 1 when a second contributor joins (tracked as a future change).
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- **GitFlow** — rejected. The `develop` / `release` / `hotfix` overhead is unjustified for an 8-week single-tenant v1; release cadence is continuous, not versioned.
+- **Merge commits preserving branch history** — rejected. Squash gives one commit per functionality on `main`; preserved branch history would dilute that signal and clutter `git log`.
+- **Rebase-and-merge** — rejected. Preserves all WIP commits on `main`, breaking the one-functionality-per-commit principle.
diff --git a/docs/adr/0002-conventional-commits.md b/docs/adr/0002-conventional-commits.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..09a03c2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/adr/0002-conventional-commits.md
@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+# ADR 0002 — Conventional commits for PR titles and commit messages
+
+- **Status:** Accepted
+- **Date:** 2026-05-24
+- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
+
+## Context
+
+With squash-merge as the only allowed merge method (ADR 0001), each PR becomes exactly one commit on `main` whose message is the PR title. The PR title format therefore drives the readability of `git log` and enables future automation (changelog generation, release notes).
+
+## Decision
+
+Use **Conventional Commits** for all PR titles and individual commits.
+
+Allowed type prefixes:
+
+| Type | Use for |
+|---|---|
+| `feat:` | New user-facing functionality |
+| `fix:` | Bug fix (PR body MUST include `Fixes #N` per working-agreement #3) |
+| `chore:` | Tooling, dependencies, repo housekeeping |
+| `docs:` | Documentation-only change (CLAUDE.md, ADRs, README, code comments) |
+| `test:` | Test-only change |
+| `refactor:` | Internal change with no behaviour change |
+
+Format: `<type>(<optional-scope>): <imperative summary>`
+
+Examples:
+- `feat(orchestration): add Airflow callback webhook handler`
+- `fix(adf): debounce duplicate trigger events within 30s window`
+- `chore: pin GX Core to 1.x`
+- `docs: add ADR 0005 for severity tier weights`
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive**
+- `git log --oneline` reads as a categorised changelog.
+- Enables future tooling: auto-changelog, release-please, semantic versioning.
+- PR titles are self-documenting.
+
+**Negative**
+- One more thing for new contributors to learn. Mitigated: the PR template includes a "Type of change" checklist that nudges the right prefix.
+
+## Enforcement
+
+- PR template includes the convention.
+- Future enhancement (post-W1): a GitHub Action that fails CI if the PR title does not match the convention.

+# ADR 0003 — GX-only for v1; DQX deferred to v1.1 for DLT/streaming
+
+- **Status:** Accepted
+- **Date:** 2026-05-24
+- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
+
+## Context
+
+DataQ v1 must run data quality checks across four datasource types: Snowflake, ADLS Gen2, AWS S3, and Unity Catalog (Databricks). Two viable DQ frameworks were considered:
+
+- **Great Expectations (GX Core v1)** — mature, multi-backend, supports Snowflake / Pandas (for flat files) / Spark via DataFrame datasources. Unified suite/expectation/result model. Batch-only.
+- **Databricks Labs DQX** — newer, native to Databricks runtime. First-class streaming and Delta Live Tables (DLT) support. Lower runtime overhead on Spark. Unity Catalog-aware. Not multi-backend.
+
+The roadmap defers DLT / streaming functionality to v1.1.
+
+## Decision
+
+**Use Great Expectations (GX Core v1) as the sole DQ framework for v1, across all four datasource types. Defer DQX to v1.1 for the streaming / DLT use case.**
+
+To enable the v1.1 swap cleanly:
+
+- Wrap the Unity Catalog GX execution behind a `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` interface in Week 3.
+- DQX in v1.1 will implement the same interface as a `DqxCheckRunner` alongside the existing GX runner.
+- A result-shape adapter will normalise DQX output into DataQ's existing `check_results` schema.
+- UI exposes `engine: gx | dqx` toggle on UC suites in v1.1.
+- Batch UC tables via SQL Warehouse remain on GX even after v1.1 (no migration of working code).
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive**
+- One framework → one result schema, one suite model, one check-editor UI, one MCP tool contract across all four datasources.
+- The 8-week timeline is feasible with a single framework; two would not be.
+- The interface-first approach in Week 3 makes the v1.1 DQX add additive, not migrative.
+
+**Negative**
+- GX has no streaming support — streaming/DLT DQ is impossible in v1 (acceptable; deferred to v1.1).
+- GX-on-Spark for Unity Catalog is higher-overhead than DQX on the same workload. Acceptable for v1 batch volumes.
+- GX Core v1 API has drifted across point releases — must pin the version in `environment.yml` and avoid tracking latest.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- **GX for Snowflake / flat files, DQX for Unity Catalog from v1** — rejected. Mixing frameworks in v1 doubles the result-shape handling and forces a check-editor variant per framework; estimated 1 extra week of work for ~0 user-visible benefit in v1 (no streaming requirement yet).
+- **DQX-only** — rejected. DQX is Databricks-native and does not cover Snowflake / S3 / ADLS as first-class targets.
+- **Build a custom DQ framework** — rejected outright. Out of scope; both GX and DQX are mature.
+
+## Related
+
+- v1.1 streaming/DLT entry in `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` "Deferred to v1.1".
+- `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` interface (Week 3 deliverable).

@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+# ADR 0004 — Unified `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction for ADF and Apache Airflow
+
+- **Status:** Accepted
+- **Date:** 2026-05-24
+- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
+
+## Context
+
+DataQ integrates with Azure Data Factory (ADF) and Apache Airflow. The original product framing listed ADF as a "5th datasource type," which conflates orchestration with data storage:
+
+- **Datasources** (Snowflake, ADLS Gen2, S3, Unity Catalog) are stores against which DQ checks are written.
+- **Orchestrators** (ADF, Airflow) are workflow engines whose pipeline/DAG runs we observe and react to. We do not write DQ checks against the orchestrator itself.
+
+Treating orchestrators as datasources pollutes the suite/check editor, mixes unrelated concerns in the data model, and makes the upcoming Airflow integration look like a one-off rather than a sibling of ADF.
+
+## Decision
+
+**Treat ADF and Apache Airflow as orchestration integrations behind a single `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction. They are NOT datasources and never appear in the connection editor / check editor / suite model as a queryable target.**
+
+### Responsibilities (identical across both providers)
+
+1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table with a `provider` column (`adf` | `airflow`) and `provider_run_id`.
+2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific webhook channels (see table below).
+3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings` (composite key: `provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs (no point running checks on data that wasn't loaded).
+
+### Interface
+
+```
+class OrchestrationProvider:
+    def parse_event(self, payload: bytes, headers: dict) -> RunUpdate: ...
+    def fetch_run_detail(self, provider_run_id: str) -> RunDetail: ...
+    def list_recent_runs(self, since: datetime) -> list[RunUpdate]: ...
+```
+
+Both `AdfProvider` and `AirflowProvider` implement this interface. Service code routes by `provider` enum, never by provider-specific branching.
+
+### Event channels per provider
+
+| Provider | Failure / success channel | Auth | Polling fallback |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| ADF | Azure Monitor alert rule → webhook `POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/adf` | Shared-secret header (Azure Monitor's only auth mode) | ADF REST API every 10 min |
+| Airflow | DAG `on_success_callback` / `on_failure_callback` → webhook `POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow` | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns` every 10 min |
+
+### UI surface
+
+Orchestrators appear ONLY in:
+- The orchestration status panel on the results dashboard.
+- The trigger-binding configuration UI.
+
+They do NOT appear in the connection editor's "pick a datasource" list or the check editor's table picker.
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive**
+- Adding a third orchestration provider in the future (Prefect, Dagster, etc.) is a new `OrchestrationProvider` implementation — no data-model or UI churn.
+- `pipeline_runs` stays clean as a single events stream regardless of provider.
+- `trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic from day one.
+- Forces correct mental model — orchestrator is not a datasource.
+
+**Negative**
+- Slightly more abstraction upfront in Week 2 vs hardcoding ADF, then refactoring when Airflow is added. Accepted because Airflow is in-scope for v1, not a hypothetical future.
+- Airflow callback adoption is voluntary on the user side (we cannot mutate their DAGs). Mitigated by documenting the polling fallback and providing a copy-paste `dataq_airflow_callback` snippet.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- **Treat ADF as a 5th datasource (original framing)** — rejected. Conflates orchestration with storage; pollutes the check editor and the data model.
+- **Hardcode ADF in v1, abstract later when Airflow is added** — rejected. Refactoring after `pipeline_runs` has data is more expensive than designing the abstraction once upfront.
+
+## Related
+
+- `pipeline_runs` and `trigger_bindings` schema lands in Week 1/2.
+- `OrchestrationProvider` interface lands in Week 2 alongside both implementations.
+- Future: ADR 0006 (ADF webhook auth) and ADR 0007 (Airflow callback model) will detail the provider-specific event channels.
diff --git a/docs/adr/README.md b/docs/adr/README.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0e51847
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/adr/README.md
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+# Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
+
+Each ADR captures a single significant architecture decision: the context, the decision, the consequences, and the alternatives considered. New ADRs are append-only — supersede an old decision by adding a new ADR and marking the old one's status as `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.
+
+## Format
+
+- File name: `NNNN-short-kebab-slug.md` (zero-padded 4-digit sequence)
+- Frontmatter fields: Status, Date, Deciders
+- Sections: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, Related (optional)
+- Keep each ADR short — 1–2 pages. If it grows past that, the decision is probably two decisions.
+
+## Index
+
+| # | Title | Status |
+|---|---|---|
+| [0001](0001-trunk-based-branching.md) | Trunk-based branching with squash-merge into `main` | Accepted |
+| [0002](0002-conventional-commits.md) | Conventional commits for PR titles and commit messages | Accepted |
+| [0003](0003-gx-only-for-v1.md) | GX-only for v1; DQX deferred to v1.1 for DLT/streaming | Accepted |
+| [0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) | Unified `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction for ADF and Airflow | Accepted |
+
+## Pending (to be written in their respective weeks)
+
+| # | Topic | Target week |
+|---|---|---|
+| 0005 | Severity tier weights (warn / fail / critical → health score) | Week 3, Day 1 |
+| 0006 | ADF webhook authentication (shared secret + Key Vault rotation) | Week 2 |
+| 0007 | Airflow callback model (HMAC signing + polling fallback) | Week 2 |
+| 0008 | MCP mounted at `/mcp` with Azure AD auth | Week 7 |
+| 0009 | Repo layout — flat monorepo (`backend/` + `frontend/`) | Week 1 |
```

# Code review — PR #4 `docs: add initial ADRs 0001-0004 + ADR index`

**Overview**
Five new files in `docs/adr/`: four foundational ADRs (branching, conventional commits, GX-only-for-v1, orchestration abstraction) plus the README index with pending-ADR list. 236 lines, docs-only.

## Findings

### 🔴 `trigger_bindings` composite key ambiguity
ADR 0004 states:
> `trigger_bindings` (composite key: `provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`)

But the execution plan (and Week 2 design) calls for **"one pipeline/DAG can map to multiple suites."** If `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env)` is a unique key, you can store at most one suite mapping per (provider, pipeline, env) — 1:N is impossible.

Fix one of:
- Composite **unique** key must include `suite_id`: `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env, suite_id)`.
- Or drop "key" language and call it a *lookup index* (non-unique), with the actual PK being a surrogate `id`.

This is the kind of schema ambiguity that gets baked in at Week 2 migration time and is painful to fix later (working-agreement #24).

### 🟡 Branch-name list in ADR 0001 doesn't match commit-type list in ADR 0002
ADR 0001 lists branch prefixes: `feature/`, `fix/`, `chore/`, `docs/`.
ADR 0002 allows commit types: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `test`, `refactor`.

Mismatch: `refactor/` and `test/` aren't named as valid branch prefixes. Either:
- Add them to ADR 0001's list, or
- Say explicitly: "branch prefix matches the conventional-commit type of the eventual PR title."

### 🟡 0009 status will diverge between this PR and PR #2
ADR index here lists 0009 as **Pending W1**. CLAUDE.md §9 (PR #2) marks 0009 as **Locked W1**. After both merge, the same decision will show two different statuses. Authoritative source is `docs/adr/README.md` — but CLAUDE.md will need a fixup.

(Already flagged on PR #2; calling it out here too for traceability.)

### 🟢 ADR 0002 restricts conventional commits but doesn't say so
Conventional Commits spec also defines `build:`, `ci:`, `perf:`, `style:`, `revert:`. ADR 0002's table omits them silently. Fine to restrict, but state the intent: "We use a subset of Conventional Commits; the omitted types (`build`, `ci`, `perf`, `style`, `revert`) are deliberately excluded to keep `git log` categorisation simple."

### 🟢 ADR 0002 example mildly contradicts ADR 0003
Example: `chore: pin GX Core to 1.x` (range).
ADR 0003 says: "must pin the version" (exact).

Update example to `chore: pin GX Core to 1.4.2` (or whatever the exact version will be) to model the right behaviour.

### 🟢 ADR 0004 interface uses untyped `dict`
```python
def parse_event(self, payload: bytes, headers: dict) -> RunUpdate: ...
```
`headers: dict` sets a poor type-hint example for readers who copy this into code. Use `Mapping[str, str]` (or `dict[str, str]`) to model the immutable-from-callee contract. mypy will flag the loose form once configured.

### 🟢 ADR 0004 doesn't address rate-limit / retry semantics for polling
`list_recent_runs(since)` — what happens when ADF/Airflow REST APIs are throttled or down? Implementation detail, not interface contract — fine to omit, but a one-line "retry/backoff is implementation detail; interface guarantees no double-emit via `last_updated_at` dedupe" would close the question.

### 🟢 ADR template missing "Consulted" / "Stakeholders" field
ADR 0005 (severity tier weights) per the plan requires product-owner sign-off before Week 3 starts. Today the template only has "Deciders." Add `Consulted:` so decisions involving non-engineering stakeholders capture who signed off and when.

### 🟢 ADR template missing explicit "Supersedes / Superseded by" placeholder
README describes the supersession process but the template doesn't reserve a structural slot. Add to template:
```
- **Status:** Accepted
- **Supersedes:** (optional, e.g. ADR-0007)
- **Superseded by:** (optional, e.g. ADR-0042)
```

## Correctness, conventions, security
- ✅ Dates consistent (2026-05-24 across all four).
- ✅ Status field present and accurate.
- ✅ Datasource-vs-orchestration distinction reinforced in ADR 0004.
- ✅ GX pinning rationale documented in ADR 0003 (preempts the "track latest" mistake).
- ✅ Alternatives sections include real rejected options, not strawmen.
- ⚪ Docs-only; no runtime behaviour, no test coverage, no security surface.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** The `trigger_bindings` key ambiguity (🔴) is the only finding that touches future schema correctness — worth resolving as a 1-line ADR clarification before merge so Week 2 doesn't inherit the wrong shape. Everything else is documentation polish that can land in a follow-up `docs:` PR.

---

Posting findings.

# Code review — PR #5 `chore: move architecture diagram to docs/`

**Overview**
Single file: `docs/architecture.svg` (140 lines). Inline SVG of the DataQ system architecture — frontend → backend → datasources, plus Azure integrations and AI clients via MCP. Sole purpose is relocating an artefact from `context/` to `docs/`.

## Findings

### 🟡 Diagram doesn't include Apache Airflow
The architecture in the SVG (and its `<desc>`) lists only **ADF** under "Azure integrations." Airflow was added as a second orchestration provider during planning (ADR 0004), but the diagram pre-dates that decision. Anyone using this diagram as a reference will think only ADF is supported.

Options:
- Update the diagram: add an Airflow box alongside ADF (same orange "Integrations" color per legend), or rename the existing one to "Orchestration (ADF · Airflow)."
- Or add a TODO note in the PR description and track as a follow-up issue per working-agreement #3.

### 🟡 The PR title says "move" but git sees an addition, not a rename
Because `context/DataQ_system_architecture.svg` was never tracked, git can't detect a rename. The diff shows a new file with no deletion. `git log --follow docs/architecture.svg` won't trace history back to `context/`. Two options:
- Accept this (likely correct — the original was a draft).
- Or rename the PR to `chore: add architecture diagram to docs/` (more accurate to what git records). Won't change the file on disk, just the commit-title accuracy.

### 🟢 `Anthropic Sans` font won't be available on most viewers
Lines like:
```
font-family:&quot;Anthropic Sans&quot;, -apple-system, &quot;system-ui&quot;, ...
```
`Anthropic Sans` isn't a system font for most readers — it'll silently fall back to `-apple-system` or `system-ui`. Harmless but slightly confusing (artefact of where the SVG was authored). Could strip from the CSS for cleanliness; not urgent.

### 🟢 SVG looks accessible
- `role="img"` ✓
- `<title>DataQ system architecture diagram</title>` ✓
- `<desc>` with a substantive description ✓

Good as-is.

### 🟢 SVG is safe to render in GitHub
- No `<script>` tags.
- No `onclick` / `onload` / `javascript:` URLs.
- No external `href` / `xlink:href` references.
- All resources inline.

GitHub will render this in the file view and via raw URLs.

### 🟢 Legend correctly groups ADF as "Integrations," not "Datasources"
Diagram visually reinforces ADR 0004's orchestration-vs-datasource distinction — Snowflake/ADLS-S3/UC are green (Datasources), ADF is orange (Integrations). This is good and worth preserving when adding Airflow.

### 🟢 Consider embedding the diagram in CLAUDE.md
GitHub's markdown renderer supports inline SVG via `<img src="docs/architecture.svg" alt="...">`. Linking (current approach in CLAUDE.md §2) requires a click; embedding shows it at-a-glance. Minor preference; either works.

### 🟢 No CI to validate SVG
Once the CI workflow lands (Week 1 PR 1), an SVG-lint step (`svglint`, `xmllint --noout`) would catch malformed edits in future. Premature now; mention as a future enhancement.

## Correctness, conventions, security
- ✅ Path/destination matches CLAUDE.md §2 forward-reference.
- ✅ No license issue (LICENSE at repo root covers).
- ✅ No secrets, no external network references.
- ⚪ No code, no tests, no runtime behaviour.
- ⚠️ Diagram content drift from ADR 0004 (missing Airflow) is the only material accuracy gap.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** The missing-Airflow issue (🟡) is the only finding that affects correctness of the doc as a reference. Either update the diagram in a fixup commit before merging, or merge as-is and open a follow-up issue to add Airflow before any external contributor sees the diagram. Everything else is polish.

---

Posting findings.

# Code review — PR #6 `chore: commit product context (roadmap + management presentation)`

**Overview**
Two files: `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` (345 lines of markdown — the 8-week, 100-task v1 product roadmap) and `context/DataQ_Management_Presentation.pptx` (566 KB binary). Both were previously untracked. PR exists to unblock forward-references in CLAUDE.md and ADR 0004 from 404-ing after merge.

## Findings

### 🔴 SECURITY — `.pptx` becomes world-readable in a public repo
Earlier in this session we made the repo public to enable branch protection on a free GitHub plan. Committing `DataQ_Management_Presentation.pptx` to that public repo means:

- Anyone (any GitHub user, any web crawler, anyone with the URL) can download the file from `https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/raw/main/context/DataQ_Management_Presentation.pptx`.
- Title implies internal / strategic content. Confirm: does the deck contain anything you wouldn't put in a tweet — pricing, customer names, internal financials, hiring plans, technical IP, competitive analysis?

Even if the answer is "no" today, committing it locks that content into public git history forever — re-privating the repo later, or `git rm`-ing the file later, does NOT remove it from the history; would require a destructive rewrite (`git filter-repo`) and a force-push, both of which are explicitly blocked by the new ruleset.

**Strong recommendation:** Don't commit the `.pptx`. Reference it by external link (SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion) from `context/README.md`. If you genuinely want it in version control, make the repo private again (paying for GitHub Pro to keep branch protection), or move the deck to a separate private repo and link.

If you've already audited the deck and confirmed it's safe to publish, mention that in the PR description so it's documented.

### 🔴 Roadmap contradicts ADR 0004
The roadmap's summary table:
> | **Datasource types** | Snowflake · Azure Data Lake (ADLS Gen2) · S3 · Unity Catalog (Databricks) · **ADF** |

But ADR 0004 explicitly states ADF is **not** a datasource — it's an orchestration provider. Without a top-of-file note clarifying that the roadmap was the *input* and the ADRs are now authoritative, future readers will hit two contradictory statements and not know which to trust.

Fix: add a preamble to the top of `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md`:
```
> **Note:** This is the original product roadmap that informed the v1 plan.
> Some categorisations and scope here have been refined by subsequent ADRs:
> - ADF (and Airflow) are orchestration providers, not datasources — see [ADR 0004](../docs/adr/0004-orchestration-abstraction.md).
> - DQX for Databricks DLT/streaming is deferred to v1.1 — see [ADR 0003](../docs/adr/0003-gx-only-for-v1.md).
> - Apache Airflow was added as a second orchestration provider after this roadmap was written.
> Where this document and the ADRs disagree, the ADRs win.
```

### 🟡 Roadmap mentions internal Azure resource names
Week 7 references concrete factory names: `lll-adf-nonprod`, `lll-adf-prod`. In a public repo, these expose internal naming conventions (and potentially the customer/org prefix `lll`). Mild info leak — not exploitable on its own, but worth either redacting or confirming you're OK publishing them.

### 🟡 PPTX as a tracked binary bloats git history
Even at 566 KB the file is small, but every future update writes a full copy to git history. After 5 deck revisions you're carrying ~3 MB just for this file forever (`git clone` downloads the full history by default). Alternatives:
- External storage + link (best).
- Git LFS — overkill for one file but the right answer if you'll commit other large binaries.

### 🟡 No `.gitattributes` marking `*.pptx binary`
Git will try to text-diff `.pptx` (a zip-archive of XML) and produce garbage. Add `.gitattributes`:
```
*.pptx binary
*.png binary
*.jpg binary
*.pdf binary
```
Either in this PR or a small follow-up.

### 🟢 No `context/README.md` explaining the folder's purpose
PR description says *"context/ is now reserved for read-only product reference material."* That intent only lives in the PR; future readers see an unexplained folder. Add `context/README.md`:
```
# context/

Read-only product reference material that informed the v1 plan but
is not part of the codebase. Files here are historical inputs —
where they conflict with current decisions, the ADRs in docs/adr/ win.
```

### 🟢 Roadmap is also missing Airflow & DQX entirely
Beyond the ADF-as-datasource issue, the roadmap doesn't mention:
- Apache Airflow (orchestration provider added post-roadmap)
- DQX (Week 3 framework discussion / v1.1 plan)

These are downstream evolutions documented in ADRs. The preamble note (above) covers it — no need to retrofit the roadmap itself.

## Correctness, conventions, security
- ✅ Path placement (`context/`) matches the intent stated in CLAUDE.md §12 and ADR-derived layout.
- ✅ Roadmap is well-structured markdown; renders cleanly on GitHub.
- ⚠️ Public-repo exposure (above) is the dominant concern.
- ⚪ No code, no tests, no runtime behaviour.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve, with one hard blocker.** The `.pptx` exposure (🔴 first finding) needs an explicit decision before merge — confirm the content is safe to publish, or replace with an external link. The roadmap-vs-ADR contradiction (🔴 second finding) is fixable in a fixup commit (~10 lines of preamble) and should land in this PR rather than a follow-up, since the contradiction is created the moment this PR merges. The other findings are polish and follow-up-PR-worthy.

---

Posting findings.

**Recommendation: hybrid — fix the irreversible/load-bearing in-PR, merge the rest, file issues for polish.** Here's why and the specific split:

## Must fix before merge (4 items)

These are either irreversible after merge, or actively wrong in a way that costs real time downstream:

1. **PR #6 — `.pptx` decision (HARD BLOCKER, IRREVERSIBLE).** Once it's in public git history, it cannot be cleanly removed (rewrite + force-push is blocked by the ruleset, and even allowed wouldn't help anyone who already cloned). Either audit-and-confirm-safe or drop and link externally.
2. **PR #6 — roadmap preamble pointing to overriding ADRs (~10 lines).** The contradiction with ADR 0004 ("ADF is a datasource") goes live the moment this PR merges. Cheap to fix in-PR, painful to leave on main even briefly.
3. **PR #4 — `trigger_bindings` key clarification (1 line of ADR text).** Schema ambiguity baked in at the ADR level becomes wrong code at Week 2 migration time. Trivial to fix now.
4. **PR #1 — `.vscode/` negation fix.** The current pattern silently lies — anyone who adds `.vscode/extensions.json` expecting it to be tracked will be surprised. Small fix, large clarity gain.

## Safe to merge as-is, file follow-up issues

These all have safe paths to fix later, are non-load-bearing for Week 1 work, and follow working-agreement #3 (`gh issue create` + `Fixes #N` in the follow-up PR):

- PR #2 branch-protection misstatement, ADR-0009 status drift, "PR 0" naming, frontend package-manager undecided, quickstart caveat
- PR #3 issue title prefixes (`fix:`/`feat:` → descriptive), security disclosure path, "Type of change" single-select wording, schema-migration exclusivity, screenshots section

- PR #5 missing Airflow in diagram (file as issue; must close before Week 2 Airflow work starts)
- PR #6 internal Azure resource names (audit + maybe redact), `.gitattributes`, `context/README.md`

## Merge order

Once the in-PR fixups land:
**#4 → #5 → #6 → #3 → #1 → #2**

This order means CLAUDE.md (#2) — with the most forward-references — merges last, when all its link targets exist. No broken-link window on `main`.

## Why this and not the alternatives

- **"Fix everything first"** is over-cautious: burns a day on polish before any foundation lands, blocks Week 1 work. Polish doesn't need to gate progress.
- **"Merge everything as-is"** is under-cautious: the `.pptx` becomes irreversible, the trigger_bindings ambiguity wastes Week 2 time, the roadmap-vs-ADR contradiction sits on main for whoever clones next. Some debts are too cheap to defer.

## Claude Code Automation Recommendations

I've analyzed the codebase end-to-end (CLAUDE.md, ADRs, working agreements, planned stack). DataQ is **pre-Week-1** — no application code yet, but the planned stack is clear and the working-agreement rules are unusually strict, which makes a few specific automations high-value.

### Codebase Profile
- **Type**: Greenfield Python 3.11 + TypeScript monorepo (no code yet, governance landed)
- **Backend (planned)**: FastAPI + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL + Alembic + Great Expectations + FastMCP
- **Frontend (planned)**: React + Vite + Ant Design + Monaco
- **Infra**: Azure Container Apps + Static Web App + Key Vault + Azure Monitor + App Insights + Azure AD (MSAL)
- **Tooling**: conda + Black + Ruff + mypy + pytest + Prettier + ESLint + gitleaks + Bandit + CodeQL
- **Process**: Trunk-based, conventional commits, squash-only, /review-before-merge, public repo with bypass-by-admin ruleset
- **Existing Claude config**: only `CLAUDE.md` — no `.claude/` directory, no hooks, no skills, no agents

---

### 🔌 MCP Servers

#### context7 (top pick)
**Why**: ADR 0003 explicitly calls out that **"GX Core v1 API has drifted across point releases"** and mandates pinning. Same risk applies to FastAPI, FastMCP, MSAL, Pydantic Settings, Celery, structlog, and Alembic — all listed as locked dependencies. context7 gives version-pinned, live API docs at code-generation time, dramatically reducing hallucinated APIs that were valid in a different version.
**Install**: `claude mcp add context7`

#### Azure MCP
**Why**: DataQ is Azure-heavy (Container Apps, Static Web App, Key Vault, App Insights, Azure Monitor alert rules, Azure AD app registration). Week 7's exit gate requires manually configuring Azure Monitor → webhook routing in two environments — a brittle, click-heavy flow that benefits from scripted MCP-driven setup and verification. Also useful for Week 1 Key Vault wiring.
**Install**: `claude mcp add azure` (or use the MS-published Azure MCP server)

---

### 🎯 Skills (custom, project-specific)

#### `adr-create` (top pick)
**Why**: 4 ADRs landed, **5 more pending in specific weeks** (0005 severity tiers W3, 0006 ADF auth W2, 0007 Airflow callback W2, 0008 MCP W7, 0009 repo layout W1). Issue [#10](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/10) also wants `Consulted` and `Supersedes` fields added to the template. A skill that templates ADRs (next free number, frontmatter, sections, branch name) eliminates 90% of the friction and prevents the template drift that prompted #10.
**Create**: `.claude/skills/adr-create/SKILL.md`
**Invocation**: User-only (`/adr-create`) — bundles next-number-detection script + template
```yaml
---
name: adr-create
description: Scaffold a new ADR with auto-numbered filename, frontmatter, and standard sections. Use when capturing a significant architecture decision.
disable-model-invocation: true
---
```

#### `gh-issue-from-finding`
**Why**: Working-agreement #3 ("defects → GitHub issue, never silent fixes") and the new `/review-before-merge` workflow both require well-formatted issues with PR-source backlinks. We just filed 6 such issues this session manually — slow and error-prone. A skill that takes a finding description + source PR/comment URL and produces a properly-labelled, properly-linked issue would compress that to one command.
**Create**: `.claude/skills/gh-issue-from-finding/SKILL.md`
**Invocation**: User-only

---

### ⚡ Hooks

#### PreToolUse: block writes to `.env*` files (top pick — security)
**Why**: Repo is **public**. `.env` is gitignored, but a hook gives defense in depth — if a contributor (or Claude) tries to create `.env` (not `.env.example`), the hook blocks the write before it even hits disk. Echoes the lesson from PR #6's `.pptx` near-miss: irreversible mistakes on a public repo need preemptive guards, not post-hoc detection.
**Where**: `.claude/settings.json`
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "if echo \"$CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS\" | grep -E '(^|/)\\.env(\\.|$)' | grep -v '\\.env\\.example'; then echo 'Blocked: .env files must not be committed (public repo). Use .env.example.' >&2; exit 2; fi"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

#### PostToolUse: Black + Ruff on Python edits (kicks in Week 1)
**Why**: Working-agreement #18 mandates Black formatter + Ruff lint enforced via CI gate. A local PostToolUse hook gives instant feedback the moment a `.py` file is edited — catches issues before commit instead of at CI time, matching the project's "fail fast" philosophy. No-op until Week 1 lands Python code.
**Where**: `.claude/settings.json`
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Edit|Write",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "FILES=$(echo \"$CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS\" | tr ' ' '\\n' | grep '\\.py$'); [ -n \"$FILES\" ] && (black $FILES 2>&1 || true) && (ruff check --fix $FILES 2>&1 || true)"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

---

### 🤖 Subagents

#### `orchestration-abstraction-guard` (top pick — project-specific risk)
**Why**: ADR 0004's biggest stated risk is provider-specific branching bypassing the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction. CLAUDE.md §11 lists it as #2 in "What NOT to do." A subagent triggered on PRs touching `backend/app/orchestration/` or `backend/app/services/` that scans for hardcoded `'adf'`/`'airflow'` string checks outside the abstraction would catch the exact regression the ADR warns about — and would catch it consistently regardless of which contributor or which week.
**Where**: `.claude/agents/orchestration-abstraction-guard.md`

#### `migration-safety` (kicks in Week 5+)
**Why**: Working-agreement #24 mandates "backward-compatible migrations only — no `DROP COLUMN` + code change in same PR." This is exactly the kind of rule humans forget under deadline pressure. A subagent that scans Alembic migration files for `DROP COLUMN`, `DROP TABLE`, `ALTER COLUMN ... NOT NULL` (without default), and `RENAME COLUMN` would flag the violations cheaply. Especially valuable from Week 5 onward when real result data starts living in Postgres.
**Where**: `.claude/agents/migration-safety.md`

---

### 📦 Plugins

#### `commit-commands` plugin
**Why**: Project enforces conventional commits via ADR 0002 and the PR template's "Type of change" checklist. The `commit-commands` plugin provides `/commit` and related slash commands that scaffold conventional-commit messages — reduces the "what was the right prefix again?" friction that the working agreement implicitly creates.
**Install**: via plugin marketplace

---

Likely high-value-but-not-top-2 candidates I held back: GitHub MCP (you use `gh` heavily), Postman MCP (Weeks 2–3 API design), PR-title conventional-commit validator hook, `adr-validator` subagent, `pr-check` skill mirroring working-agreement #1 checklist.

**Want help implementing any of these?** Say which and I'll set them up — for the .env-block hook in particular I'd recommend doing it before Week 1 since the public-repo blast radius is real.

  "content": "---\nname: adr-create\ndescription: Scaffold a new Architecture Decision Record under docs/adr/ with auto-numbered filename, standard frontmatter (Status / Date / Deciders / optional Consulted / Supersedes / Superseded by), and the canonical sections (Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, Related). Use when the user wants to capture a significant architectural decision, or asks \"let's ADR that.\"\ndisable-model-invocation: true\n---\n\n# adr-create\n\n## Purpose\n\nCreate a new ADR in `docs/adr/` that follows the conventions documented in `docs/adr/README.md` and is consistent with ADRs 0001–0004 already in the repo.\n\n## Usage\n\nUser invokes this skill with a short topic for the ADR. Optional args:\n- `--status accepted|proposed|superseded` (default: `Accepted`)\n- `--consulted \"@user1, @user2\"` (omit if engineering-only decision)\n- `--supersedes 0007` (omit if not superseding)\n\n## Steps\n\n1. **Determine the next ADR number.** Read existing files in `docs/adr/` matching `NNNN-*.md`, find the highest number, increment by 1, zero-pad to 4 digits. If `docs/adr/` doesn't exist, start at `0001`.\n\n2. **Derive a kebab-case slug** from the user's topic. Drop articles. Examples:\n   - \"Severity tier weights\" → `severity-tier-weights`\n   - \"Use Pydantic Settings for config\" → `use-pydantic-settings-for-config`\n\n3. **Create the file** at `docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md` using the template below. Today's date in ISO format (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Deciders defaults to the git user (`git config user.name` mapped to GitHub handle if known, else literal name).\n\n4. **Update the index** at `docs/adr/README.md`:\n   - Add a row to the \"Index\" table at the end (above any \"Pending\" section).\n   - If the new ADR was in the Pending list, remove it from there.\n\n5. **Stage but do not commit.** The user runs `git add` + the commit themselves per working-agreement #1 (one functionality per commit, manual commit step).\n\n6. **Print next steps:**\n   - \"Open `docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md` and fill in Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives.\"\n   - \"Branch suggestion: `docs/adr-NNNN-<slug>`\"\n   - \"PR title suggestion: `docs: add ADR NNNN — <human title>`\"\n\n## Template\n\n```markdown\n# ADR NNNN — <Human-readable title>\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD\n- **Deciders:** @<github-handle>\n- **Consulted:** <optional, e.g. @product-owner, @security-team>\n- **Supersedes:** <optional, e.g. ADR-0007>\n- **Superseded by:** <optional, e.g. ADR-0042>\n\n## Context\n\n<What problem are we deciding about? What forces are at play (constraints, requirements, prior decisions)? Keep to 1–3 paragraphs.>\n\n## Decision\n\n**<One-sentence statement of the decision, in bold.>**\n\n<Then the details: how it works, what's in scope, what's out of scope.>\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- <bullet>\n- <bullet>\n\n**Negative**\n- <bullet>\n- <bullet>\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **<Alternative 1>** — rejected. <Why.>\n- **<Alternative 2>** — rejected. <Why.>\n\n## Related\n\n- <Link to related ADRs, issues, PRs, or code paths.>\n```\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Status field is required.** Default to `Accepted` unless `--status` says otherwise.\n- **Date is today's date** in ISO format.\n- **Consulted, Supersedes, Superseded by are optional** — include the label even if empty so future editors see the slot.\n- **Body sections in this exact order:** Context → Decision → Consequences (with Positive/Negative subheadings) → Alternatives considered → Related.\n- **Slug must match the convention** in `docs/adr/README.md`: lowercase, kebab-case, no leading article.\n- **Filename matches title:** `NNNN-<slug>.md` where the slug is also derivable from the H1 title.\n- **README index is the source of truth** for which ADRs exist. Always update it.\n- **Do not commit.** Stage only. The user commits manually so they can review the diff.\n\n## Anti-patterns to avoid\n\n- Don't reuse a number. If `docs/adr/0005-*.md` exists, the next one is `0006`, never `0005a` or `0005-v2`.\n- Don't auto-fill Decision/Context with boilerplate. Leave them as the template placeholders so the user must write the actual content.\n- Don't add the ADR to the \"Pending\" section of README — Pending is for ADRs known to be coming in a specific week but not yet written.\n"

This skill compresses the manual ceremony of writing a well-formatted issue into one command.\n\n## Usage\n\nUser invokes with a short description of the finding. Required context the skill must collect:\n- `--from-pr <N>` — source PR where the finding was identified (optional but strongly preferred for traceability)\n- `--from-comment <url>` — direct link to the /review comment (optional)\n- `--severity critical|high|medium|low` (defaults to `medium`; use `critical` only for production-down / data-loss; never use `critical` for security — see `--security` flag below)\n- `--type bug|enhancement|documentation` (defaults to `bug`; maps to GitHub label)\n- `--security` — flag for security-adjacent issues. If set, the skill SHOULD NOT proceed with `gh issue create`; instead it prints the GitHub Security Advisories URL and exits, per the security-disclosure policy (see issue [#9](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/9) for context).\n- `--blocker-for-week <N>` — optional, marks the issue as a Week-N blocker.\n\n## Steps\n\n1. **If `--security` is set**, do not create a public issue. Print:\n   ```\n   Security-adjacent finding — do not file as a public issue.\n   Report via GitHub Security Advisory:\n   https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new\n   ```\n   Exit successfully without calling `gh issue create`.\n\n2. **Resolve the label** from `--type`:\n   - `bug` → `bug`\n   - `enhancement` → `enhancement`\n   - `documentation` → `documentation`\n\n3. **Build the issue title** as a plain descriptive sentence (not a `fix:` / `feat:` prefix — that belongs on the fixing PR). Examples:\n   - \"ADR template missing Consulted field\"\n   - \"Architecture diagram doesn't include Apache Airflow\"\n\n4. **Build the issue body** using the template below.\n\n5. **Call** `gh issue create --title \"<title>\" --label \"<label>\" --body \"<body>\"`. Capture the returned URL.\n\n6. **Print to the user:**\n   ```\n   Filed: <issue url>\n   Backlink it in the source PR with:\n     gh pr comment <N> --body \"Tracked as <issue url>\"\n   When the fix PR lands, include `Fixes #<issue number>` in its body.\n   ```\n\n## Body template\n\n```markdown\n<one-line problem statement>\n\n## Items\n\n- [ ] <actionable item 1>\n- [ ] <actionable item 2>\n\n## Why this is a follow-up, not a same-PR fix\n<one sentence — typically \"non-load-bearing for current PR\" or \"must land before Week N\">\n\n## Source\n`/review` comment: <comment URL if provided>\nSource PR: #<N> (if provided)\n```\n\nIf `--blocker-for-week N` is set, prepend a bold line to the body:\n\n> **Must land before Week N (<short reason>).**\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Never create a public issue when `--security` is set.** Always route to Security Advisories.\n- **Issue title is a plain descriptive sentence.** No `fix:` / `feat:` prefix on issues — those are PR-side conventional types per ADR 0002. Issue templates at `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.md` currently pre-fill the wrong prefix; this skill counteracts that until issue [#8](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/8) is resolved.\n- **Backlink is the source of truth.** Always include the /review comment URL or source PR number so the issue can be cross-referenced.\n- **Fix PR must reference `Fixes #N`** to auto-close on merge (working-agreement #3 + PR template's \"Linked issue\" section).\n- **Do not create the fix branch from this skill.** Branch creation is a separate workflow.\n\n## Anti-patterns to avoid\n\n- Don't create an issue for findings on an *unmerged* PR — fix those in-place with a fixup commit on the branch. Issues are for findings deferred to a later PR or found after merge (see [/review-before-merge memory rule](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)).\n- Don't bulk-create issues for trivial nits. Use this for items that genuinely need tracking — typos and one-line clarity fixes can be done inline.\n- Don't include sensitive details (customer names, secrets, internal URLs, exploit payloads) in a public issue. If those are involved, the finding belongs in a Security Advisory.\n"
}
