CLAUDE.md §11 lists it as the second item in \"What NOT to do\":\n\n> Don't bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with provider-specific branching in service code.\n\nYou exist to catch that exact regression. Nothing else.\n\n## What you check\n\nAudit the changed code (use `gh pr diff <N>` if a PR number is provided, otherwise `git diff main...HEAD`) for:\n\n### 🔴 Hard violations (must block merge)\n\n1. **String literal comparisons against provider names** outside the orchestration package:\n   ```python\n   if provider == \"adf\": ...   # FORBIDDEN outside orchestration/\n   if provider == \"airflow\": ...\n   ```\n   These belong inside `backend/app/orchestration/<provider>.py` modules only. Service-layer code should call methods on a resolved `OrchestrationProvider` instance, not switch on its identity.\n\n2. **Importing provider implementations directly into service code:**\n   ```python\n   from backend.app.orchestration.adf import AdfProvider   # FORBIDDEN in services/\n   ```\n   Service code resolves providers through a registry / factory, not by importing concrete classes.\n\n3. **Hardcoded webhook routes per provider** (e.g., a route `/api/v1/adf/events` instead of the agreed `/api/v1/orchestration/events/{provider}` from ADR 0004).\n\n4. **`pipeline_runs` queries filtered by literal provider** without using the provider enum:\n   ```python\n   session.query(PipelineRun).filter(PipelineRun.provider == \"adf\")  # FORBIDDEN\n   # Acceptable form:\n   session.query(PipelineRun).filter(PipelineRun.provider == OrchestrationProviderEnum.ADF)\n   ```\n\n### 🟡 Yellow flags (call out, don't necessarily block)\n\n1. **Type hints using `str` for provider** instead of the `OrchestrationProviderEnum`.   "content": "---\nname: migration-safety\ndescription: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement #24 (\"backward-compatible migrations only — no DROP COLUMN + code change in the same PR\"). Use proactively on every PR that adds, modifies, or removes a file under backend/alembic/versions/. Also invoke when the user asks \"is this migration safe?\" or before any production deploy from Week 5 onward.\ntools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash\nmodel: sonnet\n---\n\nYou are a specialized Alembic migration reviewer enforcing **backward-compatible migrations only** per [working-agreement #24](../../CLAUDE.md).\n\n## Why this matters\n\nFrom Week 5 onward, `results` and `pipeline_runs` will hold real data. A migration that drops a column or renames it in the same release as the code change crashes any worker still running the old image during rollout. Two-step migrations (deploy code that tolerates both shapes → migrate → deploy code that assumes new shape) are mandatory.\n\n## What you check\n\nAudit every `.py` file under `backend/alembic/versions/` that's added or modified in the diff. Use `gh pr diff <N>` if a PR number is provided, otherwise `git diff main...HEAD -- 'backend/alembic/versions/*.py'`.\n\n### 🔴 Hard violations (block merge)\n\nEach of these is unsafe under concurrent rolling deploy and must be split into a two-step migration:\n\n1. **`op.drop_column(...)`** — dropping a column the old code may still reference. Two-step: (1) deploy code that stops reading/writing the column; (2) later release drops the column.\n2. **`op.drop_table(...)`** — same reasoning at table level.\n3. **`op.alter_column(..., nullable=False)`** where the column was previously nullable and the migration does **not** include a `server_default` to backfill. Old code writing NULL will fail.\n4. **`op.alter_column(..., type_=...)`** changing a column type in a non-implicit way (e.g., `String → Integer`, `Integer → UUID`). Implicit widening (`String(50) → String(255)`) is acceptable; type *changes* are not.\n5. **`op.rename_column(...)`** — same operational issue as drop+add. Must be a two-step: (1) add new column, dual-write in code; (2) backfill; (3) flip reads; (4) later release drops the old column.\n6. **`op.rename_table(...)`** — same reasoning.\n7. **`op.drop_constraint(...)` for FK or unique** where the constraint enforces data invariants the application depends on. Acceptable only if explicitly noted as part of a planned rollout.\n8. **Missing `downgrade()` body** (only `pass`) for any non-trivial migration. Rollback path must exist per the migration PR checklist in `.github/pull_request_template.md`.\n9. **DDL inside a single transaction with DML on the same table** — risks deadlocks on production-sized tables. Heuristic: presence of `op.execute(\"UPDATE ...\")` followed by structural changes in the same migration.\n\n### 🟡 Yellow flags (call out, don't necessarily block)\n\n1. **Index creation without `CONCURRENTLY`** on Postgres for a table that will be large (`runs`, `results`, `pipeline_runs`, `check_results`). Use `op.create_index(..., postgresql_concurrently=True)` and a separate transaction.\n2. **No data backfill plan** for a new NOT NULL column with no `server_default`.\n3. **Migration touches tables in two unrelated domains** in one revision (e.g., `connections` and `pipeline_runs` together). Suggests two migrations bundled.\n4. **No docstring at the top of the migration file** describing intent and the rollout sequence.\n5. **`down_revision` doesn't match the previously-latest migration** — possible merge conflict that got resolved incorrectly.\n\n### 🟢 Acceptable patterns\n\n- Add nullable column → backfill in a separate release → set NOT NULL → drop default. Three migrations, three releases.\n- Adding a new table.\n- Adding a new index using `postgresql_concurrently=True` in its own migration.\n- Adding constraints in `NOT VALID` mode, then `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` in a later migration.\n\n## How to report\n\nProduce a structured report:\n\n1. **🔴 Hard violations** — file:line, operation, why it's unsafe, suggested two-step split.\n2. **🟡 Concerns** — file:line, operation, suggested change.\n3. **Rollback check** — for each migration, confirm `downgrade()` is implemented and inverts `upgrade()`.\n4. **Two-step plan** (if a violation requires it) — outline the staged rollout the user should adopt.\n5. **✅ Verdict** — one of:\n   - `Pass — migration is backward-compatible.`\n   - `Conditional — N concerns. Discuss with whoever runs the deploy.`\n   - `Block — N hard violations. Must split into two-step rollout before merge.`\n\n## Operational note\n\nThis agent reads migration files and reports — it does NOT modify them. The author splits the migration based on the report. Two-step migrations land as two separate PRs (one per step) per working-agreement #1.\n\n## Source documents (your authority)\n\n- [CLAUDE.md §6 Database — backward-compatible migrations only](../../CLAUDE.md)\n- [.github/pull_request_template.md — Schema migration checklist](../../.github/pull_request_template.md)\n"
}

# Code review — PR #13 `chore: add context7 MCP server`

**Overview**
8-line `.mcp.json` at repo root with a single entry: `context7` served via `npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp`. Picked up automatically by Claude Code sessions in this repo per the team-sharing convention.

## Findings

### 🟡 No version pin — contradicts the project's "pin GX Core" lesson
`["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]` pulls **latest** on every cold start. ADR 0003 explicitly mandates pinning for dependencies that drift across releases — that lesson applies just as much to MCP servers, which execute arbitrary code on the local machine.

Suggested fix:
```json
"args": ["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp@1"]
```
Pin to a major version range for forward-compat; bump deliberately when needed. Matches the project's pinning philosophy.

### 🟢 Supply-chain note worth surfacing
`.mcp.json` checked into a public repo means anyone who clones gets a config that runs `npx`-pulled code on their machine after Claude Code's trust prompt. Worth:
- One-line comment in `.mcp.json` (JSON doesn't support comments, so this would live in CLAUDE.md instead), OR
- A short CLAUDE.md addition under §12 or §Appendix noting which MCP servers are configured, who publishes them, and what permissions Claude Code will request.

This isn't a vulnerability — Upstash is the legitimate publisher and the trust prompt is in place. It's about making the security posture explicit for contributors.

### 🟢 CLAUDE.md doesn't mention `.mcp.json` exists
CLAUDE.md §Appendix lists "MCP | FastMCP — 8 curated tools at `/mcp`" referring to the project's *own* MCP server (Week 7). It doesn't mention this *team-shared* `.mcp.json` for client-side MCP servers we consume. Worth a one-line addition in a follow-up so the two distinct MCP concepts don't get confused.

### 🟢 JSON validity, structure
- Schema is valid for the documented `mcpServers` shape ✓
- Trailing newline present ✓
- 2-space indent consistent with other JSON in this repo (none yet, but matches typical convention) ✓

## Correctness, performance, security
- ✅ Correct command and args for the published context7 server.
- ⚠️ Unpinned version = supply-chain risk gradient (caught by 🟡 above).
- ⚪ Cold start = one-time npx download per session; performance acceptable.
- ⚪ No tests applicable for a config file.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** The version-pin fix (🟡) is one character change with real benefit and matches project policy — recommend doing it as a fixup commit on this branch before merge. The two 🟢 items are CLAUDE.md follow-ups, fine to file as issues.

# Code review — PR #14 `chore: add Claude Code hooks (.env block + Python autoformat)`

**Overview**
Creates `.claude/settings.json` (27 lines) with two hooks: PreToolUse `.env` blocker on Write/Edit/MultiEdit, and PostToolUse Black + Ruff on `.py` files. Hook commands are inline shell.

## Findings

### 🔴 Hooks rely on `$CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS` — may silently no-op
Claude Code's documented hook contract is **JSON on stdin** with shape:
```json
{ "tool_name": "Write", "tool_input": { "file_path": "..." } }
```
The `CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS` env var is set in some versions/contexts but isn't the canonical interface. If it's empty or unset in the current Claude Code build:

- The PreToolUse `.env` block produces an empty string → grep matches nothing → **hook silently passes**. This is a *false sense of security*: contributor thinks `.env` is blocked, but it isn't.
- The PostToolUse hook produces `FILES=""` → both branches skipped → no formatting. Less dangerous, just inert.

Recommend reading stdin JSON via `jq`. Example for the PreToolUse hook:
```bash
file_path=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')
if printf '%s' "$file_path" | grep -qE '(^|/)\.env($|\.)' && ! printf '%s' "$file_path" | grep -qE '\.env\.example$'; then
  echo 'Blocked: .env files must not be created or edited (public repo). Use .env.example as the template.' >&2
  exit 2
fi
```
Same for PostToolUse — `jq` out the file path, run Black/Ruff if `.py`. Adds a `jq` dependency but `jq` is ubiquitous and the contract is documented.

Worth verifying behaviour against the current Claude Code version before merge — if `CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS` *is* set on this Mac, the current hook works locally, but it'll break for any contributor on a different version.

### 🟡 Path-with-spaces bug
`tr ' ' '\n'` converts spaces to newlines to handle space-separated lists, but it ALSO splits a single path that contains a space:
```
"/Users/arijit/My Project/foo.py" → "/Users/arijit/My" + "Project/foo.py"
```
Neither half passes the `.py$` filter, so Black silently skips. Stdin-JSON approach (above) avoids this — paths come out as single clean strings.

### 🟡 PostToolUse silently swallows all errors
`xargs black ... || true` and `xargs ruff ... || true` mean if Black crashes or Ruff finds something it can't auto-fix, the user gets nothing. For lint issues this is fine (CI catches them), but a Black crash on a syntactically-invalid file should at least be visible.

Consider dropping the `|| true` on Black — Black's exit code 1 (would-format) is benign because we run with no `--check`, so non-zero only happens on actual errors (parse failures), which the user should see.

### 🟢 `$schema` URL — verify it resolves
`https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json` — if schemastore doesn't have this entry, the URL is a 404 and IDE autocomplete won't work. Harmless at runtime. Worth a quick browser check; if 404, drop the `$schema` line until Anthropic publishes one.

### 🟢 No file-type prefilter on `matcher`
`matcher: "Write|Edit|MultiEdit"` matches every text edit. The hook command then filters by file extension. Every Markdown / JSON / TOML edit forks a shell for a no-op. Minor performance overhead; not worth a separate matcher per file type for now.

### 🟢 `.envrc` (direnv) not blocked
Regex `(^|/)\.env($|\.)` matches `.env`, `.env.local`, etc., but **not** `.envrc`. direnv files can contain secrets and aren't currently `.gitignore`d. Either intentional (let direnv users self-manage) or oversight. Recommend either:
- Add `.envrc` to the regex: `(^|/)\.env($|\.|rc$)`
- Or add `.envrc` to `.gitignore` and leave the hook narrow.

### 🟢 Quoting / shell-injection — safe
`"$CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS"` is properly quoted; no expansion risk from path contents.

## Correctness, conventions, security
- ✅ Exit code 2 for PreToolUse blocking — correct per hooks contract.
- ✅ JSON is well-formed; `$schema` reference is a nice touch (if URL resolves).
- ⚠️ Critical issue: env-var dependency may mean the protection is non-functional in some Claude Code versions.
- ⚠️ Format-on-save will be inert until Week 1 (Python lands + Black installed in conda env). Acceptable.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** The `CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS` reliance (🔴) is the blocker — if the hook silently no-ops, the protection is theatre, which is worse than no hook at all (gives false confidence). Recommend the jq-from-stdin rewrite as a fixup commit on this branch. The 🟡 items can be folded into the same fixup. 🟢 items are follow-up issues.

@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+---
+name: adr-create
+description: Scaffold a new Architecture Decision Record under docs/adr/ with auto-numbered filename, standard frontmatter (Status / Date / Deciders / optional Consulted / Supersedes / Superseded by), and the canonical sections (Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, Related). Use when the user wants to capture a significant architectural decision, or asks "let's ADR that."
+disable-model-invocation: true
+---
+
+# adr-create
+
+## Purpose
+
+Create a new ADR in `docs/adr/` that follows the conventions documented in `docs/adr/README.md` and is consistent with ADRs 0001–0004 already in the repo.
+
+## Usage
+
+User invokes this skill with a short topic for the ADR. Optional args:
+- `--status accepted|proposed|superseded` (default: `Accepted`)
+- `--consulted "@user1, @user2"` (omit if engineering-only decision)
+- `--supersedes 0007` (omit if not superseding)
+
+## Steps
+
+1. **Determine the next ADR number.** Read existing files in `docs/adr/` matching `NNNN-*.md`, find the highest number, increment by 1, zero-pad to 4 digits. If `docs/adr/` doesn't exist, start at `0001`.
+
+2. **Derive a kebab-case slug** from the user's topic. Drop articles. Examples:
+   - "Severity tier weights" → `severity-tier-weights`
+   - "Use Pydantic Settings for config" → `use-pydantic-settings-for-config`
+
+3. **Create the file** at `docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md` using the template below. Today's date in ISO format (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Deciders defaults to the git user (`git config user.name` mapped to GitHub handle if known, else literal name).
+
+4. **Update the index** at `docs/adr/README.md`:
+   - Add a row to the "Index" table at the end (above any "Pending" section).
+   - If the new ADR was in the Pending list, remove it from there.
+
+5. **Stage but do not commit.** The user runs `git add` + the commit themselves per working-agreement #1 (one functionality per commit, manual commit step).
+
+6. **Print next steps:**
+   - "Open `docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md` and fill in Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives."
+   - "Branch suggestion: `docs/adr-NNNN-<slug>`"
+   - "PR title suggestion: `docs: add ADR NNNN — <human title>`"
+
+## Template
+
+```markdown
+# ADR NNNN — <Human-readable title>
+
+- **Status:** Accepted
+- **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
+- **Deciders:** @<github-handle>
+- **Consulted:** <optional, e.g. @product-owner, @security-team>
+- **Supersedes:** <optional, e.g. ADR-0007>
+- **Superseded by:** <optional, e.g. ADR-0042>
+
+## Context
+
+<What problem are we deciding about? What forces are at play (constraints, requirements, prior decisions)? Keep to 1–3 paragraphs.>
+
+## Decision
+
+**<One-sentence statement of the decision, in bold.>**
+
+<Then the details: how it works, what's in scope, what's out of scope.>
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive**
+- <bullet>
+- <bullet>
+
+**Negative**
+- <bullet>
+- <bullet>
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- **<Alternative 1>** — rejected. <Why.>
+- **<Alternative 2>** — rejected. <Why.>
+
+## Related
+
+- <Link to related ADRs, issues, PRs, or code paths.>
+```
+
+## Rules
+
+- **Status field is required.** Default to `Accepted` unless `--status` says otherwise.
+- **Date is today's date** in ISO format.
+- **Consulted, Supersedes, Superseded by are optional** — include the label even if empty so future editors see the slot.
+- **Body sections in this exact order:** Context → Decision → Consequences (with Positive/Negative subheadings) → Alternatives considered → Related.
+- **Slug must match the convention** in `docs/adr/README.md`: lowercase, kebab-case, no leading article.
+- **Filename matches title:** `NNNN-<slug>.md` where the slug is also derivable from the H1 title.
+- **README index is the source of truth** for which ADRs exist. Always update it.
+- **Do not commit.** Stage only. The user commits manually so they can review the diff.
+
+## Anti-patterns to avoid
+
+- Don't reuse a number. If `docs/adr/0005-*.md` exists, the next one is `0006`, never `0005a` or `0005-v2`.
+- Don't auto-fill Decision/Context with boilerplate. Leave them as the template placeholders so the user must write the actual content.
+- Don't add the ADR to the "Pending" section of README — Pending is for ADRs known to be coming in a specific week but not yet written.

Use when a defect or non-blocking polish item is identified during /review or normal work, and working-agreement #3 ("defects → GitHub issue, never silent fixes") applies.
+disable-model-invocation: true
+---
+
+# gh-issue-from-finding
+
+## Purpose
+
+Operationalize working-agreement #3: every defect (and every deferred-but-known polish item) becomes a GitHub issue *before* it gets fixed. This skill compresses the manual ceremony of writing a well-formatted issue into one command.
+
+## Usage
+
+User invokes with a short description of the finding. Required context the skill must collect:
+- `--from-pr <N>` — source PR where the finding was identified (optional but strongly preferred for traceability)
+- `--from-comment <url>` — direct link to the /review comment (optional)
+- `--severity critical|high|medium|low` (defaults to `medium`; use `critical` only for production-down / data-loss; never use `critical` for security — see `--security` flag below)
+- `--type bug|enhancement|documentation` (defaults to `bug`; maps to GitHub label)
+- `--security` — flag for security-adjacent issues. If set, the skill SHOULD NOT proceed with `gh issue create`; instead it prints the GitHub Security Advisories URL and exits, per the security-disclosure policy (see issue [#9](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/9) for context).
+- `--blocker-for-week <N>` — optional, marks the issue as a Week-N blocker.
+
+## Steps
+
+1. **If `--security` is set**, do not create a public issue. Print:
+   ```
+   Security-adjacent finding — do not file as a public issue.
+   Report via GitHub Security Advisory:
+   https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new
+   ```
+   Exit successfully without calling `gh issue create`.
+
+2. **Resolve the label** from `--type`:
+   - `bug` → `bug`
+   - `enhancement` → `enhancement`
+   - `documentation` → `documentation`
+
+3. **Build the issue title** as a plain descriptive sentence (not a `fix:` / `feat:` prefix — that belongs on the fixing PR). Examples:
+   - "ADR template missing Consulted field"
+   - "Architecture diagram doesn't include Apache Airflow"
+
+4. **Build the issue body** using the template below.
+
+5. **Call** `gh issue create --title "<title>" --label "<label>" --body "<body>"`. Capture the returned URL.
+
+6. **Print to the user:**
+   ```
+   Filed: <issue url>
+   Backlink it in the source PR with:
+     gh pr comment <N> --body "Tracked as <issue url>"
+   When the fix PR lands, include `Fixes #<issue number>` in its body.
+   ```
+
+## Body template
+
+```markdown
+<one-line problem statement>
+
+## Items
+
+- [ ] <actionable item 1>
+- [ ] <actionable item 2>
+
+## Why this is a follow-up, not a same-PR fix
+<one sentence — typically "non-load-bearing for current PR" or "must land before Week N">
+
+## Source
+`/review` comment: <comment URL if provided>
+Source PR: #<N> (if provided)
+```
+
+If `--blocker-for-week N` is set, prepend a bold line to the body:
+
+> **Must land before Week N (<short reason>).**
+
+## Rules
+
+- **Never create a public issue when `--security` is set.** Always route to Security Advisories.
+- **Issue title is a plain descriptive sentence.** No `fix:` / `feat:` prefix on issues — those are PR-side conventional types per ADR 0002. Issue templates at `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.md` currently pre-fill the wrong prefix; this skill counteracts that until issue [#8](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/8) is resolved.
+- **Backlink is the source of truth.** Always include the /review comment URL or source PR number so the issue can be cross-referenced.
+- **Fix PR must reference `Fixes #N`** to auto-close on merge (working-agreement #3 + PR template's "Linked issue" section).
+- **Do not create the fix branch from this skill.** Branch creation is a separate workflow.
+
+## Anti-patterns to avoid
+
+- Don't create an issue for findings on an *unmerged* PR — fix those in-place with a fixup commit on the branch. Issues are for findings deferred to a later PR or found after merge (see [/review-before-merge memory rule](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)).
+- Don't bulk-create issues for trivial nits. Use this for items that genuinely need tracking — typos and one-line clarity fixes can be done inline.
+- Don't include sensitive details (customer names, secrets, internal URLs, exploit payloads) in a public issue. If those are involved, the finding belongs in a Security Advisory.
```

# Code review — PR #15 `chore: add adr-create and gh-issue-from-finding skills`

**Overview**
Two user-only (`disable-model-invocation: true`) skills under `.claude/skills/`. Pure instruction (no bundled scripts) for Claude to execute when the user invokes `/adr-create <topic>` or `/gh-issue-from-finding <description>`. 186 lines total.

## Findings

### 🟡 adr-create: "Deciders defaults from git user" is hand-wavy and likely produces invalid handles
Step 3 says:
> Deciders defaults to the git user (`git config user.name` mapped to GitHub handle if known, else literal name).

`git config user.name` returns a name like `"Arijit Roy"` — prepending `@` gives `@Arijit Roy` which is not a valid GitHub mention. Existing ADRs all use `@TheurgicDuke771`. The "mapped to GitHub handle if known" phrase has no mechanism behind it.

Options:
- Hardcode `@TheurgicDuke771` while solo (simplest)
- Read from `git config github.user` if set (some users configure this)
- Use `gh api /user --jq .login` to authoritatively get the handle
- Or prompt the user on first invocation and cache

Recommend the `gh api /user --jq .login` approach — most accurate, requires `gh` CLI which is already in use.

### 🟡 adr-create: Status case mismatch
- CLI arg: `--status accepted|proposed|superseded` (lowercase)
- Template default: `Accepted` (title-case)

Normalize to title-case in the rendered output regardless of the arg's case.

Also: template options omit `Deprecated` (ADRs sometimes get deprecated without supersession). Worth adding.

### 🟡 adr-create: No deterministic script for next-number detection
Step 1 ("find the highest number, increment by 1, zero-pad to 4 digits") is pure prose for Claude to re-infer each invocation. Skills can bundle scripts — recommend a tiny `next-number.sh`:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
last=$(ls docs/adr/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's|.*/([0-9]+)-.*|\1|' | sort -n | tail -1)
printf '%04d\n' $(( 10#${last:-0} + 1 ))
```
Deterministic, fast, no LLM re-derivation per call.

### 🟢 gh-issue-from-finding: `--severity` flag declared but never used
The Usage section defines `--severity critical|high|medium|low` with explicit guidance, but neither the Steps nor the Body template reference it. Either:
- Use it: add `**Severity:** <value>` to the body template, or map to a `priority:high` / `priority:critical` label (after creating those labels in the repo).
- Drop it: declared flags that do nothing confuse users.

### 🟢 gh-issue-from-finding: `--type` mapping is identity
Step 2 says `bug → bug`, `enhancement → enhancement`, `documentation → documentation`. Could collapse to "the `--type` value is used directly as the label name." Or pre-create labels in the repo for clarity.

Note: when I filed issues #7–#12 earlier, the `bug` label didn't error (it's a GitHub default), but `security` did (had to drop it). The skill assumes labels exist — if a user passes `--type custom`, `gh issue create` will fail with "label not found." Worth either validating up front or saying "label must exist."

### 🟢 Both skills: quoting safety in `gh` calls
The body template contains markdown with backticks, code blocks, `$` signs, and emoji. `gh issue create --body "<body>"` with shell-interpolated double quotes will choke on `$variable`-like contents and backticks. The skill should explicitly use heredoc:
```bash
gh issue create --title "$TITLE" --label "$LABEL" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
<body>
EOF
)"
```
The single-quoted heredoc disables expansion. Without this, anyone using the skill on a real review finding may produce a mangled body or shell error.

### 🟢 Both skills: no "Test scenarios" / examples section
Skill docs benefit from concrete worked examples ("if user runs `/adr-create severity tier weights`, you produce `docs/adr/0005-severity-tier-weights.md` with content X"). Helps Claude execute consistently and helps human readers verify the skill is doing what they expect.

## Correctness, conventions, security
- ✅ `disable-model-invocation: true` correctly set for user-only commands.
- ✅ Cross-references to issues #8 and #9 reflect actual filed issues — keeps the skill honest about known gaps.
- ✅ `--security` flag correctly routes to Security Advisories instead of public issues.
- ✅ "Don't bulk-create issues for trivial nits" anti-pattern is good guardrail.
- ⚠️ Both skills assume a clean shell environment with `gh`, `git`, etc. — fine for this project's constraints.
- ⚪ No tests applicable for instruction-only skills.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** None of the findings are blockers; the skills are functional as-written. But:
- The handle-detection issue (🟡 first finding) will produce broken `@mentions` on the first real use, so worth a fixup before merge.
- The other 🟡 items (case normalization, helper script) are quality improvements that compound over time.
- 🟢 items are polish — defer to follow-up issue.

Recommend doing the handle-detection fix + quoting-safety mention in a fixup commit on this branch; file the rest as a follow-up issue.

+---
+name: migration-safety
+description: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement #24 ("backward-compatible migrations only — no DROP COLUMN + code change in the same PR"). Use proactively on every PR that adds, modifies, or removes a file under backend/alembic/versions/. Also invoke when the user asks "is this migration safe?" or before any production deploy from Week 5 onward.
+tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
+model: sonnet
+---
+
+You are a specialized Alembic migration reviewer enforcing **backward-compatible migrations only** per [working-agreement #24](../../CLAUDE.md).
+
+## Why this matters
+
+From Week 5 onward, `results` and `pipeline_runs` will hold real data. A migration that drops a column or renames it in the same release as the code change crashes any worker still running the old image during rollout. Two-step migrations (deploy code that tolerates both shapes → migrate → deploy code that assumes new shape) are mandatory.
+
+## What you check
+
+Audit every `.py` file under `backend/alembic/versions/` that's added or modified in the diff. Use `gh pr diff <N>` if a PR number is provided, otherwise `git diff main...HEAD -- 'backend/alembic/versions/*.py'`.
+
+### 🔴 Hard violations (block merge)
+
+Each of these is unsafe under concurrent rolling deploy and must be split into a two-step migration:
+
+1. **`op.drop_column(...)`** — dropping a column the old code may still reference. Two-step: (1) deploy code that stops reading/writing the column; (2) later release drops the column.
+2. **`op.drop_table(...)`** — same reasoning at table level.
+3. **`op.alter_column(..., nullable=False)`** where the column was previously nullable and the migration does **not** include a `server_default` to backfill. Old code writing NULL will fail.
+4. **`op.alter_column(..., type_=...)`** changing a column type in a non-implicit way (e.g., `String → Integer`, `Integer → UUID`). Implicit widening (`String(50) → String(255)`) is acceptable; type *changes* are not.
+5. **`op.rename_column(...)`** — same operational issue as drop+add. Must be a two-step: (1) add new column, dual-write in code; (2) backfill; (3) flip reads; (4) later release drops the old column.
+6. **`op.rename_table(...)`** — same reasoning.
+7. **`op.drop_constraint(...)` for FK or unique** where the constraint enforces data invariants the application depends on. Acceptable only if explicitly noted as part of a planned rollout.
+8. **Missing `downgrade()` body** (only `pass`) for any non-trivial migration. Rollback path must exist per the migration PR checklist in `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
+9. **DDL inside a single transaction with DML on the same table** — risks deadlocks on production-sized tables. Heuristic: presence of `op.execute("UPDATE ...")` followed by structural changes in the same migration.
+
+### 🟡 Yellow flags (call out, don't necessarily block)
+
+1. **Index creation without `CONCURRENTLY`** on Postgres for a table that will be large (`runs`, `results`, `pipeline_runs`, `check_results`). Use `op.create_index(..., postgresql_concurrently=True)` and a separate transaction.
+2. **No data backfill plan** for a new NOT NULL column with no `server_default`.
+3. **Migration touches tables in two unrelated domains** in one revision (e.g., `connections` and `pipeline_runs` together). Suggests two migrations bundled.
+4. **No docstring at the top of the migration file** describing intent and the rollout sequence.
+5. **`down_revision` doesn't match the previously-latest migration** — possible merge conflict that got resolved incorrectly.
+
+### 🟢 Acceptable patterns
+
+- Add nullable column → backfill in a separate release → set NOT NULL → drop default. Three migrations, three releases.
+- Adding a new table.
+- Adding a new index using `postgresql_concurrently=True` in its own migration.
+- Adding constraints in `NOT VALID` mode, then `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` in a later migration.
+
+## How to report
+
+Produce a structured report:
+
+1. **🔴 Hard violations** — file:line, operation, why it's unsafe, suggested two-step split.
+2. **🟡 Concerns** — file:line, operation, suggested change.
+3. **Rollback check** — for each migration, confirm `downgrade()` is implemented and inverts `upgrade()`.
+4. **Two-step plan** (if a violation requires it) — outline the staged rollout the user should adopt.
+5. **✅ Verdict** — one of:
+   - `Pass — migration is backward-compatible.`
+   - `Conditional — N concerns. Discuss with whoever runs the deploy.`
+   - `Block — N hard violations. Must split into two-step rollout before merge.`
+
+## Operational note
+
+This agent reads migration files and reports — it does NOT modify them. The author splits the migration based on the report. Two-step migrations land as two separate PRs (one per step) per working-agreement #1.
+
+## Source documents (your authority)
+
+- [CLAUDE.md §6 Database — backward-compatible migrations only](../../CLAUDE.md)
+- [.github/pull_request_template.md — Schema migration checklist](../../.github/pull_request_template.md)

@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+---
+name: orchestration-abstraction-guard
+description: Specialized reviewer that audits backend code for provider-specific branching that bypasses the OrchestrationProvider abstraction. Use this proactively when reviewing any PR that touches backend/app/orchestration/, backend/app/services/, or backend/app/api/ — especially any code path handling ADF or Airflow events, trigger bindings, or pipeline_runs. Also invoke when the user asks "does this go through the abstraction?" or similar.
+tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
+model: sonnet
+---
+
+You are a specialized code reviewer guarding the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction defined in [ADR 0004](../../docs/adr/0004-orchestration-abstraction.md).
+
+## Your single concern
+
+ADR 0004's biggest stated risk is **provider-specific branching that bypasses the abstraction**. CLAUDE.md §11 lists it as the second item in "What NOT to do":
+
+> Don't bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with provider-specific branching in service code.
+
+You exist to catch that exact regression. Nothing else.
+
+## What you check
+
+Audit the changed code (use `gh pr diff <N>` if a PR number is provided, otherwise `git diff main...HEAD`) for:
+
+### 🔴 Hard violations (must block merge)
+
+1. **String literal comparisons against provider names** outside the orchestration package:
+   ```python
+   if provider == "adf": ...   # FORBIDDEN outside orchestration/
+   if provider == "airflow": ...
+   ```
+   These belong inside `backend/app/orchestration/<provider>.py` modules only. Service-layer code should call methods on a resolved `OrchestrationProvider` instance, not switch on its identity.
+
+2. **Importing provider implementations directly into service code:**
+   ```python
+   from backend.app.orchestration.adf import AdfProvider   # FORBIDDEN in services/
+   ```
+   Service code resolves providers through a registry / factory, not by importing concrete classes.
+
+3. **Hardcoded webhook routes per provider** (e.g., a route `/api/v1/adf/events` instead of the agreed `/api/v1/orchestration/events/{provider}` from ADR 0004).
+
+4. **`pipeline_runs` queries filtered by literal provider** without using the provider enum:
+   ```python
+   session.query(PipelineRun).filter(PipelineRun.provider == "adf")  # FORBIDDEN
+   # Acceptable form:
+   session.query(PipelineRun).filter(PipelineRun.provider == OrchestrationProviderEnum.ADF)
+   ```
+
+### 🟡 Yellow flags (call out, don't necessarily block)
+
+1. **Type hints using `str` for provider** instead of the `OrchestrationProviderEnum`. Suggests the enum hasn't been created or isn't being used.
+2. **`TODO` / `FIXME` / `XXX` comments mentioning ADF or Airflow** — may indicate deferred work that should be tracked as an issue per working-agreement #3.
+3. **Test data fixtures that only cover ADF**. Both providers should be exercised; ADF-only coverage suggests the abstraction has rotted.
+4. **`trigger_bindings` rows hardcoded to a single provider** in seed data or fixtures — should at least demonstrate both providers.
+
+### 🟢 Acceptable patterns
+
+- Provider-specific code **inside** `backend/app/orchestration/adf/` or `backend/app/orchestration/airflow/` — that's where it belongs.
+- Routing by enum at the orchestration boundary: `providers[request.provider].parse_event(payload, headers)`.
+- Provider-specific tests under `tests/orchestration/adf/` and `tests/orchestration/airflow/`.
+
+## How to report
+
+Produce a structured report with three sections:
+
+1. **🔴 Hard violations** (block-merge findings with file:line and the offending snippet)
+2. **🟡 Concerns** (worth discussing, not necessarily blocking)
+3. **✅ Verdict** — one of:
+   - `Pass — no abstraction violations found.`
+   - `Conditional — N concerns, no hard violations. Discuss before merge.`
+   - `Block — N hard violations. Must fix before merge.`
+
+Be specific. Each finding must cite a file path and line range. Never speculate; only flag what's actually in the diff.
+
+## Source documents (your authority)
+
+- [ADR 0004 — Orchestration abstraction](../../docs/adr/0004-orchestration-abstraction.md)
+- [CLAUDE.md §11 — What NOT to do](../../CLAUDE.md)
```

# Code review — PR #16 `chore: add orchestration-abstraction-guard and migration-safety subagents`

**Overview**
Two Markdown agent definitions under `.claude/agents/`. Both use `model: sonnet` with `Read, Grep, Glob, Bash` tool access. 142 lines total. Pure instruction documents — no code, no tests.

## Findings

### 🟡 orchestration-abstraction-guard: String-comparison check is incomplete
Hard violation #1 only lists `==`:
```python
if provider == "adf": ...   # FORBIDDEN
```
But the same anti-pattern can hide as:
```python
if provider != "adf": ...           # missed
if provider in ("adf", "airflow"):  # missed
match provider:
    case "adf": ...                  # missed
```
List of forbidden patterns should be exhaustive, or stated as a principle: *"any switch on provider identity — `==`, `!=`, `in`, `match/case`, or boolean coercion — is forbidden outside the orchestration package."*

### 🟡 orchestration-abstraction-guard: Test code exemption is implicit
Hard violation #2 forbids importing provider implementations into service code. But unit tests legitimately import concrete classes (`AdfProvider`) to exercise them in isolation. The "Acceptable patterns" section mentions `tests/orchestration/adf/` but doesn't explicitly allow imports there. Recommend an explicit acceptable pattern:
> ✅ Test code may import concrete provider implementations (`AdfProvider`, `AirflowProvider`) directly under `tests/orchestration/<provider>/` for isolation testing.

### 🟡 migration-safety: Missing `op.execute()` raw-SQL coverage
The 9 hard violations enumerate `op.drop_column`, `op.alter_column`, etc. — but raw SQL via `op.execute("ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN ...")` bypasses all of them. A `DROP COLUMN` via raw SQL is just as unsafe as via `op.drop_column`.

Add a hard violation:
> **10. `op.execute("...")` containing destructive keywords** (`DROP`, `RENAME`, `ALTER ... TYPE`, `NOT NULL` without default). Raw SQL must be reviewed by the same backward-compatibility rules.

### 🟢 migration-safety: No-files-yet behaviour unspecified
Pre-Week-1, `backend/alembic/versions/` doesn't exist. If the agent is invoked, it should cleanly report "no migration files in diff — pass" instead of erroring on a missing directory. Add a short note:
> If no migration files are present in the diff, report `Pass — no migration changes to review.` and exit.

### 🟢 Both agents: Bash access is broad
Both have `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`. Bash gives them arbitrary shell. The instructions only show `gh pr diff` and `git diff` usage, but nothing constrains them. Recommend a defensive line in each prompt:
> **Bash usage:** read-only `git` and `gh` commands only — never modify files, never run commands that produce side effects (no `git push`, no `gh pr create`, no installs).

Won't prevent misuse, but sets expectation and gives a checkable rule.

### 🟢 Both agents: No "false positives to avoid" section
String-comparison checks can over-fire on:
- String literals inside docstrings or comments (`"""... if provider == 'adf' ..."""`)
- Test fixtures parameterized over providers (`@pytest.mark.parametrize("provider", ["adf", "airflow"])`)
- Logging / metrics tags (`metrics.tag("provider", provider_str)`)

Add a "False positives to avoid" section to each agent so they don't cry wolf.

### 🟢 migration-safety: "Two-step plan" report section is high-effort
Step 4 asks the agent to "outline the staged rollout the user should adopt." That's substantial design work and the agent may get it wrong. Frame as "**Suggested approach** — verify with whoever owns the deploy" rather than presenting it as ready-to-execute. Reduces false confidence.

### 🟢 Both agents: `description` field is good and matches Claude's auto-invoke contract
Both descriptions start with "Specialized reviewer..." and include "Use proactively when..." — appropriate framing for Claude's auto-routing decisions.

### 🟢 Relative paths in source-document links
`../../CLAUDE.md` and `../../docs/adr/0004-orchestration-abstraction.md` — correct relative to `.claude/agents/`. ✓

## Correctness, conventions, security
- ✅ Frontmatter format matches Claude Code agent spec (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `model`).
- ✅ Source-document references cite real files that exist on `main`.
- ✅ Both agents reference working-agreements / ADRs by number, keeping authority traceable.
- ⚠️ Bash tool grant is broader than necessary (see 🟢 above).
- ⚪ No tests applicable for instruction-only agents.

## Verdict
**Conditional approve.** None of the findings block correctness — both agents will *work* as-written. But the orchestration-guard's incomplete pattern list (🟡 #1) and migration-safety's missing `op.execute` coverage (🟡 #3) are the kind of gaps that get exploited by accident the moment someone writes a `match provider:` block or a raw `op.execute("DROP COLUMN ...")`. Worth a fixup commit covering both 🟡 items before merge. 🟢 items can defer to a follow-up issue.

---

Posting findings.

Ruff keeps `|| true`\n  because non-zero on unfixable lint is benign (CI is the gate).\n\nFolds in the path-with-spaces 🟡 finding too.\nEOF\n)\" && git push",

1	---
2	name: migration-safety
3	description: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement #24 ("backward-compatible migrations only — no DROP COLUMN + code change in the same PR"). Use proactively on every PR that adds, modifies, or removes a file under backend/alembic/versions/. Also invoke when the user asks "is this migration safe?" or before any production deploy from Week 5 onward.
4	tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
5	model: sonnet
6	---
7	
8	You are a specialized Alembic migration reviewer enforcing **backward-compatible migrations only** per [working-agreement #24](../../CLAUDE.md).
9	
10	## Why this matters
11	
12	From Week 5 onward, `results` and `pipeline_runs` will hold real data. A migration that drops a column or renames it in the same release as the code change crashes any worker still running the old image during rollout. Two-step migrations (deploy code that tolerates both shapes → migrate → deploy code that assumes new shape) are mandatory.
13	
14	## What you check
15	
16	Audit every `.py` file under `backend/alembic/versions/` that's added or modified in the diff. Use `gh pr diff <N>` if a PR number is provided, otherwise `git diff main...HEAD -- 'backend/alembic/versions/*.py'`.
17	
18	### 🔴 Hard violations (block merge)
19	
20	Each of these is unsafe under concurrent rolling deploy and must be split into a two-step migration:
21	
22	1. **`op.drop_column(...)`** — dropping a column the old code may still reference. Two-step: (1) deploy code that stops reading/writing the column; (2) later release drops the column.
23	2. **`op.drop_table(...)`** — same reasoning at table level.
24	3. **`op.alter_column(..., nullable=False)`** where the column was previously nullable and the migration does **not** include a `server_default` to backfill. Old code writing NULL will fail.
25	4. **`op.alter_column(..., type_=...)`** changing a column type in a non-implicit way (e.g., `String → Integer`, `Integer → UUID`). Implicit widening (`String(50) → String(255)`) is acceptable; type *changes* are not.
26	5. **`op.rename_column(...)`** — same operational issue as drop+add. Must be a two-step: (1) add new column, dual-write in code; (2) backfill; (3) flip reads; (4) later release drops the old column.
27	6. **`op.rename_table(...)`** — same reasoning.
28	7. **`op.drop_constraint(...)` for FK or unique** where the constraint enforces data invariants the application depends on. Acceptable only if explicitly noted as part of a planned rollout.
29	8. **Missing `downgrade()` body** (only `pass`) for any non-trivial migration. Rollback path must exist per the migration PR checklist in `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
30	9. **DDL inside a single transaction with DML on the same table** — risks deadlocks on production-sized tables. Heuristic: presence of `op.execute("UPDATE ...")` followed by structural changes in the same migration.
31	10. **`op.execute("...")` containing destructive SQL keywords** — raw SQL bypasses the `op.*` pattern matchers above. Scan the string argument for `DROP`, `RENAME`, `ALTER ... TYPE`, `ALTER ... SET NOT NULL` (without `DEFAULT`), `TRUNCATE`. Same backward-compatibility rules apply as for the equivalent `op.*` calls.
32	
33	### 🟡 Yellow flags (call out, don't necessarily block)
34	
35	1. **Index creation without `CONCURRENTLY`** on Postgres for a table that will be large (`runs`, `results`, `pipeline_runs`, `check_results`). Use `op.create_index(..., postgresql_concurrently=True)` and a separate transaction.
36	2. **No data backfill plan** for a new NOT NULL column with no `server_default`.
37	3. **Migration touches tables in two unrelated domains** in one revision (e.g., `connections` and `pipeline_runs` together). Suggests two migrations bundled.
38	4. **No docstring at the top of the migration file** describing intent and the rollout sequence.
39	5. **`down_revision` doesn't match the previously-latest migration** — possible merge conflict that got resolved incorrectly.
40	
41	### 🟢 Acceptable patterns
42	
43	- Add nullable column → backfill in a separate release → set NOT NULL → drop default. Three migrations, three releases.
44	- Adding a new table.
45	- Adding a new index using `postgresql_concurrently=True` in its own migration.
46	- Adding constraints in `NOT VALID` mode, then `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` in a later migration.
47	
48	## How to report
49	
50	Produce a structured report:
51	
52	1. **🔴 Hard violations** — file:line, operation, why it's unsafe, suggested two-step split.
53	2. **🟡 Concerns** — file:line, operation, suggested change.
54	3. **Rollback check** — for each migration, confirm `downgrade()` is implemented and inverts `upgrade()`.
55	4. **Two-step plan** (if a violation requires it) — outline the staged rollout the user should adopt.
56	5. **✅ Verdict** — one of:
57	   - `Pass — migration is backward-compatible.`
58	   - `Conditional — N concerns. Discuss with whoever runs the deploy.`
59	   - `Block — N hard violations. Must split into two-step rollout before merge.`
60	
61	## Operational note
62	
63	This agent reads migration files and reports — it does NOT modify them. The author splits the migration based on the report. Two-step migrations land as two separate PRs (one per step) per working-agreement #1.
64	
65	## Source documents (your authority)
66	
67	- [CLAUDE.md §6 Database — backward-compatible migrations only](../../CLAUDE.md)
68	- [.github/pull_request_template.md — Schema migration checklist](../../.github/pull_request_template.md)
69

+---
+name: docs-consistency-guard
+description: Documentation agent that audits docs for staleness and inconsistency AND generates/updates documentation on request. Use proactively when reviewing any PR that touches CLAUDE.md, docs/adr/, CONTRIBUTING.md, or docs/architecture.svg. Also invoke when the user asks "is the documentation up to date?", "update the milestone", "scaffold the ADR for X", "add this to the ADR index", "add a TODO item", "scaffold a README for X", or "create a doc stub for Y."
+tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit
+model: sonnet
+---
+
+You are the documentation agent for the DataQ project. You have two modes:
+
+1. **Audit mode** — read-only review of docs for consistency, broken links, and staleness. Invoked automatically on doc-touching PRs or on request.
+2. **Generate/update mode** — write or update documentation: scaffold new ADR files, update CLAUDE.md §13 milestone text, add rows to the ADR index, fill in CONTRIBUTING.md gaps. Invoked explicitly by the user ("scaffold the ADR for X", "update the milestone to Week 2", etc.).
+
+Never modify code files. Your writes are limited to:
+- `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` — new or existing ADR files
+- `docs/adr/README.md` — ADR index
+- `CLAUDE.md` — milestone section (§13) only; do not rewrite other sections
+- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — append or patch only; do not restructure
+- `.claude/agents/*.md`, `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` — if explicitly asked to update an agent or skill doc
+
+---
+
+## Audit mode — what you check
+
+Use `gh pr diff <N>` if a PR number is provided. Otherwise read the files directly.
+
+### 🔴 Hard violations (must fix before merge)
+
+1. **CLAUDE.md §6 branch-protection claim vs actual GitHub ruleset.** Run:
+   ```bash
+   gh api repos/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/branches/main/protection 2>/dev/null | jq '{required_reviews: .required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count, enforce_admins: .enforce_admins.enabled, allow_force_pushes: .allow_force_pushes.enabled}'
+   ```
+   Flag any mismatch (e.g., CLAUDE.md says "≥1 review" but ruleset has 0 required approving reviews).
+
+2. **ADR index out of sync.** Every file matching `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` must have a corresponding row in `docs/adr/README.md`. Check both directions:
+   - ADR file exists but not in index → missing index entry.
+   - Index entry references a file that doesn't exist → dangling reference.
+
+3. **CLAUDE.md forward references resolve.** Every relative link in CLAUDE.md (e.g., `[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)`, `[docs/adr/](docs/adr/)`, `[docs/architecture.svg](docs/architecture.svg)`) must point to a file or directory that exists. Use `Glob` or `Bash ls` to verify.
+
+4. **ADR `Superseded by` / `Supersedes` cross-links are bidirectional.** If ADR 0007 says `Supersedes: ADR-0003`, then ADR 0003 must say `Superseded by: ADR-0007`. One-sided links are broken.
+
+5. **Skill and agent files referenced in CLAUDE.md or CONTRIBUTING.md exist.** If the docs mention `.claude/skills/adr-create` or `.claude/agents/orchestration-abstraction-guard`, those paths must be present on disk.
+
+### 🟡 Yellow flags (call out, don't necessarily block)
+
+1. **CLAUDE.md §13 "current milestone" is stale.** If the documented "Current week" and "Current milestone target" describes a week that appears already completed (based on merged PRs or open issues), flag it with a suggested update.
+
+2. **"Pending" ADRs in `docs/adr/README.md` whose target week has passed.** Today's date is available via `date +%Y-%m-%d`. If an ADR listed under "Pending for Week N" still has no file and the week is past, flag it as overdue.
+
+3. **`context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` preamble missing or stale.** The preamble should note where the roadmap has been superseded by ADR decisions (ADF is orchestration not a datasource; Airflow was added post-roadmap; DQX deferred to v1.1). If the roadmap is modified without updating the preamble, flag it.
+
+4. **ADR status inconsistency.** If CLAUDE.md §9 says an ADR status is "Locked W1" but `docs/adr/README.md` says "Pending", flag the disagreement.
+
+5. **Dead working-agreement references.** CLAUDE.md and agent/skill files reference specific working-agreement numbers (e.g., "working-agreement #3", "working-agreement #24"). If `CONTRIBUTING.md` doesn't contain those numbered rules, flag the mismatch.
+
+6. **Section numbering drift in CLAUDE.md.** Agent and skill files hard-link to CLAUDE.md sections (e.g., `CLAUDE.md §11`). If sections are renumbered, those external links go stale.
+
+### 🟢 Acceptable patterns
+
+- ADR in "Proposed" status with no file yet — expected before the target week.
+- Forward ADR numbers reserved in CLAUDE.md §9 as "TBD WN" — placeholders, not dangling refs.
+- Preamble notes in `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` listing superseding decisions.
+- CLAUDE.md §13 correctly describing current in-progress work.
+
+---
+
+## Generate/update mode — what you can write
+
+### Scaffold a new ADR
+
+Follow the same steps as the `/adr-create` skill:
+
+1. Find the highest `NNNN` in `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md`, increment by 1, zero-pad to 4 digits.
+2. Derive a kebab-case slug from the user's topic (drop articles, lowercase).
+3. Create `docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md` using the standard template (see below).
+4. Add a row to `docs/adr/README.md` index table.
+5. Do **not** commit — stage only. Print next steps.
+
+**ADR template:**
+
+```markdown
+# ADR NNNN — <Human-readable title>
+
+- **Status:** Accepted
+- **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
+- **Deciders:** @<github-handle>
+- **Consulted:** <optional>
+- **Supersedes:** <optional>
+- **Superseded by:** <optional>
+
+## Context
+
+<What problem are we deciding about? 1–3 paragraphs.>
+
+## Decision
+
+**<One-sentence statement of the decision, in bold.>**
+
+<Details: how it works, what's in scope, what's out of scope.>
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive**
+- <bullet>
+
+**Negative**
+- <bullet>
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- **<Alternative 1>** — rejected. <Why.>
+
+## Related
+
+- <Link to related ADRs, issues, PRs, or code paths.>
+```
+
+Get today's date via `date +%Y-%m-%d`. Get GitHub handle via `gh api /user --jq .login` (prepend `@`). Do not use `git config user.name` — it returns a display name, not an `@mention`.
+
+### Update CLAUDE.md §13 milestone
+
+When the user says "update the milestone to Week N" or "mark PR 0 complete":
+- Read the current §13 block in CLAUDE.md.
+- Edit only the "Current week:", "Current milestone target:", and "Next milestone:" lines.
+- Do not touch any other section.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Add a row to the ADR index
+
+When a new ADR file exists but is missing from `docs/adr/README.md`:
+- Read the current index table.
+- Append a row in the same format as existing rows: `| [NNNN](NNNN-slug.md) | Title | Status | Week |`
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Patch a CONTRIBUTING.md section
+
+When asked to add or update a working agreement:
+- Read the relevant section.
+- Append or edit the numbered rule.
+- Preserve existing numbering — do not renumber unless asked.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Maintain the project TODO list (`docs/TODO.md`)
+
+A single `docs/TODO.md` tracks deferred work items that are not yet GitHub issues — exploratory ideas, known gaps, future-week tasks, and "decide before Week N" reminders.
+
+**Structure of `docs/TODO.md`:**
+
+```markdown
+# DataQ — Project TODO
+
+> Items here are tracked informally. When an item becomes concrete enough to act on,
+> convert it to a GitHub issue via `/gh-issue-from-finding` and remove it from this list.
+
+## Week N — <milestone name>
+
+- [ ] <item> — <short context or owner>
+
+## Backlog (no target week)
+
+- [ ] <item>
+
+## Decided / done (archive — do not delete, just tick)
+
+- [x] <item>
+```
+
+When asked to add, tick, or remove a TODO item:
+- If `docs/TODO.md` doesn't exist, create it with the structure above.
+- Add new items under the correct week section (or "Backlog" if no week is specified).
+- Tick items when the user says they're done; move ticked items to the "Decided / done" section.
+- When an item is promoted to a GitHub issue, note the issue number inline: `→ #N` and tick it.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Scaffold or update a README
+
+When asked to create or update a README for a directory (e.g., `backend/README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `scripts/README.md`):
+
+**Structure for a directory README:**
+
+```markdown
+# <Directory name>
+
+> One-line purpose of this directory.
+
+## What lives here
+
+| File / folder | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| `<path>` | <description> |
+
+## How to use
+
+<Minimal quickstart — one or two commands or steps. Link to CONTRIBUTING.md for the full setup.>
+
+## Related
+
+- <Links to relevant ADRs, CLAUDE.md sections, or other READMEs.>
+```
+
+Rules:
+- Do not duplicate information already in `CLAUDE.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` — link to them instead.
+- Keep it short: the goal is orientation, not a manual.
+- If the directory doesn't exist yet, say so and ask the user to confirm before creating the README.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Scaffold future documentation stubs
+
+When a new subsystem is planned but not yet built (e.g., `backend/app/mcp/`, `backend/app/orchestration/`), the user may ask to pre-create a doc stub so the location and intent are clear from day one:
+

+- Mark it clearly at the top: `> **Stub — to be filled in Week N.**`
+- Include the section headings the document will eventually need, left empty.
+- Add it to `docs/TODO.md` as a tracked item.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+---
+
+## How to report (audit mode)
+
+1. **🔴 Hard violations** — file:line, what the doc says, what reality is, required fix.
+2. **🟡 Concerns** — file:line, the inconsistency, suggested update.
+3. **Cross-reference summary** — ADR count in index vs files on disk; CLAUDE.md links checked vs broken.
+4. **✅ Verdict** — one of:

## PR #21 — `chore: add docs-consistency-guard subagent`

### Overview

Adds a dual-mode documentation agent that audits docs for consistency/staleness and can generate/update documentation on request. Single file: `.claude/agents/docs-consistency-guard.md` (238 lines added).

---

### Code quality & correctness

**Frontmatter / tooling**
- `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit` — correct. `Write` is needed for new files (`docs/TODO.md`, README stubs, ADR scaffolds). `Edit` is needed for patching existing files. Both are justified.
- `model: sonnet` — consistent with the other two agents.

**ADR scaffold logic**
- The ADR template here duplicates the template in `.claude/skills/adr-create/SKILL.md`. If the template ever evolves, they'll drift. Consider one of:
  - Add a note like `Use the template from .claude/skills/adr-create/SKILL.md` to keep a single source of truth.

Surfaced by `/review` on PR #3. **Must land before Week 7 public deployment.**

## Problem

`bug.md` currently bundles security defects under the `critical` severity:
```
- [ ] critical — production down / data loss / security
```

A public GitHub issue for an exploitable vulnerability discloses it before a fix is ready. Once we deploy publicly in Week 7, reporters need a private channel.

## Proposed

1. Split "security" out of the `critical` severity in `bug.md`.
2. Add `.github/SECURITY.md` with a `Reporting a Vulnerability` section pointing to GitHub Security Advisories: https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new
3. (Optional) Add an `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/security.md` that displays a redirect notice and links to the Security Advisories URL.
4. Enable private vulnerability reporting in repo settings (Settings → Security → Private vulnerability reporting).
5. Create a `security` GitHub label for ongoing tracking.

## Why this is a Week 7 blocker
Once the API and `/mcp` endpoint are publicly reachable, external security researchers may find issues. A misconfigured disclosure path either drives them to public-issue disclosure (worst case) or loses the report entirely.

## Proposed

- Preserve the legend grouping (Datasources green, Integrations orange) — it visually reinforces ADR 0004.

## Why this is a Week 2 blocker
Week 2 builds the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with both ADF and Airflow implementations. The diagram is the first thing new contributors look at — if it shows only ADF, they'll write ADF-specific code instead of going through the abstraction.

7	## 1. Project summary
8	
9	**DataQ** is the v1 evolution of SnowQ — a single-tenant data quality monitoring platform built around Great Expectations (GX Core). It runs DQ checks across **4 datasources** and integrates with **2 orchestration providers**.
10	
11	| Layer | Components |
12	|---|---|
13	| **Datasources (you can write checks against)** | Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT), ADLS Gen2, AWS S3, Unity Catalog (Databricks) |
14	| **Orchestration providers (monitor + trigger only — NOT datasources)** | Azure Data Factory (ADF), Apache Airflow |
15	| **Backend** | FastAPI + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL + Alembic |
16	| **Frontend** | React + Vite + Ant Design + Monaco editor |
17	| **Auth / secrets** | Azure AD (MSAL) + Azure Key Vault |
18	| **Deploy** | Azure Container Apps + Azure Static Web App |
19	| **Observability** | Azure Application Insights + structlog |
20	| **AI integration** | FastMCP (8 curated tools mounted at `/mcp`) — Claude Desktop / Claude.ai / Copilot / Cursor |
21	
22	Timeline: **8 weeks** to v1. Scope: single tenant, suite-level access sharing, Azure-hosted.

32	                                                    │  │
33	AI clients ──MCP/HTTP──► FastAPI /mcp endpoint      │  └──► Celery worker ──► GX execution ──► Snowflake / ADLS / S3 / UC
34	                                                    │
35	                                                    ├──► Redis (task queue)
36	                                                    ├──► Key Vault (secrets)

88	---
89	
90	## 4. Datasources vs orchestration — critical distinction
91	
92	**Datasources** are stores you write DQ checks against:
93	- Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT)
94	- ADLS Gen2 (flat files)
95	- AWS S3 (flat files)
96	- Unity Catalog / Databricks
97	
98	**Orchestration providers** are NOT datasources. They are workflow engines whose pipelines/DAGs we observe and react to. Their *only* three responsibilities in DataQ:
99	
100	1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table (separate from `runs` / `results`).
101	2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific event channels (webhook for both).
102	3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings` (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `suite_id`, `env`). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs.
103	
104	Both providers implement a single `OrchestrationProvider` interface — ADF is the reference implementation, Airflow is the second. **Never hardcode ADF-only logic; always go through the abstraction.**
105	
106	| Provider | Event channel | Auth | Polling fallback |
107	|---|---|---|---|
108	| ADF | Azure Monitor alert → webhook | Shared secret header (Azure Monitor's only mode) | ADF REST API, 10 min |
109	| Airflow | DAG `on_*_callback` → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns`, 10 min |
110	
111	Airflow callbacks require the user to add a snippet to their DAGs (we can't mutate them). Polling is the documented fallback.
112	
113	**Anti-pattern (do not do this):** treating ADF/Airflow as a 5th/6th datasource in the connection editor, check editor, or suite model.
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 5. Framework choice — GX-only for v1
118	
119	- **v1:** Great Expectations (GX Core) is the sole DQ framework across all 4 datasources. Unifies result schema, suite/check model, MCP tools, and the check editor.
120	- **v1.1:** Databricks Labs **DQX** will be added for DLT / streaming use cases (GX is batch-only and runs poorly on streaming). DQX will implement the same `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` interface introduced in Week 3 — UI exposes `engine: gx | dqx` toggle on UC suites.
121	- **Implication for Week 3:** keep the UC adapter thin behind `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` so v1.1 DQX swap-in doesn't ripple into the suite/check/result layer.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## 6. Working agreements (rules above feature work)
126	
127	Full list (30 rules across 8 categories) lives in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Highlights:
128	
129	### Commit & change discipline
130	- **One functionality per commit** (where possible).
131	- **Manually test each committed change before starting the next functionality** (required until unit tests land in Week 8).
132	- **Defects → GitHub issue, never silent fixes.** Use `gh issue create`. The fixing PR must include `Fixes #N`.
133	- **From Week 8 onward, every new functionality ships with tests.**
134	
135	### Git workflow
136	- **Trunk-based** with short-lived feature branches off `main`. No long-lived `develop`.
137	- Branch names: `feature/<desc>`, `fix/issue-<N>-<desc>`, `chore/<desc>`, `docs/<desc>`.
138	- `main` is protected: PR + ≥1 review + passing CI + no force-push.
139	- **Squash-merge only into `main`.**
140	- **Conventional commits** (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`).
141	
142	### CI/CD quality gates (block merge)
143	- Ruff (lint), Black `--check` (format), mypy (types), pytest (from W8), frontend lint/format/test.
144	- `gitleaks` secret scanning (pre-commit + CI).
145	- Bandit (Python SAST) + CodeQL.
146	- Dependabot for npm + pip + github-actions.
147	
148	### Tooling (locked in Week 1, do not drift)
149	- **Python:** conda env (`conda create -n dataq python=3.11`) — *not* venv, *not* poetry.
150	- **Black** formatter (CI-enforced).
151	- **Ruff** lint, **mypy** types, **structlog** logging, **Pydantic Settings** config (12-factor).
152	- **Frontend:** Prettier + ESLint.
153	
154	### Observability
155	- **Structured logging from Week 1.** structlog, JSON, `request_id` correlation propagated FastAPI → Celery → GX.
156	- **PII redaction at logger level** (failed-check sample rows may contain sensitive data).
157	- **App Insights exception tracking wired Week 1**, not Week 7.
158	
159	### Database
160	- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** No `DROP COLUMN` + code change in same PR. Two-step deploys from W5 onward.
161	- Migration PR checklist: rollback plan + "tested up + down locally."
162	
163	### Documentation
164	- **ADRs in `docs/adr/`** — one short markdown per significant decision.
165	- `scripts/setup.sh` — one command from clone to working dev env.
166	
167	### Security cadence
168	- End-of-week quick scan from Week 2: vuln alerts, secret scan, OWASP spot check, Key Vault audit.
169	- Hard security review gate before Week 7 deploy.
170	
171	---

186	cd DataQ
187	./scripts/setup.sh           # creates conda env, installs pre-commit, pulls images, runs migrations, seeds dev data
188	conda activate dataq
189	docker-compose up            # Postgres + Redis + FastAPI + React + Celery worker

192	# Browse Swagger: http://localhost:8000/docs

200	|---|---|---|
201	| Trunk-based branching, squash-merge into `main` | [0001](docs/adr/0001-trunk-based-branching.md) | Locked W1 |
202	| Conventional commits | [0002](docs/adr/0002-conventional-commits.md) | Locked W1 |
203	| GX-only for v1; DQX deferred to v1.1 | [0003](docs/adr/0003-gx-only-for-v1.md) | Locked W1 |
204	| Orchestration abstraction (ADF + Airflow share `OrchestrationProvider`) | [0004](docs/adr/0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) | Locked W1 |
205	| Severity tier weights (warn/fail/critical → health score) | `0005` (TBD W3) | Pending stakeholder agreement before W3 starts |
206	| ADF webhook auth (shared secret) + Key Vault rotation | `0006` (TBD W2) | Pending W2 |
207	| Airflow callback model (HMAC-signed) + polling fallback | `0007` (TBD W2) | Pending W2 |
208	| MCP mounted at `/mcp` with Azure AD auth | `0008` (TBD W7) | Pending W7 |
209	| Repo layout: flat monorepo (`backend/` + `frontend/`) | `0009` (TBD W1) | Locked W1 |

212	
213	## 10. Critical pointers (easy to get wrong)
214	
215	- **`pipeline_runs` ≠ `runs`.** Orchestrator pipeline executions live in `pipeline_runs`; DQ suite executions live in `runs`. They link via `triggered_by: '<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>'`.
216	- **`trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic.** Composite key (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) → `suite_id`. Don't add an ADF-specific bindings table.
217	- **PII redaction at the logger level**, not at every call site. The redactor sits in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.
218	- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** Code that depends on a new column ships in a separate PR *after* the migration is deployed.
219	- **Secret scanning in pre-commit AND CI.** Don't rely on one alone.
220	- **Azure Monitor alert setup (Week 7) needs the deployed public API URL.** Deployment must come first; coordinate Container Apps ingress with infra/security before Week 7 to avoid a deployment-day surprise.
221	- **MCP tool descriptions are LLM-facing, not REST-API-facing.** Write them for natural-language selection; test against the 4 canonical NL queries in the roadmap.
222	
223	---
224	
225	## 11. What NOT to do
226	
227	- ❌ Don't add ADF or Airflow as a queryable datasource in the connection editor / check editor / suite model.
228	- ❌ Don't bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with provider-specific branching in service code.
229	- ❌ Don't `git commit --no-verify` past hooks. If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue.
230	- ❌ Don't commit `.env` files. Use `.env.example` as the template.
231	- ❌ Don't drop columns in the same PR as the code change that stops using them. Two-step it.
232	- ❌ Don't fix bugs silently. Raise a GitHub issue, then PR with `Fixes #N`.
233	- ❌ Don't batch unrelated changes into one commit. One functionality per commit.
234	- ❌ Don't track GX Core at "latest." Pin the version in `environment.yml` — GX v1 API has drifted across point releases.
235	- ❌ Don't use venv or poetry for backend dev. Conda only.
236	- ❌ Don't write the MCP layer before Week 7. The service layer must stabilise first.

1	# Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
2	
3	Each ADR captures a single significant architecture decision: the context, the decision, the consequences, and the alternatives considered. New ADRs are append-only — supersede an old decision by adding a new ADR and marking the old one's status as `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.
4	
5	## Format
6	
7	- File name: `NNNN-short-kebab-slug.md` (zero-padded 4-digit sequence)
8	- Frontmatter fields: Status, Date, Deciders
9	- Sections: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, Related (optional)
10	- Keep each ADR short — 1–2 pages. If it grows past that, the decision is probably two decisions.

+# Security Policy
+
+## Reporting a Vulnerability
+
+**Do not open a public GitHub issue for security vulnerabilities.** Public disclosure before a fix is ready puts all users at risk.
+
+Report vulnerabilities privately via **[GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new)**.
+
+You will receive a response within **5 business days** acknowledging the report. We aim to release a fix within **30 days** for critical issues and **90 days** for lower-severity issues, depending on complexity.
+
+## What to include
+
+- A clear description of the vulnerability and the affected component
+- Steps to reproduce (or a proof-of-concept)
+- Potential impact and severity assessment
+- Any suggested mitigations
+
+## Scope
+
+Components in scope:
+- FastAPI backend (`/api/v1/*`, `/mcp`)
+- Azure AD authentication flow (MSAL token validation)
+- Celery worker + GX execution path
+- Key Vault secret access patterns
+
+Out of scope:
+- Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies — report those upstream; we track them via Dependabot
+- Issues requiring physical access to Azure infrastructure
+
+## Supported versions
+
+Only the latest commit on `main` is supported. There are no versioned releases in the v1 development phase.

Here are the reviews for all three PRs, then my take on the diagram format.

---

### PR #22 — CLAUDE.md accuracy

**Pass.** All 7 items from issue #7 addressed correctly. No concerns.

---

### PR #23 — SECURITY.md

**Conditional — 1 fix needed.**

The relative path `../../SECURITY.md` in both template files is wrong. The file is at `.github/SECURITY.md`; templates are one level up in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, so the correct path is `../SECURITY.md`.

---

### PR #24 — Architecture SVG

**Pass with note.** The rename is correct and text fits within the 143px box. But this PR is a perfect illustration of the SVG maintainability problem — adding one provider required manually recalculating mask bounding box coordinates. Which brings me to your question:

---

### Diagram format recommendation: **Mermaid**

**Recommendation: Mermaid, embedded in `docs/architecture.md`.** Here's the comparison:

| | Mermaid | draw.io | ASCII |
|---|---|---|---|
| Renders on GitHub | ✅ natively in `.md` | ❌ need export | ✅ anywhere |
| Git-diff readable | ✅ plain text | ❌ XML blob | ✅ |
| AI can update it | ✅ trivially | ❌ | ⚠️ tedious |
| Visual quality | Good | Best | Basic |
| Maintains layout as diagram grows | ⚠️ auto-layout | ✅ manual | ❌ breaks |

draw.io produces the best visuals but is effectively unmaintainable through code — every edit requires the GUI, and the XML diff is unreadable. ASCII works but falls apart once the diagram has more than ~10 components. Mermaid hits the sweet spot: GitHub renders it inline, it's plain text I can update in every PR, and it handles our 4-layer architecture cleanly.

The tradeoff: Mermaid's auto-layout engine won't reproduce the exact visual grouping of the current SVG (the dashed "DataQ platform" bounding box is hard to do in Mermaid). We'd trade pixel-perfect layout for something that actually stays up to date.

Let me fix the broken path in PR #23 first, then I can convert the diagram if you want to go with Mermaid.

> AGENT

Beyond the three already mentioned, a few more worth knowing:

**D2** — Modern text-based language with the cleanest syntax of the bunch. Supports labeled groups/subgraphs (so the "DataQ platform" bounding box is easy). Doesn't render on GitHub natively, but you commit the `.d2` source as the maintainable file and a rendered `.svg` as the output artifact. Update the `.d2`, re-run `d2 architecture.d2 docs/architecture.svg`, commit both. The diff you read is the `.d2`; the SVG is just a build output.

**PlantUML** — Mature, widely used, good C4 model support. Ugly default styling unless you apply a theme. Same deal as D2 — needs a renderer; GitHub Actions can auto-render on push. More verbose than D2.

**Structurizr DSL** — Purpose-built for C4 architecture diagrams (System Context → Container → Component levels). Excellent for expressing "what talks to what and why" rather than just boxes and arrows. Overkill for a single-layer diagram but scales well as the architecture grows. Needs external tooling.

**Short answer:** If GitHub-native rendering without any build step matters → **Mermaid only**. If you're fine with a "source + rendered output" workflow → **D2** is the best of the non-Mermaid options (cleaner syntax, better-looking output, easier grouping). Everything else adds tooling complexity without a clear payoff for a project this size.

Which constraint matters more to you — zero extra tooling, or best visual output?
