{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/CONTRIBUTING.md",
  "content": "# Contributing to DataQ\n\n> Working agreements for everyone (human and AI) writing code in this repo. These rules are locked in Week 1 and override any \"speed > quality\" temptation. If a week's exit gate conflicts with them, **the rules win**.\n\n---\n\n## A. Commit & change discipline\n\n1. **One functionality per commit** (where possible). Each commit must be independently reviewable; do not bundle two unrelated changes.\n2. **Manually test each committed change before starting the next functionality.** Required until the unit-test suite reaches 80% coverage (Week 8 gate). \"Tested\" means: the affected code path was exercised locally, not just that it compiled.\n3. **Defects → GitHub issue first, never silent fixes.** Use `gh issue create --title \"fix: <desc>\"`. The PR that fixes it must include `Fixes #N` in the title or body.\n4. **From Week 8 onward, every new functionality ships with unit tests.** Tests live next to the code they cover (`backend/tests/`, `frontend/tests/`).\n5. **Definition of Done (DoD)** per task:\n   - Code merged to `main`\n   - Manually tested locally\n   - (From Week 8) unit tests written and passing\n   - Docs / ADR updated if the change is user-facing or architectural\n   - Linked GitHub issue closed if one exists\n\n---\n\n## B. Git workflow\n\n6. **Trunk-based development** — branch off `main`, PR back to `main`. No long-lived `develop` or `release` branches.\n7. **Branch naming:**\n   - `feature/<short-desc>` — new functionality\n   - `fix/issue-<N>-<short-desc>` — bug fix tied to a GitHub issue\n   - `chore/<short-desc>` — tooling, deps, config, non-functional\n   - `docs/<short-desc>` — documentation only\n8. **`main` branch protection:** PR required + passing CI + no force-push. Approving-review count is 0 during solo-dev phase; re-enable (≥1) before onboarding a second contributor.\n9. **Squash-merge only into `main`.** Keeps history linear and matches rule #1. Feature branch commit history is squashed into a single commit on merge.\n10. **Conventional commits** for PR titles and the squash-merge commit message:\n    - `feat:` — new user-facing functionality\n    - `fix:` — bug fix\n    - `chore:` — tooling, config, deps (no production behaviour change)\n    - `docs:` — documentation only\n    - `test:` — tests only\n    - `refactor:` — code restructure with no behaviour change\n    - `ci:` — CI/CD workflow changes\n    - Format: `<type>(<optional scope>): <short imperative description>`\n    - Examples: `feat(api): add suite dry-run endpoint`, `fix(celery): handle graceful shutdown on SIGTERM`\n11. **PR template** checklist (`.github/pull_request_template.md`): manual test ✓, linked issue, security implications, schema migration.\n12. **`CODEOWNERS`** (`.github/CODEOWNERS`) auto-routes reviews per area.\n\n---\n\n## C. CI/CD quality gates\n\nAll checks run on every PR and must pass before merge.\n\n13. **Python:** Ruff (lint) → Black `--check` (format) → mypy (types) → Bandit (SAST) → pytest (from Week 8).\n14. **Frontend:** ESLint → Prettier `--check` → Vitest (from Week 8).\n15. **Secret scanning:** gitleaks in pre-commit hook AND in CI. A secret detected in CI blocks merge.\n16. **SAST:** Bandit (Python) + CodeQL (GitHub Actions) on every PR.\n17. **Dependency vulnerability scanning:** Dependabot alerts + auto-PRs for security updates. Deps are pinned in `environment.yml` and locked with `conda-lock`.\n\n---\n\n## D. Coding structure & tooling\n\nThese are locked on Day 1 of Week 1. Do not drift.\n\n18. **Python runtime:** `conda` only (`conda create -n dataq python=3.11`). Not venv, not poetry, not pyenv.\n19. **Python formatter:** Black. Config in `pyproject.toml`. CI rejects unformatted code.\n20. **Python linter:** Ruff. Replaces flake8 + isort + pyupgrade. Config in `pyproject.toml`.\n21. **Python type checker:** mypy (strict mode). Config in `pyproject.toml`.\n22. **Frontend package manager:** pnpm. Not npm, not yarn.\n23. **Frontend formatter:** Prettier. Config in `frontend/.prettierrc`.\n24. **Frontend linter:** ESLint with TypeScript rules. Config in `frontend/.eslintrc.cjs`.\n25. **Config / 12-factor:** All environment-specific config via env vars. Backend uses Pydantic Settings (`backend/app/core/config.py`). Frontend uses Vite env vars (`VITE_*`). No env-specific code branches.\n\n---\n\n## E. Observability & error handling\n\n26. **Structured logging from Week 1.** `structlog` with JSON output. Every log entry carries a `request_id` correlation ID propagated FastAPI → Celery → GX. Configuration in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.\n27. **PII redaction at the logger level** — not at every call site. Failed-check sample rows can contain sensitive data. The redactor in `backend/app/core/logging.py` strips known PII fields centrally.\n28. **Consistent error shape** across all API responses. Definition in `backend/app/core/errors.py`:\n    ```json\n    { \"error\": { \"code\": \"SNAKE_CASE_CODE\", \"message\": \"Human-readable string\", \"detail\": {} } }\n    ```\n29. **App Insights exception tracking wired from Week 1**, not Week 7. Middleware in `backend/app/main.py` captures all unhandled exceptions from the first commit.\n\n---\n\n## F. Database & migrations\n\n30. **Backward-compatible migrations only.** No `DROP COLUMN` + code change in the same PR. Two-step deploys from Week 5 onward:\n    1. PR A: migration adds/renames column; old code still works.\n    2. PR B (later): code change that depends on the new schema.\n31. **Migration PR checklist:** rollback plan documented + \"tested `alembic upgrade head` and `alembic downgrade -1` locally\" ticked before requesting review.\n\n---\n\n## G. Documentation & decision history\n\n32. **ADRs in `docs/adr/`** for every significant architecture decision. Use the `/adr-create` skill or follow the template in `docs/adr/README.md`. One short markdown per decision; keep it to 1–2 pages.\n33. **Architecture diagram in `docs/architecture.md`** (Mermaid). When a new component, datasource, or integration is added, update the diagram in the same PR as the code.\n34. **Local setup script** `scripts/setup.sh` — one command from a fresh clone to a working dev environment (conda env + pre-commit install + docker-compose up + `alembic upgrade head` + seed data).\n\n---\n\n## H. Security review cadence\n\n35. **End-of-week quick scan from Week 2 onward:** review Dependabot vuln alerts, secret scan results, OWASP top-10 spot check on any new endpoints, Key Vault access audit.\n36. **Hard security review gate before Week 7 deploy:** full pass on all of the above plus public-endpoint exposure review (especially `/api/v1/orchestration/events/*` and `/mcp`).\n37. **Security vulnerabilities are not public GitHub issues.** Report via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new). See [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Module boundaries & naming conventions\n\n### Backend (`backend/`)\n\n| Layer | Package | Responsibility |\n|---|---|---|\n| API | `backend/app/api/v1/` | FastAPI routers only — no business logic |\n| Services | `backend/app/services/` | Business logic, orchestration between layers |\n| Orchestration | `backend/app/orchestration/` | `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction + ADF/Airflow impls |\n| Datasources | `backend/app/datasources/` | GX adapter per datasource type |\n| DB | `backend/app/db/` | SQLAlchemy models + session management |\n| Core | `backend/app/core/` | Config, logging, errors — imported by all layers |\n| MCP | `backend/app/mcp/` | FastMCP tools (Week 7 only) |\n\n**Naming:**\n- Files: `snake_case.py`\n- Classes: `PascalCase`\n- Functions / variables: `snake_case`\n- Constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`\n- Async functions: always `async def` for anything that touches DB, Redis, or external HTTP\n\n**Import order** (enforced by Ruff / isort):\n1. Standard library\n2. Third-party (`fastapi`, `sqlalchemy`, `celery`, …)\n3. First-party (`backend.app.*`)\n\n### Frontend (`frontend/`)\n\n| Layer | Path | Responsibility |\n|---|---|---|\n| Pages | `src/pages/` | Route-level components |\n| Components | `src/components/` | Reusable UI components |\n| API client | `src/api/` | Generated OpenAPI client (Week 4+) |\n| Hooks | `src/hooks/` | Custom React hooks |\n| Store | `src/store/` | Global state (if needed) |\n\n**Naming:**\n- Component files: `PascalCase.tsx`\n- Hook files: `useXxx.ts`\n- Util files: `camelCase.ts`\n\n---\n\n## Local development\n\n```bash\n# One-time setup from a fresh clone (requires conda installed):\n./scripts/setup.sh\n\n# Day-to-day:\nconda activate dataq\ndocker-compose up           # starts Postgres, Redis, FastAPI, React dev server, Celery worker\n\n# Backend only:\ncd backend && uvicorn app.main:app --reload\n\n# Frontend only:\ncd frontend && pnpm dev\n\n# Run pre-commit on all files:\npre-commit run --all-files\n\n# Run backend tests (Week 8+):\ncd backend && pytest\n\n# Run frontend tests (Week 8+):\ncd frontend && pnpm test\n```\n\n> Commands above assume Week 1 scaffolding (`environment.yml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/setup.sh`) is committed.\n"
}

full scan via Bandit)\n    \"RUF\", # ruff-specific rules\n]\nignore = [\n    \"S101\",  # assert statements are fine in tests\n    \"S104\",  # binding to 0.0.0.0 is intentional in Docker\n    \"B008\",  # FastAPI Depends() in function args is idiomatic\n]\n\n[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]\n\"backend/tests/**\" = [\"S\", \"N802\"]  # relax security + naming in tests\n\"backend/alembic/**\" = [\"N999\"]     # migration files use non-PEP8 names\n\n[tool.ruff.lint.isort]\nknown-first-party = [\"app\"]\n\n# ── mypy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n[tool.mypy]\npython_version = \"3.11\"\nstrict = true\nwarn_return_any = true\nwarn_unused_configs = true\nignore_missing_imports = false\nplugins = [\"sqlalchemy.ext.mypy.plugin\", \"pydantic.mypy\"]\n\n[[tool.mypy.overrides]]\nmodule = [\n    \"great_expectations.*\",\n    \"celery.*\",\n    \"opencensus.*\",\n    \"snowflake.*\",\n    \"databricks.*\",\n    \"azure.storage.*\",\n]\nignore_missing_imports = true\n\n# ── pytest ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\nasyncio_mode = \"auto\"\ntestpaths = [\"backend/tests\"]\naddopts = \"--cov=backend/app --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=0\"\n# cov-fail-under raised to 80 in Week 8\n\n# ── Bandit ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n[tool.bandit]\ntargets = [\"backend/app\"]\nexclude_dirs = [\"backend/tests\", \"backend/alembic\"]\nskips = [\"B101\"]  # assert is fine in non-production code\n"

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# One-command dev environment setup from a fresh clone.\n# Usage: ./scripts/setup.sh\n# Requires: conda (miniconda/miniforge), docker, pnpm, git\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nCYAN='\\033[0;36m'; GREEN='\\033[0;32m'; RED='\\033[0;31m'; NC='\\033[0m'\nstep() { echo -e \"${CYAN}▶ $1${NC}\"; }\nok()   { echo -e \"${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}\"; }\ndie()  { echo -e \"${RED}✗ $1${NC}\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\n# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nstep \"Checking prerequisites\"\ncommand -v conda  >/dev/null || die \"conda not found — install miniconda or miniforge first\"\ncommand -v docker >/dev/null || die \"docker not found\"\ncommand -v pnpm   >/dev/null || die \"pnpm not found — run: npm install -g pnpm\"\ncommand -v git    >/dev/null || die \"git not found\"\nok \"Prerequisites OK\"\n\n# ── Conda environment ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nstep \"Creating / updating conda environment 'dataq'\"\nif conda env list | grep -q \"^dataq \"; then\n  conda env update -n dataq -f environment.yml --prune\n  ok \"Conda env updated\"\nelse\n  conda env create -f environment.yml\n  ok \"Conda env created\"\nfi\n\n# ── Pre-commit hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nstep \"Installing pre-commit hooks\"\nconda run -n dataq pre-commit install --install-hooks\nok \"Pre-commit hooks installed\"\n\n# ── Frontend dependencies ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nstep \"Installing frontend dependencies (pnpm)\"\n(cd frontend && pnpm install)\nok \"Frontend dependencies installed\"\n\n# ── Docker services ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nstep \"Starting Docker services (Postgres, Redis)\"\ndocker compose up -d postgres redis\nok \"Docker services started\"\n\n# ── Database migrations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nstep \"Waiting for Postgres to be ready\"\nfor i in $(seq 1 30); do\n  if docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U dataq >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    ok \"Postgres ready\"\n    break\n  fi\n  [ \"$i\" -eq 30 ] && die \"Postgres did not become ready in time\"\n  sleep 1\ndone\n\nstep \"Running Alembic migrations\"\nconda run -n dataq sh -c \"cd backend && alembic upgrade head\"\nok \"Migrations applied\"\n\n# ── Seed data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nstep \"Seeding dev data\"\nif [ -f backend/scripts/seed_dev.py ]; then\n  conda run -n dataq python backend/scripts/seed_dev.py\n  ok \"Dev data seeded\"\nelse\n  echo \"  (no seed script yet — skipping)\"\nfi\n\n# ── Done ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\necho \"\"\necho -e \"${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}\"\necho -e \"${GREEN}  DataQ dev environment ready!${NC}\"\necho -e \"${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}\"\necho \"\"\necho \"  Next steps:\"\necho \"    conda activate dataq\"\necho \"    docker compose up          # start all services\"\necho \"    # API: http://localhost:8000/docs\"\necho \"    # UI:  http://localhost:3000\"\necho \"\"\n"
}

Good, fixes pushed. Now while CI re-runs, here's the code review of PR #25:

---

### PR #25 Review

**CONTRIBUTING.md** — Solid. 37 rules across 8 categories, module boundary table, naming conventions, error shape contract. One note: rules 30 and 31 overlap with the DB section already in CLAUDE.md §6 — intentional duplication as CONTRIBUTING.md is the authoritative reference.

**environment.yml** — Good pinning strategy. GX Core exact (`==`) per working-agreement, others `==` for full reproducibility. One issue just fixed: pytest 9 + pytest-asyncio 0.26 was incompatible.

**pyproject.toml** — Well-structured. `B008` (FastAPI `Depends`) and `S101` (assert in tests) ignores are correct. `cov-fail-under=0` placeholder with comment is clear. The `[build-system]` block is technically not needed since this isn't a package, but it doesn't hurt.

**pre-commit** — All versions match `environment.yml`. `no-commit-to-branch: main` guard is a good safety net. One potential friction: `mypy` hook runs on every commit with `additional_dependencies` that get re-downloaded — this will be slow. Acceptable for now, worth noting.

**Frontend** — React 19 + Vite 6 + TS strict. ESLint flat config via `.eslintrc.cjs` is correct for the `"type": "module"` package. `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: error` is appropriately strict. `vite.config.ts` doubles as Vitest config cleanly.

**ci.yml** — After the fix: 7 jobs, all guarded for empty-repo state. `continue-on-error` on CodeQL is the right call until code exists. Frontend now uses `--no-frozen-lockfile` (fine until a lockfile is committed in PR 2). One follow-up: once `backend/` lands in PR 2, remove the `[ -d backend ]` guards — they'll become dead code.

**dependabot.yml** — GX Core correctly excluded from auto-update.

**scripts/setup.sh** — Idempotent (`env update` vs `env create`), waits for Postgres readiness with a 30s timeout, skips seed if script doesn't exist. Solid.

**Verdict: Conditional — wait for CI green, then merge.** No code changes needed beyond the fix just pushed.

1	# Contributing to DataQ
2	
3	> Working agreements for everyone (human and AI) writing code in this repo. These rules are locked in Week 1 and override any "speed > quality" temptation. If a week's exit gate conflicts with them, **the rules win**.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## A. Commit & change discipline
8	
9	1. **One functionality per commit** (where possible). Each commit must be independently reviewable; do not bundle two unrelated changes.
10	2. **Manually test each committed change before starting the next functionality.** Required until the unit-test suite reaches 80% coverage (Week 8 gate). "Tested" means: the affected code path was exercised locally, not just that it compiled.
11	3. **Defects → GitHub issue first, never silent fixes.** Use `gh issue create --title "fix: <desc>"`. The PR that fixes it must include `Fixes #N` in the title or body.
12	4. **From Week 8 onward, every new functionality ships with unit tests.** Tests live next to the code they cover (`backend/tests/`, `frontend/tests/`).
13	5. **Definition of Done (DoD)** per task:
14	   - Code merged to `main`
15	   - Manually tested locally
16	   - (From Week 8) unit tests written and passing
17	   - Docs / ADR updated if the change is user-facing or architectural
18	   - Linked GitHub issue closed if one exists
19	
20	---
21	
22	## B. Git workflow
23	
24	6. **Trunk-based development** — branch off `main`, PR back to `main`. No long-lived `develop` or `release` branches.
25	7. **Branch naming:**
26	   - `feature/<short-desc>` — new functionality
27	   - `fix/issue-<N>-<short-desc>` — bug fix tied to a GitHub issue
28	   - `chore/<short-desc>` — tooling, deps, config, non-functional
29	   - `docs/<short-desc>` — documentation only
30	8. **`main` branch protection:** PR required + passing CI + no force-push. Approving-review count is 0 during solo-dev phase; re-enable (≥1) before onboarding a second contributor.
31	9. **Squash-merge only into `main`.** Keeps history linear and matches rule #1. Feature branch commit history is squashed into a single commit on merge.
32	10. **Conventional commits** for PR titles and the squash-merge commit message:
33	    - `feat:` — new user-facing functionality
34	    - `fix:` — bug fix
35	    - `chore:` — tooling, config, deps (no production behaviour change)
36	    - `docs:` — documentation only
37	    - `test:` — tests only
38	    - `refactor:` — code restructure with no behaviour change
39	    - `ci:` — CI/CD workflow changes
40	    - Format: `<type>(<optional scope>): <short imperative description>`
41	    - Examples: `feat(api): add suite dry-run endpoint`, `fix(celery): handle graceful shutdown on SIGTERM`
42	11. **PR template** checklist (`.github/pull_request_template.md`): manual test ✓, linked issue, security implications, schema migration.
43	12. **`CODEOWNERS`** (`.github/CODEOWNERS`) auto-routes reviews per area.
44	
45	---
46	
47	## C. CI/CD quality gates
48	
49	All checks run on every PR and must pass before merge.
50	
51	13. **Python:** Ruff (lint) → Black `--check` (format) → mypy (types) → Bandit (SAST) → pytest (from Week 8).
52	14. **Frontend:** ESLint → Prettier `--check` → Vitest (from Week 8).
53	15. **Secret scanning:** gitleaks in pre-commit hook AND in CI. A secret detected in CI blocks merge.
54	16. **SAST:** Bandit (Python) + CodeQL (GitHub Actions) on every PR.
55	17. **Dependency vulnerability scanning:** Dependabot alerts + auto-PRs for security updates. Deps are pinned in `environment.yml` and locked with `conda-lock`.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## D. Coding structure & tooling
60	
61	These are locked on Day 1 of Week 1. Do not drift.
62	
63	18. **Python runtime:** `conda` only (`conda create -n dataq python=3.11`). Not venv, not poetry, not pyenv.
64	19. **Python formatter:** Black. Config in `pyproject.toml`. CI rejects unformatted code.
65	20. **Python linter:** Ruff. Replaces flake8 + isort + pyupgrade. Config in `pyproject.toml`.
66	21. **Python type checker:** mypy (strict mode). Config in `pyproject.toml`.
67	22. **Frontend package manager:** pnpm. Not npm, not yarn.
68	23. **Frontend formatter:** Prettier. Config in `frontend/.prettierrc`.
69	24. **Frontend linter:** ESLint with TypeScript rules. Config in `frontend/.eslintrc.cjs`.
70	25. **Config / 12-factor:** All environment-specific config via env vars. Backend uses Pydantic Settings (`backend/app/core/config.py`). Frontend uses Vite env vars (`VITE_*`). No env-specific code branches.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## E. Observability & error handling
75	
76	26. **Structured logging from Week 1.** `structlog` with JSON output. Every log entry carries a `request_id` correlation ID propagated FastAPI → Celery → GX. Configuration in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.
77	27. **PII redaction at the logger level** — not at every call site. Failed-check sample rows can contain sensitive data. The redactor in `backend/app/core/logging.py` strips known PII fields centrally.
78	28. **Consistent error shape** across all API responses. Definition in `backend/app/core/errors.py`:
79	    ```json
80	    { "error": { "code": "SNAKE_CASE_CODE", "message": "Human-readable string", "detail": {} } }
81	    ```
82	29. **App Insights exception tracking wired from Week 1**, not Week 7. Middleware in `backend/app/main.py` captures all unhandled exceptions from the first commit.
83	
84	---
85	
86	## F. Database & migrations
87	
88	30. **Backward-compatible migrations only.** No `DROP COLUMN` + code change in the same PR. Two-step deploys from Week 5 onward:
89	    1. PR A: migration adds/renames column; old code still works.
90	    2. PR B (later): code change that depends on the new schema.
91	31. **Migration PR checklist:** rollback plan documented + "tested `alembic upgrade head` and `alembic downgrade -1` locally" ticked before requesting review.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## G. Documentation & decision history
96	
97	32. **ADRs in `docs/adr/`** for every significant architecture decision. Use the `/adr-create` skill or follow the template in `docs/adr/README.md`. One short markdown per decision; keep it to 1–2 pages.
98	33. **Architecture diagram in `docs/architecture.md`** (Mermaid). When a new component, datasource, or integration is added, update the diagram in the same PR as the code.
99	34. **Local setup script** `scripts/setup.sh` — one command from a fresh clone to a working dev environment (conda env + pre-commit install + docker-compose up + `alembic upgrade head` + seed data).
100	
101	---
102	
103	## H. Security review cadence
104	
105	35. **End-of-week quick scan from Week 2 onward:** review Dependabot vuln alerts, secret scan results, OWASP top-10 spot check on any new endpoints, Key Vault access audit.
106	36. **Hard security review gate before Week 7 deploy:** full pass on all of the above plus public-endpoint exposure review (especially `/api/v1/orchestration/events/*` and `/mcp`).
107	37. **Security vulnerabilities are not public GitHub issues.** Report via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new). See [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md).
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Module boundaries & naming conventions
112	
113	### Backend (`backend/`)
114	
115	| Layer | Package | Responsibility |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| API | `backend/app/api/v1/` | FastAPI routers only — no business logic |
118	| Services | `backend/app/services/` | Business logic, orchestration between layers |
119	| Orchestration | `backend/app/orchestration/` | `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction + ADF/Airflow impls |
120	| Datasources | `backend/app/datasources/` | GX adapter per datasource type |
121	| DB | `backend/app/db/` | SQLAlchemy models + session management |
122	| Core | `backend/app/core/` | Config, logging, errors — imported by all layers |
123	| MCP | `backend/app/mcp/` | FastMCP tools (Week 7 only) |
124	
125	**Naming:**
126	- Files: `snake_case.py`
127	- Classes: `PascalCase`
128	- Functions / variables: `snake_case`
129	- Constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`
130	- Async functions: always `async def` for anything that touches DB, Redis, or external HTTP
131	
132	**Import order** (enforced by Ruff / isort):
133	1. Standard library
134	2. Third-party (`fastapi`, `sqlalchemy`, `celery`, …)
135	3. First-party (`backend.app.*`)
136	
137	### Frontend (`frontend/`)
138	
139	| Layer | Path | Responsibility |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| Pages | `src/pages/` | Route-level components |
142	| Components | `src/components/` | Reusable UI components |
143	| API client | `src/api/` | Generated OpenAPI client (Week 4+) |
144	| Hooks | `src/hooks/` | Custom React hooks |
145	| Store | `src/store/` | Global state (if needed) |
146	
147	**Naming:**
148	- Component files: `PascalCase.tsx`
149	- Hook files: `useXxx.ts`
150	- Util files: `camelCase.ts`
151	
152	---
153	
154	## Local development
155	
156	```bash
157	# One-time setup from a fresh clone (requires conda installed):
158	./scripts/setup.sh
159	
160	# Day-to-day:
161	conda activate dataq
162	docker-compose up           # starts Postgres, Redis, FastAPI, React dev server, Celery worker
163	
164	# Backend only:
165	cd backend && uvicorn app.main:app --reload
166	
167	# Frontend only:
168	cd frontend && pnpm dev
169	
170	# Run pre-commit on all files:
171	pre-commit run --all-files
172	
173	# Run backend tests (Week 8+):
174	cd backend && pytest
175	
176	# Run frontend tests (Week 8+):
177	cd frontend && pnpm test
178	```
179	
180	> Commands above assume Week 1 scaffolding (`environment.yml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/setup.sh`) is committed.
181

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# One-command dev environment setup from a fresh clone.
3	# Usage: ./scripts/setup.sh
4	# Requires: conda (miniconda/miniforge), docker, pnpm, git
5	
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	CYAN='\033[0;36m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; RED='\033[0;31m'; NC='\033[0m'
9	step() { echo -e "${CYAN}▶ $1${NC}"; }
10	ok()   { echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}"; }
11	die()  { echo -e "${RED}✗ $1${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }
12	
13	# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	step "Checking prerequisites"
15	command -v conda  >/dev/null || die "conda not found — install miniconda or miniforge first"
16	command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not found"
17	command -v pnpm   >/dev/null || die "pnpm not found — run: npm install -g pnpm"
18	command -v git    >/dev/null || die "git not found"
19	ok "Prerequisites OK"
20	
21	# ── Conda environment ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
22	step "Creating / updating conda environment 'dataq'"
23	if conda env list | grep -q "^dataq "; then
24	  conda env update -n dataq -f environment.yml --prune
25	  ok "Conda env updated"
26	else
27	  conda env create -f environment.yml
28	  ok "Conda env created"
29	fi
30	
31	# ── Pre-commit hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
32	step "Installing pre-commit hooks"
33	conda run -n dataq pre-commit install --install-hooks
34	ok "Pre-commit hooks installed"
35	
36	# ── Frontend dependencies ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
37	step "Installing frontend dependencies (pnpm)"
38	(cd frontend && pnpm install)
39	ok "Frontend dependencies installed"
40	
41	# ── Docker services ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
42	step "Starting Docker services (Postgres, Redis)"
43	docker compose up -d postgres redis
44	ok "Docker services started"
45	
46	# ── Database migrations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
47	step "Waiting for Postgres to be ready"
48	for i in $(seq 1 30); do
49	  if docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U dataq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	    ok "Postgres ready"
51	    break
52	  fi
53	  [ "$i" -eq 30 ] && die "Postgres did not become ready in time"
54	  sleep 1
55	done
56	
57	step "Running Alembic migrations"
58	conda run -n dataq sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"
59	ok "Migrations applied"
60	
61	# ── Seed data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
62	step "Seeding dev data"
63	if [ -f backend/scripts/seed_dev.py ]; then
64	  conda run -n dataq python backend/scripts/seed_dev.py
65	  ok "Dev data seeded"
66	else
67	  echo "  (no seed script yet — skipping)"
68	fi
69	
70	# ── Done ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
71	echo ""
72	echo -e "${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}"
73	echo -e "${GREEN}  DataQ dev environment ready!${NC}"
74	echo -e "${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}"
75	echo ""
76	echo "  Next steps:"
77	echo "    conda activate dataq"
78	echo "    docker compose up          # start all services"
79	echo "    # API: http://localhost:8000/docs"
80	echo "    # UI:  http://localhost:3000"
81	echo ""
82

12	## Commit & change discipline
13	1. **One functionality per commit** (where possible). No batched commits.
14	2. **Manually test each committed change before starting the next functionality** — required until unit tests land in Week 8.

+from functools import lru_cache
+from typing import Literal
+
+from pydantic import Field
+from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
+
+
+class Settings(BaseSettings):
+    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
+        env_file=".env",
+        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
+        extra="ignore",
+        case_sensitive=False,
+    )
+
+    environment: Literal["dev", "staging", "prod"] = "dev"
+    log_level: Literal["DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR", "CRITICAL"] = "INFO"
+
+    database_url: str = Field(default="REDACTED")
+    redis_url: str = Field(default="redis://localhost:6379/0")
+
+    applicationinsights_connection_string: str | None = None
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def get_settings() -> Settings:
+    return Settings()

> AGENT

## Code Review — PR #39

**Overview:** Lands docker-compose (postgres + redis) and `Settings` (Pydantic). 70 lines, 6 new files. Tightly scoped, matches plan.

**Correctness**
- `Settings` loads cleanly; defaults are sensible for dev.
- Compose healthchecks correct; named volume for postgres data persistence.
- `lru_cache(maxsize=1)` makes `get_settings()` a proper singleton.

**Conventions**
- Conforms to CLAUDE.md (Pydantic Settings, 12-factor, conda env deps already present).
- `chore:` prefix correct for non-user-facing.
- No comments-noise; one short comment in `.env.example` explaining the file's purpose.

**Suggestions (all minor, none blocking)**
- `case_sensitive=False` is Pydantic Settings' default — line is redundant. Drop or keep for explicitness.
- `extra="ignore"` is permissive (typos in env vars silently ignored). Acceptable now because `.env` is shared with compose (POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD/DB live there too and aren't Settings fields). Note for later: once we split app-only vs compose-only env files, tighten to `extra="forbid"`.
- Hardcoded `dataq:dataq` credentials are fine for local dev (compose-only, localhost-bound) but should be a deploy-checklist item: production must set all secrets via Container Apps secret refs.

**Risks**
- None for this slice. Real risk surface arrives in PR 2b (App Insights wiring, error shape, FastAPI middleware order) and PR 2c (schema model).

**Test plan executed locally:** ✅ compose validates, services come up healthy, all backend lints/types pass.

**Verdict:** Merge-ready.

backend.app.core.config import get_settings\n\nrequest_id_var: ContextVar[str | None] = ContextVar(\"request_id\", default=None)\n\n_PII_KEYS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(\n    {\n        \"password\",\n        \"passwd\",\n        \"secret\",\n        \"token\",\n        \"api_key\",\n        \"apikey\",\n        \"authorization\",\n        \"auth\",\n        \"access_key\",\n        \"private_key\",\n        \"email\",\n        \"phone\",\n        \"ssn\",\n        \"credit_card\",\n        \"card_number\",\n    }\n)\n_REDACTED = \"<redacted>\"\n\n\ndef _redact_pii(_logger: Any, _name: str, event_dict: EventDict) -> EventDict:\n    def walk(value: Any) -> Any:\n        if isinstance(value, dict):\n            return {k: (_REDACTED if k.lower() in _PII_KEYS else walk(v)) for k, v in value.items()}\n        if isinstance(value, list):\n            return [walk(v) for v in value]\n        return value\n\n    return walk(event_dict)\n\n\ndef _add_request_id(_logger: Any, _name: str, event_dict: EventDict) -> EventDict:\n    rid = request_id_var.get()\n    if rid is not None:\n        event_dict[\"request_id\"] = rid\n    return event_dict\n\n\ndef configure_logging() -> None:\n    settings = get_settings()\n    level = getattr(logging, settings.log_level)\n\n    logging.basicConfig(\n        format=\"%(message)s\",\n        stream=sys.stdout,\n        level=level,\n    )\n\n    shared_processors: list[Processor] = [\n        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,\n        _add_request_id,\n        structlog.processors.add_log_level,\n        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt=\"iso\", utc=True),\n        _redact_pii,\n    ]\n\n    structlog.configure(\n        processors=[\n            *shared_processors,\n            structlog.processors.dict_tracebacks,\n            structlog.processors.JSONRenderer(),\n        ],\n        wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(level),\n        logger_factory=structlog.stdlib.LoggerFactory(),\n        cache_logger_on_first_use=True,\n    )\n\n\ndef get_logger(name: str | None = None) -> structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger:\n    return structlog.get_logger(name)\n"

import BaseModel, Field\nfrom starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException\n\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\n\nlogger = get_logger(__name__)\n\n\nclass ErrorBody(BaseModel):\n    code: str\n    message: str\n    detail: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)\n\n\nclass ErrorResponse(BaseModel):\n    error: ErrorBody\n\n\nclass DataQError(Exception):\n    status_code: int = status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR\n    code: str = \"internal_error\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        message: str,\n        *,\n        code: str | None = None,\n        status_code: int | None = None,\n        detail: dict[str, Any] | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.message = message\n        if code is not None:\n            self.code = code\n        if status_code is not None:\n            self.status_code = status_code\n        self.detail: dict[str, Any] = detail or {}\n\n\ndef _envelope(code: str, message: str, detail: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    return ErrorResponse(error=ErrorBody(code=code, message=message, detail=detail or {})).model_dump()\n\n\nasync def _dataq_error_handler(_request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n    assert isinstance(exc, DataQError)\n    logger.warning(\"dataq_error\", code=exc.code, message=exc.message, status=exc.status_code)\n    return JSONResponse(\n        status_code=exc.status_code,\n        content=_envelope(exc.code, exc.message, exc.detail),\n    )\n\n\nasync def _http_exception_handler(_request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n    assert isinstance(exc, StarletteHTTPException)\n    return JSONResponse(\n        status_code=exc.status_code,\n        content=_envelope(\"http_error\", str(exc.detail)),\n    )\n\n\nasync def _validation_exception_handler(_request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n    assert isinstance(exc, RequestValidationError)\n    return JSONResponse(\n        status_code=status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,\n        content=_envelope(\"validation_error\", \"Request validation failed\", {\"errors\": exc.errors()}),\n    )\n\n\nasync def _unhandled_exception_handler(_request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n    logger.exception(\"unhandled_exception\", error_type=type(exc).__name__)\n    return JSONResponse(\n        status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,\n        content=_envelope(\"internal_error\", \"Internal server error\"),\n    )\n\n\ndef register_exception_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:\n    app.add_exception_handler(DataQError, _dataq_error_handler)\n    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, _http_exception_handler)\n    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, _validation_exception_handler)\n    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, _unhandled_exception_handler)\n"

diff --git a/backend/app/core/errors.py b/backend/app/core/errors.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bafa1bb
--- /dev/null
+++ b/backend/app/core/errors.py
@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+from typing import Any
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, status
+from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
+from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
+
+from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class ErrorBody(BaseModel):
+    code: str
+    message: str
+    detail: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class ErrorResponse(BaseModel):
+    error: ErrorBody
+
+
+class DataQError(Exception):
+    status_code: int = status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
+    code: str = "internal_error"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        message: str,
+        *,
+        code: str | None = None,
+        status_code: int | None = None,
+        detail: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(message)
+        self.message = message
+        if code is not None:
+            self.code = code
+        if status_code is not None:
+            self.status_code = status_code
+        self.detail: dict[str, Any] = detail or {}
+
+
+def _envelope(code: str, message: str, detail: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return ErrorResponse(
+        error=ErrorBody(code=code, message=message, detail=detail or {})
+    ).model_dump()
+
+
+async def _dataq_error_handler(_request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
+    assert isinstance(exc, DataQError)
+    logger.warning("dataq_error", code=exc.code, message=exc.message, status=exc.status_code)
+    return JSONResponse(
+        status_code=exc.status_code,
+        content=_envelope(exc.code, exc.message, exc.detail),
+    )
+
+
+async def _http_exception_handler(_request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
+    assert isinstance(exc, StarletteHTTPException)
+    return JSONResponse(
+        status_code=exc.status_code,
+        content=_envelope("http_error", str(exc.detail)),
+    )
+
+
+async def _validation_exception_handler(_request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
+    assert isinstance(exc, RequestValidationError)
+    return JSONResponse(
+        status_code=status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
+        content=_envelope(
+            "validation_error", "Request validation failed", {"errors": exc.errors()}
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+async def _unhandled_exception_handler(_request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
+    logger.exception("unhandled_exception", error_type=type(exc).__name__)
+    return JSONResponse(
+        status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
+        content=_envelope("internal_error", "Internal server error"),
+    )
+
+
+def register_exception_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
+    app.add_exception_handler(DataQError, _dataq_error_handler)
+    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, _http_exception_handler)
+    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, _validation_exception_handler)
+    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, _unhandled_exception_handler)

+++ b/backend/app/core/logging.py
@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+import logging
+import sys
+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from typing import Any
+
+import structlog
+from structlog.types import EventDict, Processor
+
+from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
+
+request_id_var: ContextVar[str | None] = ContextVar("request_id", default=None)
+
+_PII_KEYS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
+    {
+        "password",
+        "passwd",
+        "secret",
+        "token",
+        "api_key",
+        "apikey",
+        "authorization",
+        "auth",
+        "access_key",
+        "private_key",
+        "email",
+        "phone",
+        "ssn",
+        "credit_card",
+        "card_number",
+    }
+)
+_REDACTED = "<redacted>"
+
+
+def _redact_pii(_logger: Any, _name: str, event_dict: EventDict) -> EventDict:
+    def walk(value: Any) -> Any:
+        if isinstance(value, dict):
+            return {k: (_REDACTED if k.lower() in _PII_KEYS else walk(v)) for k, v in value.items()}
+        if isinstance(value, list):
+            return [walk(v) for v in value]
+        return value
+
+    result: EventDict = walk(event_dict)
+    return result
+
+
+def _add_request_id(_logger: Any, _name: str, event_dict: EventDict) -> EventDict:
+    rid = request_id_var.get()
+    if rid is not None:
+        event_dict["request_id"] = rid
+    return event_dict
+
+
+def configure_logging() -> None:
+    settings = get_settings()
+    level = getattr(logging, settings.log_level)
+
+    logging.basicConfig(
+        format="%(message)s",
+        stream=sys.stdout,
+        level=level,
+    )
+
+    conn = settings.applicationinsights_connection_string
+    if conn:
+        from opencensus.ext.azure.log_exporter import AzureLogHandler
+
+        handler = AzureLogHandler(connection_string=conn)
+        handler.setLevel(level)
+        logging.getLogger().addHandler(handler)
+
+    shared_processors: list[Processor] = [
+        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,
+        _add_request_id,
+        structlog.processors.add_log_level,
+        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso", utc=True),
+        _redact_pii,
+    ]
+
+    structlog.configure(
+        processors=[
+            *shared_processors,
+            structlog.processors.dict_tracebacks,
+            structlog.processors.JSONRenderer(),
+        ],
+        wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(level),
+        logger_factory=structlog.stdlib.LoggerFactory(),
+        cache_logger_on_first_use=True,
+    )
+
+
+def get_logger(name: str | None = None) -> structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger:
+    logger: structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger = structlog.get_logger(name)
+    return logger

+++ b/backend/app/main.py
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+import uuid
+from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable
+from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, Response
+
+from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
+from backend.app.core.errors import register_exception_handlers
+from backend.app.core.logging import configure_logging, get_logger, request_id_var
+
+REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "X-Request-ID"
+
+
+@asynccontextmanager
+async def lifespan(_app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
+    configure_logging()
+    logger = get_logger(__name__)
+    settings = get_settings()
+    logger.info(
+        "app_startup",
+        environment=settings.environment,
+        log_level=settings.log_level,
+        app_insights_enabled=bool(settings.applicationinsights_connection_string),
+    )
+    yield
+    logger.info("app_shutdown")
+
+
+app = FastAPI(title="DataQ API", lifespan=lifespan)
+
+
+@app.middleware("http")
+async def request_id_middleware(
+    request: Request, call_next: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]]
+) -> Response:
+    rid = request.headers.get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER) or uuid.uuid4().hex
+    token = request_id_var.set(rid)
+    try:
+        response = await call_next(request)
+    finally:
+        request_id_var.reset(token)
+    response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = rid
+    return response
+
+
+register_exception_handlers(app)
+
+
+@app.get("/healthz")
+async def healthz() -> dict[str, str]:
+    return {"status": "ok"}

## Code Review — PR #40

**Overview:** Lands structlog-based JSON logging with request-id correlation + PII redaction, consistent error envelope with handlers for the 4 exception classes, and a minimal FastAPI app with lifespan-managed init and `/healthz`. 3 files, 235 lines, mypy-strict clean, locally smoke-tested end-to-end.

**Correctness**
- Error envelope matches working-agreement §28 exactly.
- `request_id` middleware correctly uses ContextVar with try/finally reset; rid echoed on response.
- `_unhandled_exception_handler` returns generic "Internal server error" — no exception detail leak (security ✓). Logs via `logger.exception` so traceback flows to App Insights when wired.
- `_redact_pii` contract is **kwargs-only** (it only sees the structured event_dict). f-strings like `logger.info(f"user={email}")` will still leak. Acceptable — this matches the "at logger level" intent: callers must use kwargs, redactor enforces.
- `Field(default_factory=dict)` on `ErrorBody.detail` — correct, avoids shared mutable default.
- `assert isinstance(exc, ...)` in handlers is for mypy narrowing; safe because FastAPI dispatches by registered type. Caveat: stripped under `python -O`, but production won't run with that.

**Conventions**
- ✓ CLAUDE.md §10 (App Insights wired W1, no-op when unset; lazy import keeps opencensus out of the import graph otherwise).
- ✓ Working-agreement §27 (PII redaction central, not per-call-site).
- ✓ `chore:` scope correct.

**Suggestions (all minor, non-blocking)**
- PII keys are exact-match. `user_email` / `client_password` won't trip. Could use `any(pii in k.lower() for pii in _PII_KEYS)` for substring matching — accept the false-positive risk (e.g. "secretary" → "secret"). Defer until we have real log samples to tune against.
- `_envelope` builds a Pydantic model only to `model_dump()` it. Exception path so cold — don't optimize.
- `dict_tracebacks` puts exception args into the JSON event. If an exception message happens to contain PII, the redactor won't see it (it's a string, not a dict key). Caller-discipline issue, same kind as f-strings.

**Risks**
- None blocking for this slice.
- Future work: CORS middleware will be needed when frontend connects (out of scope for PR2). Auth middleware lands later per roadmap.

**Verdict:** merge-ready.

Locked. Here's the proposed schema — please flag anything you want changed before I write the migration. (Status enums, indexes, and PII-in-`sample_failures` are noted at the bottom.)

### Tables (9)

**`users`** — AAD mirror
- `id` UUID PK, `aad_object_id` TEXT UNIQUE, `email`, `display_name`, `last_seen_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`

**`connections`** — datasources + orchestration providers (one table, `type` discriminates)
- `id`, `name`, `type` TEXT (`snowflake|adls_gen2|s3|unity_catalog|adf|airflow`), `env` (`dev|qa|uat|prod`), `config` JSONB, `secret_ref` TEXT (Key Vault secret **name**, never the secret itself), `created_by` → users, timestamps
- UNIQUE `(name, env)`

**`suites`**
- `id`, `name`, `description`, `connection_id` → connections (the *datasource* the suite runs against; orchestration connections can't be referenced here — enforced at app layer, not DB), `created_by` → users, timestamps

**`checks`**
- `id`, `suite_id` → suites (CASCADE), `name`, `expectation_type` TEXT (GX expectation name), `config` JSONB (kwargs), timestamps
- *No severity columns yet* — added in W3 backward-compatibly.

**`runs`** — DQ suite executions
- `id`, `suite_id` → suites, `status` TEXT (`queued|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled`), `triggered_by` TEXT (free-form: `manual:<user_id>`, `schedule:<name>`, `<provider>:<pipeline_id>:<provider_run_id>`), `started_at`, `finished_at`, `created_at`

**`results`** — per-check results within a run
- `id`, `run_id` → runs (CASCADE), `check_id` → checks, `status` TEXT (`passed|failed|skipped`), `observed_value` JSONB, `expected_value` JSONB, `sample_failures` JSONB, `created_at`

**`shares`**
- `id`, `suite_id` → suites (CASCADE), `user_id` → users (CASCADE), `permission` TEXT (`view|edit|admin`), `created_at`
- UNIQUE `(suite_id, user_id)`

**`pipeline_runs`** — orchestrator runs (NOT `runs`)
- `id`, `provider` TEXT (`adf|airflow`), `connection_id` → connections, `provider_run_id` TEXT, `pipeline_or_dag_id` TEXT, `env`, `status`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `failure_reason` TEXT, `last_updated_at`, `created_at`
- UNIQUE `(provider, provider_run_id)`

**`trigger_bindings`** — pipeline/DAG → suite
- `id`, `provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`, `suite_id` → suites (CASCADE), `enabled` BOOL, timestamps
- UNIQUE `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env, suite_id)` — one pipeline can map to multiple suites, each binding unique

### Cross-cutting choices

- **Status enums:** `TEXT` + CHECK constraint, not native PG enum. Easier to add values via migration.
- **Indexes baseline:** all FKs, `pipeline_runs(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id)`, `trigger_bindings(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env)`.
- **Timestamps:** `TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` for `created_at`; `updated_at` maintained via SQLAlchemy `onupdate` (server default not portable enough).
- **Naming:** snake_case tables and columns per CONTRIBUTING.md.
- **Alembic config:** baseline migration only — no autogenerate against an empty DB; hand-written for clarity.

### Two flagged concerns (not blocking — noting)

1. **`results.sample_failures` can contain PII.** Stored raw in JSONB; redactor only operates on logs. v1 trade-off; revisit (encryption-at-rest? row masking?) when first real datasource onboards.
2. **`suites.connection_id` referencing an orchestration-type connection** is invalid but not enforced at the DB level — only at the app layer (`suite_service.create()`). Could add a CHECK that joins `connections.type IN ('snowflake', 'adls_gen2', 's3', 'unity_catalog')`, but that requires either a trigger or denormalising `type` onto `suites`. I'd leave it as an app-layer guard.

Anything to change?

+def run_migrations_offline() -> None:
+    url = config.get_main_option("sqlalchemy.url")
+    context.configure(
+        url=url,
+        target_metadata=target_metadata,
+        literal_binds=True,
+        dialect_opts={"paramstyle": "named"},
+        compare_type=True,
+    )
+    with context.begin_transaction():
+        context.run_migrations()
+
+
+def run_migrations_online() -> None:
+    connectable = engine_from_config(
+        config.get_section(config.config_ini_section, {}),
+        prefix="sqlalchemy.",
+        poolclass=pool.NullPool,
+    )
+    with connectable.connect() as connection:
+        context.configure(
+            connection=connection,
+            target_metadata=target_metadata,
+            compare_type=True,
+        )
+        with context.begin_transaction():
+            context.run_migrations()
+
+
+if context.is_offline_mode():
+    run_migrations_offline()
+else:
+    run_migrations_online()

## Code Review — PR #41

**Overview:** Lands 9-table v1 schema + Alembic baseline. 732 lines across 10 files. CI green (10/10).

**Correctness**
- `gen_random_uuid()` is PG 13+ core — we're on `postgres:16-alpine` ✓. No extension needed.
- `compare_type=True` in alembic env — future autogenerate will catch column-type drift.
- `pool_pre_ping=True` on engine — handles dropped DB connections gracefully.
- Constraint names all under PG's 63-char identifier limit (longest: `ix_trigger_bindings_provider_pipeline_env` = 42 chars).
- Round-trip verified locally: upgrade → downgrade → upgrade clean.

**Conventions**
- ✓ snake_case, CONTRIBUTING.md naming convention enforced via SQLAlchemy metadata.
- ✓ All design decisions land as agreed: UUID v4, no severity columns, hard-delete only, local users table, TEXT+CHECK enums, `sample_failures_purged_at` for W5 sweep.
- ✓ `pipeline_runs` ≠ `runs`; `trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic (CLAUDE.md §10).

**Notable gap — missing FK indexes (worth a follow-up)**

PostgreSQL doesn't auto-index FK columns. The migration is missing indexes on these FK columns (queries reverse-traversing the FK will seq-scan):
- `connections.created_by`
- `suites.connection_id`, `suites.created_by`
- `checks.suite_id`
- `pipeline_runs.connection_id`
- `trigger_bindings.suite_id`

Covered (indexed because of UNIQUE constraint or explicit index): `shares.(suite_id, user_id)`, `runs.suite_id`, `results.run_id`, `pipeline_runs.(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id)`, `trigger_bindings.(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env)`.

Not blocking — schema works today, tables start empty. Recommend filing a follow-up issue to add FK indexes in a backward-compatible migration before real data lands (Week 4 ish).

**Other minor (non-blocking)**
- `connections.secret_ref` is NULLABLE. Most connection types need creds, but Airflow basic-poll or unauthenticated S3 could theoretically lack them. Permissive default; tighten later if you want.
- `trigger_bindings` keyed by `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env)` — can't disambiguate two `airflow` instances both in the same env (e.g. two dev Airflows). Agreed shape from earlier signoff; assumes one orchestrator instance per (provider, env).

**Risks**
- None blocking. The schema is the load-bearing decision for everything downstream; getting it right matters more than getting it shipped fast. Locked design choices are sound.

**Verdict:** merge-ready. I'll file the FK-index follow-up after merge.

1	---
2	name: migration-safety
3	description: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement #24 ("backward-compatible migrations only — no DROP COLUMN + code change in the same PR"). Use proactively on every PR that adds, modifies, or removes a file under backend/alembic/versions/. Also invoke when the user asks "is this migration safe?" or before any production deploy from Week 5 onward.
4	tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash

6	---
7	
8	You are a specialized Alembic migration reviewer enforcing **backward-compatible migrations only** per [working-agreement #24](../../CLAUDE.md).
9	
10	## Why this matters
11	
12	From Week 5 onward, `results` and `pipeline_runs` will hold real data. A migration that drops a column or renames it in the same release as the code change crashes any worker still running the old image during rollout. Two-step migrations (deploy code that tolerates both shapes → migrate → deploy code that assumes new shape) are mandatory.
13	
14	## What you check
15	
16	Audit every `.py` file under `backend/alembic/versions/` that's added or modified in the diff. Use `gh pr diff <N>` if a PR number is provided, otherwise `git diff main...HEAD -- 'backend/alembic/versions/*.py'`.
17	
18	### 🔴 Hard violations (block merge)
19	
20	Each of these is unsafe under concurrent rolling deploy and must be split into a two-step migration:
21	
22	1. **`op.drop_column(...)`** — dropping a column the old code may still reference. Two-step: (1) deploy code that stops reading/writing the column; (2) later release drops the column.
23	2. **`op.drop_table(...)`** — same reasoning at table level.
24	3. **`op.alter_column(..., nullable=False)`** where the column was previously nullable and the migration does **not** include a `server_default` to backfill. Old code writing NULL will fail.
25	4. **`op.alter_column(..., type_=...)`** changing a column type in a non-implicit way (e.g., `String → Integer`, `Integer → UUID`). Implicit widening (`String(50) → String(255)`) is acceptable; type *changes* are not.
26	5. **`op.rename_column(...)`** — same operational issue as drop+add. Must be a two-step: (1) add new column, dual-write in code; (2) backfill; (3) flip reads; (4) later release drops the old column.
27	6. **`op.rename_table(...)`** — same reasoning.
28	7. **`op.drop_constraint(...)` for FK or unique** where the constraint enforces data invariants the application depends on. Acceptable only if explicitly noted as part of a planned rollout.
29	8. **Missing `downgrade()` body** (only `pass`) for any non-trivial migration. Rollback path must exist per the migration PR checklist in `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
30	9. **DDL inside a single transaction with DML on the same table** — risks deadlocks on production-sized tables. Heuristic: presence of `op.execute("UPDATE ...")` followed by structural changes in the same migration.
31	10. **`op.execute("...")` containing destructive SQL keywords** — raw SQL bypasses the `op.*` pattern matchers above. Scan the string argument for `DROP`, `RENAME`, `ALTER ... TYPE`, `ALTER ... SET NOT NULL` (without `DEFAULT`), `TRUNCATE`. Same backward-compatibility rules apply as for the equivalent `op.*` calls.
32	
33	### 🟡 Yellow flags (call out, don't necessarily block)
34	
35	1. **Index creation without `CONCURRENTLY`** on Postgres for a table that will be large (`runs`, `results`, `pipeline_runs`, `check_results`). Use `op.create_index(..., postgresql_concurrently=True)` and a separate transaction.
36	2. **No data backfill plan** for a new NOT NULL column with no `server_default`.
37	3. **Migration touches tables in two unrelated domains** in one revision (e.g., `connections` and `pipeline_runs` together). Suggests two migrations bundled.
38	4. **No docstring at the top of the migration file** describing intent and the rollout sequence.
39	5. **`down_revision` doesn't match the previously-latest migration** — possible merge conflict that got resolved incorrectly.
40	
41	### 🟢 Acceptable patterns
42	
43	- Add nullable column → backfill in a separate release → set NOT NULL → drop default. Three migrations, three releases.
44	- Adding a new table.
45	- Adding a new index using `postgresql_concurrently=True` in its own migration.
46	- Adding constraints in `NOT VALID` mode, then `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` in a later migration.
47	
48	## How to report
49	
50	Produce a structured report:
51	
52	1. **🔴 Hard violations** — file:line, operation, why it's unsafe, suggested two-step split.
53	2. **🟡 Concerns** — file:line, operation, suggested change.
54	3. **Rollback check** — for each migration, confirm `downgrade()` is implemented and inverts `upgrade()`.
55	4. **Two-step plan** (if a violation requires it) — outline the staged rollout the user should adopt.
56	5. **✅ Verdict** — one of:
57	   - `Pass — migration is backward-compatible.`
58	   - `Conditional — N concerns. Discuss with whoever runs the deploy.`
59	   - `Block — N hard violations. Must split into two-step rollout before merge.`
60	
61	## Operational note
62	
63	This agent reads migration files and reports — it does NOT modify them. The author splits the migration based on the report. Two-step migrations land as two separate PRs (one per step) per working-agreement #1.
64

+You are the documentation agent for the DataQ project. You have two modes:
+
+1. **Audit mode** — read-only review of docs for consistency, broken links, and staleness. Invoked automatically on doc-touching PRs or on request.
+2. **Generate/update mode** — write or update documentation: scaffold new ADR files, update CLAUDE.md §13 milestone text, add rows to the ADR index, fill in CONTRIBUTING.md gaps. Invoked explicitly by the user ("scaffold the ADR for X", "update the milestone to Week 2", etc.).

+- `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` — new or existing ADR files

+- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — append or patch only; do not restructure
+- `.claude/agents/*.md`, `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` — if explicitly asked to update an agent or skill doc
+
+---
+
+## Audit mode — what you check
+
+Use `gh pr diff <N>` if a PR number is provided. Otherwise read the files directly.
+
+### 🔴 Hard violations (must fix before merge)
+
+1. **CLAUDE.md §6 branch-protection claim vs actual GitHub ruleset.** Run:
+   ```bash
+   gh api repos/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/branches/main/protection 2>/dev/null | jq '{required_reviews: .required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count, enforce_admins: .enforce_admins.enabled, allow_force_pushes: .allow_force_pushes.enabled}'
+   ```
+   Flag any mismatch (e.g., CLAUDE.md says "≥1 review" but ruleset has 0 required approving reviews).
+
+2. **ADR index out of sync.** Every file matching `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` must have a corresponding row in `docs/adr/README.md`. Check both directions:
+   - ADR file exists but not in index → missing index entry.
+   - Index entry references a file that doesn't exist → dangling reference.
+
+3. **CLAUDE.md forward references resolve.** Every relative link in CLAUDE.md (e.g., `[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)`, `[docs/adr/](docs/adr/)`, `[docs/architecture.svg](docs/architecture.svg)`) must point to a file or directory that exists. Use `Glob` or `Bash ls` to verify.
+
+4. **ADR `Superseded by` / `Supersedes` cross-links are bidirectional.** If ADR 0007 says `Supersedes: ADR-0003`, then ADR 0003 must say `Superseded by: ADR-0007`. One-sided links are broken.
+
+5. **Skill and agent files referenced in CLAUDE.md or CONTRIBUTING.md exist.** If the docs mention `.claude/skills/adr-create` or `.claude/agents/orchestration-abstraction-guard`, those paths must be present on disk.
+
+### 🟡 Yellow flags (call out, don't necessarily block)
+
+1. **CLAUDE.md §13 "current milestone" is stale.** If the documented "Current week" and "Current milestone target" describes a week that appears already completed (based on merged PRs or open issues), flag it with a suggested update.
+
+2. **"Pending" ADRs in `docs/adr/README.md` whose target week has passed.** Today's date is available via `date +%Y-%m-%d`. If an ADR listed under "Pending for Week N" still has no file and the week is past, flag it as overdue.
+
+3. **`context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` preamble missing or stale.** The preamble should note where the roadmap has been superseded by ADR decisions (ADF is orchestration not a datasource; Airflow was added post-roadmap; DQX deferred to v1.1). If the roadmap is modified without updating the preamble, flag it.
+
+4. **ADR status inconsistency.** If CLAUDE.md §9 says an ADR status is "Locked W1" but `docs/adr/README.md` says "Pending", flag the disagreement.
+
+5. **Dead working-agreement references.** CLAUDE.md and agent/skill files reference specific working-agreement numbers (e.g., "working-agreement #3", "working-agreement #24"). If `CONTRIBUTING.md` doesn't contain those numbered rules, flag the mismatch.
+
+6. **Section numbering drift in CLAUDE.md.** Agent and skill files hard-link to CLAUDE.md sections (e.g., `CLAUDE.md §11`). If sections are renumbered, those external links go stale.
+
+### 🟢 Acceptable patterns
+
+- ADR in "Proposed" status with no file yet — expected before the target week.
+- Forward ADR numbers reserved in CLAUDE.md §9 as "TBD WN" — placeholders, not dangling refs.
+- Preamble notes in `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` listing superseding decisions.
+- CLAUDE.md §13 correctly describing current in-progress work.
+

+## Generate/update mode — what you can write
+
+### Scaffold a new ADR
+
+Follow the same steps as the `/adr-create` skill:
+
+1. Find the highest `NNNN` in `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md`, increment by 1, zero-pad to 4 digits.
+2. Derive a kebab-case slug from the user's topic (drop articles, lowercase).
+3. Create `docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md` using the standard template (see below).
+4. Add a row to `docs/adr/README.md` index table.
+5. Do **not** commit — stage only. Print next steps.
+
+**ADR template:**
+
+```markdown
+# ADR NNNN — <Human-readable title>
+
+- **Status:** Accepted
+- **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
+- **Deciders:** @<github-handle>
+- **Consulted:** <optional>
+- **Supersedes:** <optional>
+- **Superseded by:** <optional>
+
+## Context
+
+<What problem are we deciding about? 1–3 paragraphs.>
+
+## Decision
+
+**<One-sentence statement of the decision, in bold.>**
+
+<Details: how it works, what's in scope, what's out of scope.>
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive**
+- <bullet>
+
+**Negative**
+- <bullet>
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+- **<Alternative 1>** — rejected. <Why.>
+
+## Related
+
+- <Link to related ADRs, issues, PRs, or code paths.>
+```
+
+Get today's date via `date +%Y-%m-%d`. Get GitHub handle via `gh api /user --jq .login` (prepend `@`). Do not use `git config user.name` — it returns a display name, not an `@mention`.
+
+### Update CLAUDE.md §13 milestone
+
+When the user says "update the milestone to Week N" or "mark PR 0 complete":
+- Read the current §13 block in CLAUDE.md.
+- Edit only the "Current week:", "Current milestone target:", and "Next milestone:" lines.
+- Do not touch any other section.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Add a row to the ADR index
+
+When a new ADR file exists but is missing from `docs/adr/README.md`:
+- Read the current index table.
+- Append a row in the same format as existing rows: `| [NNNN](NNNN-slug.md) | Title | Status | Week |`
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Patch a CONTRIBUTING.md section
+
+When asked to add or update a working agreement:
+- Read the relevant section.
+- Append or edit the numbered rule.
+- Preserve existing numbering — do not renumber unless asked.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Maintain the project TODO list (`docs/TODO.md`)
+
+A single `docs/TODO.md` tracks deferred work items that are not yet GitHub issues — exploratory ideas, known gaps, future-week tasks, and "decide before Week N" reminders.
+
+**Structure of `docs/TODO.md`:**
+
+```markdown
+# DataQ — Project TODO
+
+> Items here are tracked informally. When an item becomes concrete enough to act on,
+> convert it to a GitHub issue via `/gh-issue-from-finding` and remove it from this list.
+
+## Week N — <milestone name>
+
+- [ ] <item> — <short context or owner>
+
+## Backlog (no target week)
+
+- [ ] <item>
+
+## Decided / done (archive — do not delete, just tick)
+
+- [x] <item>
+```
+
+When asked to add, tick, or remove a TODO item:
+- If `docs/TODO.md` doesn't exist, create it with the structure above.
+- Add new items under the correct week section (or "Backlog" if no week is specified).
+- Tick items when the user says they're done; move ticked items to the "Decided / done" section.
+- When an item is promoted to a GitHub issue, note the issue number inline: `→ #N` and tick it.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Scaffold or update a README
+
+When asked to create or update a README for a directory (e.g., `backend/README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `scripts/README.md`):
+
+**Structure for a directory README:**
+
+```markdown
+# <Directory name>
+
+> One-line purpose of this directory.
+
+## What lives here
+
+| File / folder | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| `<path>` | <description> |
+
+## How to use
+
+<Minimal quickstart — one or two commands or steps. Link to CONTRIBUTING.md for the full setup.>
+
+## Related
+
+- <Links to relevant ADRs, CLAUDE.md sections, or other READMEs.>
+```
+
+Rules:
+- Do not duplicate information already in `CLAUDE.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` — link to them instead.
+- Keep it short: the goal is orientation, not a manual.
+- If the directory doesn't exist yet, say so and ask the user to confirm before creating the README.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+### Scaffold future documentation stubs
+
+When a new subsystem is planned but not yet built (e.g., `backend/app/mcp/`, `backend/app/orchestration/`), the user may ask to pre-create a doc stub so the location and intent are clear from day one:
+
+- Create the stub at the expected path (e.g., `docs/mcp-tools.md`).
+- Mark it clearly at the top: `> **Stub — to be filled in Week N.**`
+- Include the section headings the document will eventually need, left empty.
+- Add it to `docs/TODO.md` as a tracked item.
+- Stage the change; do not commit.
+
+---
+
+## How to report (audit mode)
+
+1. **🔴 Hard violations** — file:line, what the doc says, what reality is, required fix.
+2. **🟡 Concerns** — file:line, the inconsistency, suggested update.
+3. **Cross-reference summary** — ADR count in index vs files on disk; CLAUDE.md links checked vs broken.
+4. **✅ Verdict** — one of:
+   - `Pass — documentation is consistent and references resolve.`
+   - `Conditional — N concerns. Update before next milestone starts.`
+   - `Block — N hard violations. Must fix before merge.`
+
+If a finding warrants a deferred GitHub issue, say so explicitly — the engineer can run `/gh-issue-from-finding` to file it per working-agreement #3.
+

## PR #21 — `chore: add docs-consistency-guard subagent`

### Overview

Adds a dual-mode documentation agent that audits docs for consistency/staleness and can generate/update documentation on request. Single file: `.claude/agents/docs-consistency-guard.md` (238 lines added).

---

### Code quality & correctness

**Frontmatter / tooling**
- `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit` — correct. `Write` is needed for new files (`docs/TODO.md`, README stubs, ADR scaffolds). `Edit` is needed for patching existing files. Both are justified.
- `model: sonnet` — consistent with the other two agents.

**ADR scaffold logic**
- The ADR template here duplicates the template in `.claude/skills/adr-create/SKILL.md`. If the template ever evolves, they'll drift. Consider one of:
  - Add a note like `Use the template from .claude/skills/adr-create/SKILL.md` to keep a single source of truth.
  - Or keep the duplicate but add a comment saying "must stay in sync with adr-create/SKILL.md."

**`--body-file` quoting safety**
- The ADR scaffold section says "Stage only; do not commit" but doesn't mention the quoting-safety rule from the `adr-create` skill (use `--body-file` with a temp file when calling `gh issue create`). This agent doesn't call `gh issue create` directly, so it's not a bug — but worth confirming there's no path where this agent creates issues.

**`docs/TODO.md` location**
- Good choice (`docs/` keeps it tracked in git alongside ADRs). The structure — "Decided / done" archive rather than deletion — is exactly right so context is preserved.

**CLAUDE.md §13 edit scope**
- Correctly limits writes to the milestone section only. But the instruction says "Edit only the 'Current week:', 'Current milestone target:', and 'Next milestone:' lines" — CLAUDE.md §13 also has "open blocker issues" text. Might want to add that to the editable lines to avoid it going stale as blockers are filed/closed.

---

### 🟡 Concerns

1. **Duplicate ADR template** — the template block in this agent must stay in sync with `.claude/skills/adr-create/SKILL.md`. The `adr-create` skill is the canonical source; this agent should defer to it or note the sync requirement explicitly.

2. **`docs/TODO.md` isn't mentioned in `CLAUDE.md §12 "Where things live"`** — once this merges and `docs/TODO.md` starts being used, §12 will silently not mention it. Flag for CLAUDE.md update when TODO.md is first created.

3. **Write-scope list may be too narrow** — the agent says writes are limited to `docs/adr/`, `docs/adr/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (§13 only), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `.claude/agents/` + `.claude/skills/`. But the new README and doc stub features write to arbitrary paths like `backend/README.md`, `docs/mcp-tools.md`. The stated write-scope list should be updated to include `docs/*.md` and `<any-dir>/README.md`, or simply state "documentation files only — no `.py`, `.ts`, `.json`, `.yml` code files."

4. **`context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` preamble check (yellow flag #3)** — the check says "if the roadmap is modified without updating the preamble, flag it." But this agent has no write capability for the roadmap preamble — it can only flag it. Worth explicitly saying the fix path is an `Edit` to that file (or filing via `/gh-issue-from-finding`).

5. **No mention of `docs/execution-plan.md`** — CLAUDE.md §12 notes the execution plan will eventually be committed to `docs/execution-plan.md` (still open promise from PR 0). This agent should know to check if that file is missing when auditing §12 forward references.

---

### 🔴 Hard violations

None. The agent is a doc file, not code — no correctness bugs that block merge.

---

### ✅ Verdict

`Conditional — 5 concerns, no hard violations.` Safe to merge; concerns 1 and 3 are the most worth addressing before the agent is actively used.

Surfaced by `/review` on PR #3. **Must land before Week 7 public deployment.**

## Problem

`bug.md` currently bundles security defects under the `critical` severity:
```
- [ ] critical — production down / data loss / security
```

A public GitHub issue for an exploitable vulnerability discloses it before a fix is ready. Once we deploy publicly in Week 7, reporters need a private channel.

## Proposed

1. Split "security" out of the `critical` severity in `bug.md`.
2. Add `.github/SECURITY.md` with a `Reporting a Vulnerability` section pointing to GitHub Security Advisories: https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new
3. (Optional) Add an `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/security.md` that displays a redirect notice and links to the Security Advisories URL.
4. Enable private vulnerability reporting in repo settings (Settings → Security → Private vulnerability reporting).
5. Create a `security` GitHub label for ongoing tracking.

## Why this is a Week 7 blocker
Once the API and `/mcp` endpoint are publicly reachable, external security researchers may find issues. A misconfigured disclosure path either drives them to public-issue disclosure (worst case) or loses the report entirely.

## Problem

`docs/architecture.svg` (and its `<desc>` text) lists only **ADF** under "Azure integrations." Airflow was added as a second orchestration provider during planning (ADR 0004) but the diagram pre-dates that.

Anyone using this diagram as a reference will think only ADF is supported.

## Proposed

Update the SVG:
- Add an Airflow box alongside ADF (same orange "Integrations" color per legend), **or** rename the existing ADF box to "Orchestration (ADF · Airflow)" with both labels.
- Update the `<desc>` text to mention both orchestration providers and the unified `/api/v1/orchestration/events/{provider}` endpoint.
- Preserve the legend grouping (Datasources green, Integrations orange) — it visually reinforces ADR 0004.

## Why this is a Week 2 blocker
Week 2 builds the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with both ADF and Airflow implementations. The diagram is the first thing new contributors look at — if it shows only ADF, they'll write ADF-specific code instead of going through the abstraction.

7	## 1. Project summary
8	
9	**DataQ** is the v1 evolution of SnowQ — a single-tenant data quality monitoring platform built around Great Expectations (GX Core). It runs DQ checks across **4 datasources** and integrates with **2 orchestration providers**.
10	
11	| Layer | Components |
12	|---|---|
13	| **Datasources (you can write checks against)** | Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT), ADLS Gen2, AWS S3, Unity Catalog (Databricks) |
14	| **Orchestration providers (monitor + trigger only — NOT datasources)** | Azure Data Factory (ADF), Apache Airflow |
15	| **Backend** | FastAPI + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL + Alembic |
16	| **Frontend** | React + Vite + Ant Design + Monaco editor |
17	| **Auth / secrets** | Azure AD (MSAL) + Azure Key Vault |
18	| **Deploy** | Azure Container Apps + Azure Static Web App |
19	| **Observability** | Azure Application Insights + structlog |
20	| **AI integration** | FastMCP (8 curated tools mounted at `/mcp`) — Claude Desktop / Claude.ai / Copilot / Cursor |
21	
22	Timeline: **8 weeks** to v1. Scope: single tenant, suite-level access sharing, Azure-hosted.

33	AI clients ──MCP/HTTP──► FastAPI /mcp endpoint      │  └──► Celery worker ──► GX execution ──► Snowflake / ADLS / S3 / UC
34	                                                    │
35	                                                    ├──► Redis (task queue)

88	---
89	
90	## 4. Datasources vs orchestration — critical distinction
91	
92	**Datasources** are stores you write DQ checks against:
93	- Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT)
94	- ADLS Gen2 (flat files)
95	- AWS S3 (flat files)
96	- Unity Catalog / Databricks
97	
98	**Orchestration providers** are NOT datasources. They are workflow engines whose pipelines/DAGs we observe and react to. Their *only* three responsibilities in DataQ:
99	
100	1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table (separate from `runs` / `results`).
101	2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific event channels (webhook for both).
102	3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings` (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `suite_id`, `env`). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs.
103	
104	Both providers implement a single `OrchestrationProvider` interface — ADF is the reference implementation, Airflow is the second. **Never hardcode ADF-only logic; always go through the abstraction.**
105	
106	| Provider | Event channel | Auth | Polling fallback |
107	|---|---|---|---|
108	| ADF | Azure Monitor alert → webhook | Shared secret header (Azure Monitor's only mode) | ADF REST API, 10 min |
109	| Airflow | DAG `on_*_callback` → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns`, 10 min |
110	
111	Airflow callbacks require the user to add a snippet to their DAGs (we can't mutate them). Polling is the documented fallback.
112	
113	**Anti-pattern (do not do this):** treating ADF/Airflow as a 5th/6th datasource in the connection editor, check editor, or suite model.
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 5. Framework choice — GX-only for v1
118	
119	- **v1:** Great Expectations (GX Core) is the sole DQ framework across all 4 datasources. Unifies result schema, suite/check model, MCP tools, and the check editor.
120	- **v1.1:** Databricks Labs **DQX** will be added for DLT / streaming use cases (GX is batch-only and runs poorly on streaming). DQX will implement the same `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` interface introduced in Week 3 — UI exposes `engine: gx | dqx` toggle on UC suites.
121	- **Implication for Week 3:** keep the UC adapter thin behind `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` so v1.1 DQX swap-in doesn't ripple into the suite/check/result layer.
