## MCP tools reference

| Tool / Resource | Type | Description | Example natural language query |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_suites` | resource | All suites accessible to current user — name, datasource, env, last run status, check count | "What suites do I have in QA?" |
| `get_suite_results` | resource | Latest DQ run results for a suite — pass/fail per check, observed vs expected, failing row samples | "What failed in the orders suite today?" |
| `get_health_score` | resource | Overall health score and 7-day trend, filterable by env and datasource | "What's the data health score for QA this week?" |
| `get_adf_pipeline_status` | resource | Latest ADF pipeline run status with correlated DQ result per pipeline | "Did any ADF pipelines fail overnight?" |
| `trigger_suite_run` | tool | Trigger async GX suite execution — returns `run_id` to poll for status | "Run the orders completeness suite on DEV" |
| `get_run_status` | tool | Poll live check-by-check progress for a running execution using `run_id` | "Is the orders run finished yet?" |
| `create_check` | tool | Add a new GX expectation to a suite — form path (check type + column + threshold) or raw SQL | "Add a null check on email to the customer suite" |
| `profile_column` | tool | Run column profiler on a table or file — nulls, distinct count, min/max, top values | "Profile the revenue column in FACT_ORDERS" |

> **Auth:** All MCP tools require a valid Azure AD Bearer token. The same token used for the DataQ web UI works for MCP clients. Configure once in your AI tool of choice — Claude Desktop, Copilot, or Cursor — and all 8 tools are available.

# Code Review — PR #64

## Overview
Pure docs PR: adds `docs/progress.md` (374 lines, task-level mirror of the 100-task roadmap with per-PR status), bumps CLAUDE.md §13 to a headline-only pointer at the new tracker, and adds a PR-template checkbox to enforce the update cadence. **+389/-12 across 3 files. All 10 CI checks green.**

## Correctness ✅
- **Initial state matches reality.** I cross-checked the Week 1 ticks against `git log` — all 5 ✅ entries reference real merged PRs (#37, #39, #41, #53, #56, #63). The 🟡 entries (Key Vault, session refresh, FastAPI conventions) accurately reflect partially-shipped scope.
- **Out-of-roadmap additions are honestly flagged.** Airflow tasks added per ADR 0004 are marked "added per ADR 0004; not in original roadmap" and the aggregate explains "144 > 100 because…". Doesn't fudge the numbers.
- **PR template checkbox + N/A escape hatch** handle both feature PRs (must update) and tooling/docs PRs (tick N/A). Mechanically enforceable; reviewers can see at a glance.
- **CLAUDE.md §13 update is consistent** — switches from listing every PR (which would grow forever) to a pointer + headline, with progress.md as the durable record. Right architecture.
- **PR-template ordering**: the new `docs/progress.md updated` checkbox is grouped with other doc/admin items (`Docs / ADRs updated`, `Security implications`). Good placement.

## Conventions ✅
- ✅ Conventional commit (`docs:`).
- ✅ Verify-locally ran pre-commit clean.
- ✅ Single functionality (the tracker + the enforcement mechanism + the §13 pointer-update are one logical unit — splitting would just create churn).
- ✅ PR body documents the design rationale (why not GitHub Issues/Projects).

## Suggestions / nits (none blocking)
- **Nit:** The aggregate table says `**TOTAL** 6 / 2 / 136 / 144` but the snapshot at the top says "Roadmap tasks done: 7 / 100 (7%)". 6 vs 7 is a one-off — the per-week subtotals show 5 (Week 1) + 1 (Week 8) = 6 ✅, plus the 🟡 entries get half-counted (1.5 in W8). Both numbers are defensible, but they tell different stories. Consider unifying: "Done: 6, In-progress: 2, Pending: 136, Total: 144" everywhere and dropping the "7 / 100 (7%)" line to avoid confusion. Optional — not blocking, can clean up next time the tracker is updated.
- **Nit:** "Active since 2026-05-24" + "Today 2026-05-28" + "calendar burn day 5 of 56" — those two dates will go stale immediately. Consider just keeping the start date + "first PR landed: …" and computing burn at view time, or trusting readers to do the math from git. Minor.
- **Nit:** The "How to update this file" guide says "If the PR added an out-of-roadmap task… add a row with the note." The aggregate table doesn't have an obvious place to track _newly added_ tasks (only the deltas from 100→144 already there). Worth a follow-up if scope keeps shifting.
- **Followable convention but unenforced:** The PR template requires `docs/progress.md updated` *or* N/A. There's no CI check that fails if both are unticked or both are ticked. Acceptable — reviewers catch this. A pre-commit hook that grep'd the body could enforce, but that's overkill.

## Risks
- **Zero runtime risk.** Docs only.
- **Maintenance overhead:** Adds 1–2 minutes per PR to flip ticks + update subtotals. Acceptable trade for the visibility win. If the overhead starts to feel like friction at week 5/6, revisit the GitHub-Issues option.
- **Drift risk if updates lapse:** The tracker only stays useful if every PR updates it. PR template checkbox is the only safeguard. Worth a calendar reminder to audit it weekly during the Friday gate review.

## Verdict
**LGTM — safe to squash-merge.** Honest snapshot, sensible structure, enforcement mechanism in place, CLAUDE.md correctly downgraded to a pointer. Ship it.

- **Math reconciles end-to-end.** Week 4 subtotal 18→19 = +1; aggregate total 144→145 = +1. Pending bucket 136→137. ✅/🟡 counts unchanged at 6/2 (this is a new ⬜ task, not a completion). All four numbers consistent.

## Conventions ✅
- ✅ Conventional commit (`docs(progress):`).

Treat all of the following as the \"diff under review\":\n\n**Backend:**\n- `backend/app/core/auth.py` — Azure AD bearer-token validation + user upsert + dev-bypass mode + fail-closed\n- `backend/app/core/secrets.py` — SecretStore abstraction (Env + Azure Key Vault, lazy-imported)\n- `backend/app/core/config.py` — Settings additions (azure_*, auth_dev_bypass, secret_store, azure_key_vault_url)\n- `backend/app/db/session.py` — get_db() FastAPI dependency generator\n- `backend/app/api/v1/me.py` — GET /api/v1/me endpoint\n- `backend/app/main.py` — async lifespan with init_auth(), request_id middleware\n- `backend/app/core/logging.py` — structlog config + PII redactor\n- `backend/app/core/errors.py` — error envelope + exception handlers\n\n**Frontend:**\n- `frontend/src/auth/config.ts` — VITE_* env-var parsing + authMode computation\n- `frontend/src/auth/msalInstance.ts` — PublicClientApplication singleton (lazy)\n- `frontend/src/auth/MsalProvider.tsx` — wraps tree in real mode, passthrough otherwise\n- `frontend/src/auth/CurrentUserProvider.tsx` + `currentUserContext.ts` + `useCurrentUser.ts`\n- `frontend/src/auth/AuthGate.tsx` — gates children based on mode\n- `frontend/src/api/client.ts` — axios with bearer-token interceptor (acquireTokenSilent)\n- `frontend/src/api/me.ts` — typed fetch\n- `frontend/src/pages/Home.tsx` — useEffect + state machine to load /api/v1/me\n- `frontend/src/main.tsx` — async bootstrap with MSAL lifecycle (initialize → handleRedirectPromise → render)\n\n**Configuration:**\n- `.env.example` — placeholder env-var documentation\n- `pyproject.toml` mypy overrides for azure SDK\n\nFocus areas (high-confidence findings only):\n\n1. **AuthN/AuthZ logic** — fail-open paths, mode-confusion (dev-bypass leaking to prod), missing token validation, scope/audience/issuer bypass.\n2. **Dev bypass triple-gate** — `environment==\"dev\"` && `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true` && Azure vars empty. Is the gate actually safe? Can any env-var manipulation flip it open in staging/prod?\n3. **Lazy Azure SDK import in AzureKeyVaultStore** — any way this fails in a way that returns the env store silently?\n4. **User upsert SQL** — using `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (aad_object_id) DO UPDATE`. Is the conflict target reliable (UNIQUE on `aad_object_id`)? Could a malicious AAD `oid` claim cause data corruption?\n5. **Bearer token attach in frontend** — token stored in MSAL's sessionStorage, attached via interceptor. Any XSS surface that could read it?\n6. **MSAL handleRedirectPromise lifecycle** — fail-loud on error, or fail-silent?\n7. **Frontend authMode evaluated at module load** — could `import.meta.env.DEV` be `true` in a production deploy due to misconfiguration?\n8. **PII redaction in logging** — does the redactor cover claim fields (oid, name, email) that are logged in auth_user_resolved events?\n9. **Error envelope leakage** — do error responses leak stack traces or internal paths?\n10. **Request ID middleware** — caller-supplied X-Request-ID is echoed verbatim. Could a caller use this for log injection?\n\nSkip exclusions (per security-review skill):\n- DoS / rate-limiting / resource exhaustion\n- Pure documentation issues\n- Theoretical race conditions\n- \"Lack of hardening\" without a concrete attack path\n- Log spoofing concerns\n- Dependency version concerns (handled by Dependabot)\n\nOutput format:\n- For each finding: severity (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), file:line, category, description, exploit scenario, fix recommendation, confidence 1-10.\n- Only report confidence ≥ 8.\n- If clean across the surface, say \"No high-confidence findings\" and list what you checked.\n- Under 500 words.\n\nRead the files; do not write. Return the report inline.",

}

## Key invariants

- **Orchestration providers (ADF · Airflow) are not datasources.** They live in `pipeline_runs`, not `runs`. Trigger bindings map `(provider, pipeline_id, env) → suite_id`.
- **GX execution is Celery-only.** FastAPI never calls GX directly; it enqueues tasks.
- **All secrets via Key Vault.** No credentials in env vars or code.

**PR A [#67](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/67) opened.**

## Security audit recap (already done in background)

Two MEDIUM findings worth fixing — **folding into PR E** (observability bundle) since both touch logging / middleware:

1. **PII redactor doesn't cover AAD claim fields.** `auth_user_resolved` logs `aad_oid` and `user_id` at INFO every authenticated request. AAD `oid` is GDPR-identifier-grade. Fix: extend `_PII_KEYS` to `{oid, aad_oid, aad_object_id, upn, preferred_username, user_id, name, display_name}` or hash them.
2. **Caller-supplied `X-Request-ID` is echoed unvalidated.** No length cap, no charset whitelist. 10KB+ values bloat every log line for the request. Fix: validate against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$`; on mismatch, generate fresh UUID.

Otherwise clean: dev-bypass triple gate verified safe, fail-closed enforced, `_upsert_user` UNIQUE constraint correct, lazy AKV import correctly raises rather than silently falls back, error envelope doesn't leak stack traces, MSAL bootstrap fails loud.

Ping when PR #67 CI is green and I'll review + merge, then start PR B (#54 mypy dep consolidation).

# Code Review — PR #67

## Overview
Cleanup PR removing 6 "no source yet" defensive branches + 1 `continue-on-error: true` bandage from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, plus three doc-consistency fixes from this session's docs-guard audit, plus a new stub `README.md`. **+53/-40 across 5 files. All 10 CI checks green** — including CodeQL, which is the key signal because that's the job that was previously bandaged.

## Correctness ✅

- **The CI changes are the high-signal piece.** All six conditional steps now invoke their tool directly (`black --check backend/`, `mypy backend/app/`, etc.). With `backend/`, `backend/app/`, `backend/tests/`, and `frontend/src/` all populated, the `if [ -d ... ]` branches are dead. CI passes on this PR — that's positive proof the un-bandaged paths run cleanly.
- **CodeQL `continue-on-error: true` removed.** Comment on that line explicitly said `# no source yet; remove once backend/frontend code lands` — the trigger condition is met. CodeQL now blocks merge on real findings going forward. The fact that CodeQL passes on this PR's diff also confirms there are no pending CodeQL issues to surface.
- **CLAUDE.md §12 dangling reference fix is clean.** Replaced the never-committed `docs/execution-plan.md` row with a pointer to `docs/progress.md`. Same intent (where the live execution status lives), correct target.
- **`README.md` stub is well-scoped.** Stack summary table, quick-start (`./scripts/setup.sh` + `docker-compose up`), doc index, license pointer. Doesn't overpromise; correctly notes "pre-v1 — Week 1 in progress." Every link target exists on disk (verified: CONTRIBUTING.md ✓, CLAUDE.md ✓, docs/architecture.md ✓, docs/adr/ ✓, docs/progress.md ✓, context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md ✓, .github/SECURITY.md ✓).
- **Architecture invariant softening is honest.** The old absolute statement contradicted the `EnvSecretStore` shipped in PR 3b. New wording correctly scopes Key Vault to prod/staging and surfaces the dev env-var path. Cross-references the secrets.py file for the receipts.
- **docs/progress.md snapshot bump.** "Out-of-roadmap PRs landed" 4→5 — accurate accounting per the tracker's own convention.

## Conventions ✅
- ✅ Conventional commit (`chore:`).
- ✅ Pre-commit clean.
- ✅ PR template's `docs/progress.md updated` checkbox ticked (snapshot count bumped).
- ✅ One logical unit: "PR 3 follow-ups" — all changes derive from "now that PR 3 landed real code, what bandages and doc claims are stale?"
- ✅ Explicitly defers the two security findings to PR E (the observability bundle) with a one-line note in the PR body — proper scope hygiene.

## Suggestions / nits
- **Nit (non-blocking):** the new README's footnote points to `[LICENSE](LICENSE)` but I didn't verify a `LICENSE` file exists at the repo root. If it doesn't, that's a tiny dangling link. (The original commit history mentions LICENSE as the only file in the repo before any code landed, so likely fine.)
- **Nit (non-blocking):** the README's "Status" line says "pre-v1 — Week 1 in progress." Will go stale weekly. Pointing at `docs/progress.md` for live status is fine; the static phrase is acceptable for now.
- **Nit (non-blocking):** the new architecture invariant text references "ADR 0009 layout note" — ADR 0009 is the flat-monorepo decision, not a secrets/KV decision. The pointer makes sense as "see architectural-decisions index" but a reader might find it less immediate than just `backend/app/core/secrets.py` (which is also referenced). Minor — the file ref is the load-bearing one.

## Risks
- **Zero runtime risk** to backend or frontend.
- **CI risk: now lower**, not higher. The un-bandaged jobs explicitly proved they pass on this PR; removing the bandages can only fail-loud on future regressions, which is what you want.
- **CodeQL risk: now correct.** The job is no longer suppressed. If future code introduces a real CodeQL finding, merge blocks. That's the intended security posture.

## Verdict
**LGTM — safe to squash-merge.** Clean cleanup, doc fixes are reality-aligned, the new README is minimal and accurate. The CodeQL un-suppression is the highest-value change in this PR.

**PR B [#68](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/68) opened.**

## What this fixes
- `backend/requirements-typecheck.txt` — single source of truth (one file to update for new runtime imports)
- CI installs `pip install -r backend/requirements-typecheck.txt` in both type-check + test jobs
- `scripts/check-typecheck-deps.py` — diffs the YAML against the txt, exits 1 on drift with clear "only in X / only in Y" message
- Pre-commit `typecheck-deps-sync` local hook runs the script — catches drift locally **and** in CI (via the lint job)
- Verified: positive (sync clean) + negative (added `fake-pkg`, hook correctly failed)

So new contributors update 2 files; if they forget one, the hook stops them before push. **Down from 4 places with no enforcement to 2 places with automated enforcement.**

@@ -0,0 +1,91 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verify .pre-commit-config.yaml mypy hook deps == backend/requirements-typecheck.txt.
+
+Run as a pre-commit local hook (typecheck-deps-sync) to catch drift before push.
+Also runnable directly: `python scripts/check-typecheck-deps.py`.
+
+Exit code:
+    0 — lists are in sync
+    1 — drift detected (with diff printed to stderr)
+    2 — could not parse one of the files (config error)
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+REQS_FILE = REPO_ROOT / "backend" / "requirements-typecheck.txt"
+PRECOMMIT_FILE = REPO_ROOT / ".pre-commit-config.yaml"
+
+# Match the mirrors-mypy hook block + its additional_dependencies sub-list.
+_MYPY_DEPS_RE = re.compile(
+    r"mirrors-mypy.*?additional_dependencies:\s*\n((?:\s*-\s*[^\n]+\n)+)",
+    re.DOTALL,
+)
+
+
+def _parse_requirements_txt(path: Path) -> set[str]:
+    """Return the pinned packages from a requirements.txt (skip comments + blanks)."""
+    out: set[str] = set()
+    for raw in path.read_text().splitlines():
+        line = raw.strip()
+        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        out.add(line)
+    return out
+
+
+def _parse_precommit_mypy_deps(path: Path) -> set[str]:
+    """Return additional_dependencies entries from the mirrors-mypy hook."""
+    match = _MYPY_DEPS_RE.search(path.read_text())
+    if not match:
+        print(
+            f"ERROR: could not find mirrors-mypy additional_dependencies block in {path}",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+        sys.exit(2)
+    out: set[str] = set()
+    for raw in match.group(1).splitlines():
+        line = raw.strip()
+        if line.startswith("- "):
+            out.add(line[2:].strip())
+    return out
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    reqs = _parse_requirements_txt(REQS_FILE)
+    precommit = _parse_precommit_mypy_deps(PRECOMMIT_FILE)
+
+    only_reqs = reqs - precommit
+    only_precommit = precommit - reqs
+
+    if not only_reqs and not only_precommit:
+        return 0
+
+    print(

# Code Review — PR #68

## Overview
Fixes #54 — the 3-file drift trap that caused two CI failures during PR 3 (forgotten fastapi-azure-auth in CI's mypy job, forgotten pydantic/structlog in the test job). Establishes `backend/requirements-typecheck.txt` as the single source of truth; CI installs from it; a pre-commit local hook enforces that the YAML `additional_dependencies` list never drifts from the txt. **+132/-18 across 6 files. All 10 CI checks green** — including the new `typecheck-deps-sync` hook in the lint job.

## Correctness ✅

- **The fix actually closes the trap.** Before: 4 lists (env.yml, pre-commit YAML, CI type-check job, CI test job). After: 2 lists (the txt + the YAML) with automated enforcement that they agree. Lockstep guaranteed by a hook that fires on either file changing. Adding a new runtime import now: update one file (the txt) → pre-commit fails until you update the YAML → done.
- **The CI passes on this PR.** Including the new `typecheck-deps-sync` hook (run by the lint job's `pre-commit run --all-files` equivalent), so we have positive proof both reads work.
- **Drift was actually present pre-PR and got fixed silently.** Old CI type-check job had `celery==5.6.3`; the pre-commit YAML did not. Neither was wrong (backend doesn't import celery yet), but it was real drift. The new txt drops celery — both sides now consistent. Good cleanup as a side-effect.
- **Negative test recorded in PR body.** Appending `fake-pkg==1.0.0` made the sync hook fail with the documented "Only in requirements-typecheck.txt" error. Reverted. Means the enforcement actually fires.
- **The regex parser is robust enough.** `mirrors-mypy.*?additional_dependencies:\s*\n((?:\s*-\s*[^\n]+\n)+)` correctly captures the YAML block. The non-greedy `.*?` between `mirrors-mypy` and `additional_dependencies` won't span hook boundaries because the line-start `additional_dependencies:` only appears under the mypy hook. Tolerates indentation changes.
- **Pre-commit hook scope is right.** `files: ^(backend/requirements-typecheck\.txt|\.pre-commit-config\.yaml)$` runs only when one of the two files actually changes. No wasted runs.
- **Stdlib-only script.** No new dependencies, no chicken-and-egg problem on a fresh clone before conda env exists.

## Conventions ✅
- ✅ Conventional commit (`fix(ci):`).
- ✅ `Fixes #54` properly attributed — auto-closes on merge.
- ✅ Pre-commit clean before push.
- ✅ One-functionality-per-commit.
- ✅ CONTRIBUTING.md rule 21 updated to reflect the new workflow (CONTRIBUTING.md was the rule that previously warned about the manual 3-file sync; the rule's text is now in lockstep with code reality).
- ✅ `docs/progress.md` updated (strike-through #54 row + PR link).
- ✅ Script is executable (chmod +x).
- ✅ Comments at the top of the txt explain the consumer relationships explicitly.

## Suggestions / nits (none blocking)
- **Nit:** the txt allows a leading `#` to look like Python — fine, but pip treats any line containing `#` *after* the package as inline comment too. Currently no inline comments used. Worth noting if anyone tries to add `# windows-only` style annotations later.
- **Nit:** the regex parser assumes `mirrors-mypy` appears only once in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (currently true). If we ever add a second mypy hook (e.g., one for `scripts/`), the regex would only match the first; document if that case arises.
- **Nit:** the sync hook runs even if only the YAML's *unrelated* sections changed (e.g., adding a new gitleaks rev). Acceptable — the hook is fast (parses two small files) — but tightening to `files` paths that only contain the mypy block isn't really feasible with YAML.
- **Nit (forward-looking):** when Week 8 brings actual test fixtures that need additional runtime deps (e.g., `httpx-mock`, `respx`), they'd also need to land in the txt. The file's purpose statement ("Type-checking + test-import requirements") covers that. Fine.

## Risks
- **Zero runtime risk.** Tooling-only.
- **CI risk: lower.** Previously, CI mypy job could quietly miss a dep and produce false-positive failures on the next PR. Now drift is caught locally + in CI before push.
- **Maintenance risk: lower.** One workflow ("edit txt → fix YAML when the hook tells you to") vs four files no one remembered.
- **Lock-in risk: nil.** The pattern is reversible at any time; if pre-commit ever gains native `-r requirements.txt` support for `additional_dependencies`, we could collapse to a single file.

## Verdict
**LGTM — safe to squash-merge.** Clean engineering of a real maintenance pain. The sync hook + negative-test verification + CONTRIBUTING.md update give this the long half-life it deserves. Closes #54 properly.

# Code Review — PR #69

## Overview
Adds `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` to silence two recurring CodeQL false positives (Alembic globals, Protocol `...` stub bodies). Switches the CodeQL action from inline `queries: security-and-quality` to `config-file:`. The config inherits the same query suite. **+26/-2 across 3 files. All 10 CI checks green — including CodeQL itself**, which is the key signal because that's the job we're reconfiguring.

## Correctness ✅

- **The reconfiguration is wire-correct.** CodeQL CI passes on this PR's diff, confirming the action successfully parses and applies the custom config file. If the path or schema were wrong, this job would have failed.
- **`paths-ignore` scope is right.** `backend/alembic/**` matches both `versions/*.py` and `env.py` — both file types had findings in PR #41. No risk of over-matching (`backend/alembic/` is exclusively migration territory).
- **`query-filters: exclude` for `py/ineffectual-statement` is the only safe rule to drop.** It's the rule that fired on Protocol stubs (verified by inspection of the PR #56 review threads). Other `py/*` quality rules remain active.
- **Safety net for the excluded rule is concrete.** Ruff's `B018` is already active in `pyproject.toml`'s `tool.ruff.lint.select` (`"B"` set includes B018). The PR body has the sanity-check transcript:
  - `1 + 1` body → B018 fires ✓
  - Protocol `...` body → B018 silent ✓

  This is the right test because it proves both directions: we still catch real no-ops AND we no longer block on the idiom.
- **`security-and-quality` query suite preserved.** Custom config doesn't downgrade to `security-extended` or anything narrower — we only exclude one rule.
- **Comments in the config file are load-bearing.** They explain *why* each exclusion exists with concrete code examples. Future contributors will understand the trade-offs without spelunking issue #43.

## Conventions ✅
- ✅ Conventional commit (`fix(ci):`).
- ✅ `Fixes #43` properly attributed.
- ✅ Pre-commit clean (including `check-yaml` on the new config file).
- ✅ Single functionality (CodeQL config) — no piggybacked changes.
- ✅ `docs/progress.md` updated (strike-through + PR link) per the cadence rule.

## Suggestions / nits (none blocking)
- **Nit:** consider adding `pull-requests: read` to the CodeQL job's `permissions:` block if you ever want PR-comment annotations. Not relevant today; current permissions (`security-events: write`, `actions: read`, `contents: read`) are sufficient for the SARIF upload.
- **Nit:** for completeness, the JS/TS matrix branch also reads this config now. There are no JS-specific filters, but if the frontend ever generates similar false positives (e.g., React forwardRef stubs), this is the file to extend. Worth noting in a brief code comment? Optional — the existing comments scope themselves to Python and that's accurate today.
- **Nit (forward-looking):** if a future PR drops or replaces ruff's B-rule set, the safety net for `py/ineffectual-statement` evaporates silently. Worth a `# require_ruff: B018` style comment in `pyproject.toml`'s ruff config? Probably overkill — CONTRIBUTING.md rule 20 says ruff is locked.

## Risks
- **Zero runtime risk** to backend or frontend.
- **CI risk: lower.** Genuine CodeQL findings still block merge (we only excluded a single rule and a single path). False positives on migrations + Protocols are eliminated. Net: more signal, less noise.
- **Lock-in risk: nil.** Removing the config file or restoring inline `queries: security-and-quality` returns to the prior behavior in one diff.

## Verdict
**LGTM — safe to squash-merge.** Right-sized fix, well-documented trade-offs, safety net verified end-to-end. The Alembic + Protocol-stub merge friction we hit on PR #41 and #56 is gone for future PRs.

# Code Review — PR #70

## Overview
Adds 8 FK-column indexes to address #42. SQLAlchemy `Index()` declarations land in `backend/app/db/models.py`; Alembic autogenerate produced a clean forward-and-back migration. **+74/-1 across 3 files. All 10 CI checks green.**

## Correctness ✅

- **All 8 indexes match the model declarations exactly.** Each `Index(...)` in `models.py` has a corresponding `op.create_index(...)` in the migration, and the migration's `downgrade()` drops them in reverse order. Names follow the project's `ix_<table>_<column>` naming convention from `backend/app/db/base.py`.
- **Roundtrip verification** (recorded in PR body): up → 13 indexes, down → 5, up again → 13. Confirms forward and backward both work and are idempotent across re-runs.
- **The 2 columns added beyond #42's list (`results.check_id`, `shares.user_id`) are correctly identified.** I cross-checked both:
  - `results.check_id`: FK to `checks.id`, no existing index. Correct add.
  - `shares.user_id`: FK to `users.id`. Existing `uq_shares_suite_user(suite_id, user_id)` covers `suite_id` lookups (leftmost prefix), not `user_id` lookups. Correct add.
- **The 5 FK columns explicitly *not* added are correctly identified as covered:**
  - `runs.suite_id` → `ix_runs_suite_id` ✓
  - `results.run_id` → `ix_results_run_id` ✓
  - `shares.suite_id` → `uq_shares_suite_user` leftmost ✓
  - `pipeline_runs.provider/pipeline_or_dag_id` → `ix_pipeline_runs_provider_pipeline` ✓
  - `trigger_bindings.(provider,pipeline_or_dag_id,env)` → `ix_trigger_bindings_provider_pipeline_env` ✓
- **`Suite` and `Check` now have `__table_args__`** for the first time; both follow the trailing-comma tuple form required for single-element `__table_args__` (`(Index(...),)`). Correct Python syntax — easy to get wrong; this got it right.
- **Existing 12 pytest tests still pass.** Schema additions are pure-add; no test fixture or seed data needed updating.

## Conventions ✅
- ✅ Conventional commit (`fix(db):`).
- ✅ `Fixes #42` properly attributed.
- ✅ Pre-commit clean (Black + Ruff + mypy + typecheck-deps-sync + the new CodeQL config from PR C all pass).
- ✅ Migration docstring is exceptional — explains *why* it's backward-compatible (read-side metadata, no data rewrites), what the production-mode path looks like (`postgresql_concurrently=True`, disable transactional DDL), and lists all 8 columns. Future contributor can answer "should I revisit this for prod?" without spelunking the PR.
- ✅ `docs/progress.md` updated (strike-through + PR link) — PR template checkbox honored.
- ✅ Migration revision linkage correct: `Revises: 923dab15eb8c` is the PR 2c baseline ID.

## Performance
- ✅ **Net win.** 8 additional B-tree indexes on FK columns where Postgres would otherwise sequential-scan. Trade-off (write-amplification on INSERT/UPDATE of these tables) is irrelevant given the DataQ workload: writes per row are O(1), reads/joins/cascades are the dominant query pattern (suite listings, results dashboards, share lookups).
- ⚠️ **Production-mode `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` switch is documented but not implemented.** Acceptable today (DB is empty), risky if anyone deploys this against a populated dev environment without reading the docstring. The migration docstring is the primary mitigation; PR body also calls it out.

## Security
- ✅ **No security implications.** Pure read-side metadata. No new attack surface, no auth/AuthZ change, no data exposure.

## Suggestions / nits (none blocking)
- **Nit (non-blocking):** the migration body retains the autogen boilerplate comments (`### commands auto generated by Alembic - please adjust! ###`). Some teams strip these once they've reviewed; others leave them. Leaving them is the safer default — they signal future contributors that the body originated from autogen.
- **Nit (non-blocking):** the docstring says `postgresql_using='btree'` for the production path. Btree is the default in Postgres, so the explicit `using=` is optional — but it's harmless and clarifies intent. Fine as-is.
- **Nit (forward-looking):** when Week 4 schema additions land (severity tier columns on `checks`), if any new FK arises, the same pattern applies — easy to forget. The progress.md tracker should call this out as a Week 3 Day 1 reminder.

## Risks
- **Zero runtime risk.** Backward-compatible.
- **Zero CI risk.** Tests pass; CodeQL `paths-ignore: backend/alembic/**` (from PR C) keeps the migration out of CodeQL's noise zone.
- **Operational risk in prod (future):** if the production run forgets the CONCURRENTLY switch, each `CREATE INDEX` takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock briefly. With 8 indexes on tables that may be hot, that could mean short query freezes. Docstring is the mitigation; no current data so not a today-risk.

## Verdict
**LGTM — safe to squash-merge.** Comprehensive coverage of FK indexing, including the two columns #42 missed; clean roundtrip-verified migration; docstring captures the production-mode handoff; all tests pass. Closes #42.

41	        return value

  "old_string": "def configure_logging() -> None:\n    settings = get_settings()\n    level = getattr(logging, settings.log_level)\n\n    logging.basicConfig(\n        format=\"%(message)s\",\n        stream=sys.stdout,\n        level=level,\n    )\n\n    conn = settings.applicationinsights_connection_string\n    if conn:\n        from opencensus.ext.azure.log_exporter import AzureLogHandler\n\n        handler = AzureLogHandler(connection_string=conn)\n        handler.setLevel(level)\n        logging.getLogger().addHandler(handler)\n\n    shared_processors: list[Processor] = [\n        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,\n        _add_request_id,\n        structlog.processors.add_log_level,\n        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt=\"iso\", utc=True),\n        _redact_pii,\n    ]\n\n    structlog.configure(\n        processors=[\n            *shared_processors,\n            structlog.processors.dict_tracebacks,\n            structlog.processors.JSONRenderer(),\n        ],\n        wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(level),\n        logger_factory=structlog.stdlib.LoggerFactory(),\n        cache_logger_on_first_use=True,\n    )",
  "new_string": "def configure_logging() -> None:\n    settings = get_settings()\n    level = getattr(logging, settings.log_level)\n\n    shared_processors: list[Processor] = [\n        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,\n        _add_request_id,\n        structlog.processors.add_log_level,\n        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt=\"iso\", utc=True),\n        _redact_pii,\n    ]\n\n    # Bridge stdlib logging (uvicorn.access, uvicorn.error, etc.) through the\n    # same processor chain so every line out of the app is JSON with a\n    # request_id when available. Without this the uvicorn access log emits\n    # human-readable text that App Insights can't correlate (#50).\n    formatter = structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter(\n        foreign_pre_chain=shared_processors,\n        processors=[\n            structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter.remove_processors_meta,\n            structlog.processors.dict_tracebacks,\n            structlog.processors.JSONRenderer(),\n        ],\n    )\n\n    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)\n    handler.setFormatter(formatter)\n    root = logging.getLogger()\n    root.handlers = [handler]\n    root.setLevel(level)\n\n    # Detach uvicorn's pre-configured handlers; let logs propagate to root so\n    # they hit the structlog ProcessorFormatter above.\n    for name in (\"uvicorn\", \"uvicorn.access\", \"uvicorn.error\"):\n        uvicorn_logger = logging.getLogger(name)\n        uvicorn_logger.handlers = []\n        uvicorn_logger.propagate = True\n\n    conn = settings.applicationinsights_connection_string\n    if conn:\n        from opencensus.ext.azure.log_exporter import AzureLogHandler\n\n        ai_handler = AzureLogHandler(connection_string=conn)\n        ai_handler.setLevel(level)\n        root.addHandler(ai_handler)\n\n    structlog.configure(\n        processors=[\n            *shared_processors,\n            structlog.processors.dict_tracebacks,\n            structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter.wrap_for_formatter,\n        ],\n        wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(level),\n        logger_factory=structlog.stdlib.LoggerFactory(),\n        cache_logger_on_first_use=True,\n    )"
}

  "old_string": "@app.middleware(\"http\")\nasync def request_id_middleware(\n    request: Request, call_next: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]]\n) -> Response:\n    rid = request.headers.get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER) or uuid.uuid4().hex\n    token = request_id_var.set(rid)\n    try:\n        response = await call_next(request)\n    finally:\n        request_id_var.reset(token)\n    response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = rid\n    return response",
  "new_string": "@app.middleware(\"http\")\nasync def request_id_middleware(\n    request: Request, call_next: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]]\n) -> Response:\n    incoming = request.headers.get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER)\n    rid = incoming if incoming and _REQUEST_ID_RE.match(incoming) else uuid.uuid4().hex\n    token = request_id_var.set(rid)\n    start = time.perf_counter()\n    try:\n        response = await call_next(request)\n    except Exception:\n        elapsed_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2)\n        _log.exception(\n            \"request_failed\",\n            method=request.method,\n            path=request.url.path,\n            duration_ms=elapsed_ms,\n        )\n        request_id_var.reset(token)\n        raise\n    elapsed_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2)\n    _log.info(\n        \"request\",\n        method=request.method,\n        path=request.url.path,\n        status=response.status_code,\n        duration_ms=elapsed_ms,\n    )\n    request_id_var.reset(token)\n    response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = rid\n    return response"
}

FastAPI lifespan runs configure_logging(); avoid re-running it for tests\n    # by entering the context manually under TestClient.\n    with TestClient(app) as c:\n        yield c\n\n\n# ───────────────────────── X-Request-ID validation ─────────────────────────\n\n\ndef test_request_id_generated_when_caller_omits(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    response = client.get(\"/healthz\")\n    rid = response.headers.get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER)\n    assert rid is not None\n    # uuid4().hex is 32 lowercase hex chars\n    assert len(rid) == 32\n    assert all(c in \"0123456789abcdef\" for c in rid)\n\n\ndef test_request_id_echoed_when_valid(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    response = client.get(\"/healthz\", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: \"trace-abc.123_XYZ\"})\n    assert response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] == \"trace-abc.123_XYZ\"\n\n\ndef test_request_id_replaced_when_too_long(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Caller-supplied IDs over 64 chars are rejected (security audit #2).\"\"\"\n    too_long = \"a\" * 65\n    response = client.get(\"/healthz\", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: too_long})\n    echoed = response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER]\n    assert echoed != too_long\n    assert len(echoed) == 32  # fresh uuid\n\n\ndef test_request_id_replaced_on_bad_chars(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Caller-supplied IDs containing whitespace or JSON-control chars are rejected.\"\"\"\n    for bad in ['inject\"quote', \"with space\", \"tab\\there\", \"semi;colon\"]:\n        response = client.get(\"/healthz\", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: bad})\n        echoed = response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER]\n        assert echoed != bad\n        assert len(echoed) == 32\n\n\ndef test_request_id_replaced_on_empty(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    response = client.get(\"/healthz\", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: \"\"})\n    echoed = response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER]\n    assert len(echoed) == 32\n\n\n# ───────────────────────── per-request structured log ─────────────────────────\n\n\ndef test_per_request_log_emitted_on_success(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    \"\"\"#51: every successful request emits one event=request structlog entry.\"\"\"\n    with structlog.testing.capture_logs() as cap:\n        client.get(\"/healthz\", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: \"trace-1\"})\n    request_events = [e for e in cap if e.get(\"event\") == \"request\"]\n    assert len(request_events) == 1\n    evt = request_events[0]\n    assert evt[\"method\"] == \"GET\"\n    assert evt[\"path\"] == \"/healthz\"\n    assert evt[\"status\"] == 200\n    assert isinstance(evt[\"duration_ms\"], int | float)\n    assert evt[\"duration_ms\"] >= 0\n\n\ndef test_per_request_log_uses_validated_request_id(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The structlog event should carry the validated rid in the contextvar.\"\"\"\n    with structlog.testing.capture_logs() as cap:\n        client.get(\"/healthz\", headers={REQUEST_ID_HEADER: \"trace-validated\"})\n    # The captured-logs harness inspects the bound contextvars on each event.\n    request_events = [e for e in cap if e.get(\"event\") == \"request\"]\n    assert request_events\n    # The middleware's _log.info(\"request\", ...) fires while the contextvar\n    # is set; structlog.testing.capture_logs ignores processor side-effects\n    # so we can only assert the event was emitted. Header round-trip already\n    # proves the rid plumbing in the validation test above.\n"
}

  "command": "gh pr create --title \"feat(observability): per-request log + uvicorn bridge + PII / rid hardening (#50 #51)\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Summary\n\nCloses the observability bundle and addresses the two medium-confidence findings from the 2026-05-28 security audit. All four changes land in one PR because they touch the same files (logging.py + main.py middleware) and are best reviewed together.\n\n| # | Finding / Issue | Type | Fix |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Audit finding 1 | **MEDIUM** | Extend PII redactor for Azure AD claim fields |\n| 2 | Audit finding 2 | **MEDIUM** | Validate X-Request-ID before echoing |\n| 3 | #51 | feat | Per-request structured log from request_id middleware |\n| 4 | #50 | feat | Bridge uvicorn access logs through structlog |\n\nFixes #50. Fixes #51.\n\n## What lands\n\n### Security: PII redactor extension (audit finding 1)\n- \\`_PII_KEYS\\` extended with 8 Azure AD claim fields: \\`oid\\`, \\`aad_oid\\`, \\`aad_object_id\\`, \\`upn\\`, \\`preferred_username\\`, \\`user_id\\`, \\`name\\`, \\`display_name\\`.\n- Rationale: AAD object IDs are GDPR-grade personal data (Article 4(1)). \\`auth_user_resolved\\` logs them at INFO; without redaction they ship to App Insights / stdout in clear text on every authenticated request, building a directory of every active user's AAD OID.\n\n### Security: X-Request-ID validation (audit finding 2)\n- Caller-supplied header validated against \\`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$\\` before being:\n  - Bound to \\`request_id_var\\` (and therefore stamped on every structlog event for the request).\n  - Echoed in the response header.\n- Mismatch → fresh \\`uuid4().hex\\`. Prevents log-line pollution (10KB+ inputs inflating log storage) and SIEM dashboard corruption (JSON-control chars breaking naive parsers).\n\n### Observability: per-request structured log (#51)\n- \\`request_id_middleware\\` now emits \\`event=request\\` after every successful request: \\`method\\`, \\`path\\`, \\`status\\`, \\`duration_ms\\`, \\`request_id\\`.\n- Failed requests emit \\`event=request_failed\\` with traceback before re-raising.\n- Foundational for Week 6 dashboards and Week 7 App Insights wiring.\n\n### Observability: uvicorn → structlog bridge (#50)\n- \\`configure_logging()\\` installs a \\`structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter\\` on the root logger so stdlib log records (uvicorn.access, uvicorn.error, httpx, etc.) flow through the same processor chain as structlog events: timestamp, level, request_id, PII redaction, JSON renderer.\n- Result: every line out of the app is JSON with \\`request_id\\` when in request scope. App Insights ingestion + log aggregators can join the access log to handler-emitted logs by \\`request_id\\` for the first time.\n\n## Tests (12 new — 24 total)\n- \\`backend/tests/core/test_logging.py\\` — 5 tests:\n  - Credentials + personal contact PII redacted\n  - Azure AD claim fields redacted (per audit)\n  - Nested dicts walked correctly\n  - Lists of dicts walked correctly\n  - Safe keys (method, status, level, duration_ms) pass through\n- \\`backend/tests/test_main.py\\` — 7 tests:\n  - Auto-generated request_id when caller omits\n  - Caller-supplied valid id echoed\n  - Too-long (>64 char) rejected and replaced\n  - Bad-char (quote, space, tab, semi) rejected and replaced\n  - Empty header replaced\n  - Per-request log emission on success\n  - Per-request log carries the validated (not raw) rid\n\nCoverage on touched files: \\`logging.py\\` 90%, \\`main.py\\` 90%. Total backend: **85%**.\n\n## E2E verified against the running stack\n- Valid \\`e2e-trace-001\\` → echoed verbatim\n- 100-char input → replaced with 32-char hex\n- \\`inject\"quote\\` → replaced with 32-char hex\n- Uvicorn access log now JSON: \\`{\"event\": \"127.0.0.1:52541 - \\\\\"GET /api/v1/me HTTP/1.1\\\\\" 200\", \"level\": \"info\", ...}\\`\n- Per-request event: \\`{\"method\": \"GET\", \"path\": \"/api/v1/me\", \"status\": 200, \"duration_ms\": 38.77, \"event\": \"request\", \"request_id\": \"5f49607f92e04983aa7fdc850d5e290a\", \"level\": \"info\", \"timestamp\": \"...\"}\\`\n\n## Notes\n\n- Test uses \\`caplog\\` (stdlib logging records) instead of \\`structlog.testing.capture_logs()\\` because the module-level \\`_log = get_logger(__name__)\\` in main.py is cached at import time before tests can install structlog's capture harness. \\`caplog\\` works because structlog's stdlib bridge routes records through stdlib logging anyway. Trade-off acceptable; behavior is what we assert.\n- \\`conftest.py\\` now sets \\`AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true\\` + \\`ENVIRONMENT=dev\\` at import time so the TestClient lifespan doesn't raise on missing AAD config.\n- \\`backend/app/db/models.py\\` and \\`backend/app/db/base.py\\` are now at 100% coverage thanks to model introspection during TestClient lifespan.\n\n## docs/progress.md updated checkbox: ✅ — #50 and #51 struck through with PR link.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\nEOF\n)\"",

# Code Review — PR #71

## Overview
Closes the observability bundle (#50, #51) and addresses the two MEDIUM findings from the 2026-05-28 security audit: extends the PII redactor for Azure AD claim fields, validates the `X-Request-ID` header before echoing, emits a per-request structured log from the middleware, and bridges stdlib logging (uvicorn) through structlog so every line out of the app is JSON. **+307/-20 across 8 files. All 10 CI checks green.**

## Correctness

### ✅ Solid

- **PII redactor extension is comprehensive.** Adds the full set of AAD claim fields (`oid`, `aad_oid`, `aad_object_id`, `upn`, `preferred_username`, `user_id`, `name`, `display_name`) called out in the audit. Organized into three commented groups (credentials, personal contact, AAD claims) — makes the rationale legible for future contributors.
- **X-Request-ID validation is right-sized.** `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$` allows the standard distributed-trace ID alphabets (uuid hex, base64-url, dashed-uuid, vendor traceparent fragments) while rejecting whitespace, quotes, semicolons, and control chars. Length cap of 64 matches W3C trace context conventions.
- **Middleware flow is correct on both paths.** Success: log `event=request` with method/path/status/duration_ms, reset ContextVar, set response header, return. Exception: log `event=request_failed` with `log.exception` (captures traceback), reset ContextVar, re-raise. The `_REQUEST_ID_RE.match` check is anchored at start; combined with `+` quantifier it correctly rejects empty strings.
- **Uvicorn bridge wiring is correct.** Detach pre-configured handlers from `uvicorn`, `uvicorn.access`, `uvicorn.error`; set `propagate=True`; install a single `StreamHandler(sys.stdout)` on root with the structlog `ProcessorFormatter`. `foreign_pre_chain=shared_processors` runs the timestamp + level + request_id + PII redaction on stdlib records before the JSON renderer. structlog's own log calls go through `wrap_for_formatter` so they're recognized as pre-processed and only get the JSON render step.
- **`ProcessorFormatter.remove_processors_meta` correctly inserted** so the `_record` and `_from_structlog` metadata don't bleed into the JSON output. Good catch.
- **Conftest sets env vars at module-load time** (`os.environ.setdefault` before the backend imports), with `# noqa: E402` on the deferred imports. This is the right pattern — `auth.py` computes its mode at import time, so the env must be set *before* any backend import.
- **E2E smoke recorded in PR body** shows the actual JSON output for all four behaviors (valid id echo, too-long replace, bad-char replace, JSON-formatted uvicorn access log). Concrete evidence the design works end-to-end.

### ⚠️ Worth noting (not blockers)

- **Module-level `_log = get_logger(__name__)`** is cached by structlog's `cache_logger_on_first_use=True` config. This is why `structlog.testing.capture_logs()` doesn't work in tests; the PR uses `caplog` instead (called out in the PR body). Acceptable trade — production gets the perf benefit, tests use the stdlib-bridge route. A follow-up could pull the get_logger inside the middleware function, but that re-enters the cache on every request (still cheap).
- **`request.url.path` in the per-request log** uses the actual URL path. If routes ever embed user IDs (`/api/v1/users/<id>`), those would land in the log. Today the only routes are `/healthz` and `/api/v1/me` — no PII in paths. Worth flagging when Week 2 adds parameterized routes; the move to `request.scope['route'].path` (the template) would address it.
- **`@app.middleware("http")`'s `_log.exception` only fires for exceptions that propagate past `call_next`.** FastAPI handles most exceptions via `register_exception_handlers` before returning a Response, so `request_failed` is mainly the deep-failure path (unhandled server errors). The successful `event=request` log on a 5xx response still fires — `status=500` is logged. That's the intended semantics.
- **The `_redact_pii` walker uses `k.lower() in _PII_KEYS`** so keys with mixed case (e.g., a header copied verbatim) are normalized. Good.

## Tests
- ✅ **12 new tests** — 5 in `test_logging.py` (redactor matrix) + 7 in `test_main.py` (validation matrix + per-request log).
- ✅ The validation matrix covers all the auditor's concerns: too-long, bad chars (quote / space / tab / semi), empty, and the happy path. Each independently verifies the response header doesn't echo the bad input.
- ✅ The per-request log test uses `caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger="backend.app.main")` correctly. Structlog routes records to stdlib via `LoggerFactory()`, so `caplog` sees them.
- ✅ The `_request_events_from_caplog` helper handles the structlog-stdlib bridge correctly (the `event_dict` survives on the LogRecord as the message payload).
- ✅ Backend coverage now **85%** overall, with `logging.py` and `main.py` both at 90%.

## Conventions
- ✅ Conventional commit (`feat(observability):`).
- ✅ `Fixes #50` and `Fixes #51` both attributed — auto-closes on merge.
- ✅ Pre-commit clean (including the new `typecheck-deps-sync` hook from PR B catching the `psycopg2-binary` add).
- ✅ `docs/progress.md` updated (both issues struck through with PR link).
- ✅ One logical functionality — all four changes are observability/security on the same code paths (logging.py + main.py middleware).
- ✅ Security comments are concrete: cite the audit date and the GDPR Article 4(1) classification for AAD object IDs.

## Security
- ✅ **Both audit findings now closed.** AAD PII no longer ships to App Insights / stdout; caller-supplied X-Request-ID can't pollute log infrastructure.
- ✅ **No new attack surface.** Both changes are additive hardening on existing code paths.
- ✅ **Fail-loud on caller errors:** invalid X-Request-ID doesn't error or warn the caller — it's silently replaced. That's the right call (don't leak validation logic to attackers); the response header tells them the canonical value.
- ✅ **Exception path closes the ContextVar** before re-raising. Verified by code reading.

## Performance
- ✅ Per-request log adds 1 structlog event per request. At ~1µs per event (cached logger) this is unmeasurable.
- ✅ Uvicorn bridge replaces inline access logging with structlog formatting — minor overhead but the previous human-readable format wasn't free either.
- ✅ ProcessorFormatter is built once at startup, cached on the handler.
- ✅ Regex compile is module-level (`_REQUEST_ID_RE`) — no per-request compile.

## Suggestions / nits (none blocking)
- **Nit:** the `_REQUEST_ID_RE` charset is `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`. W3C `tracestate` allows `:` and `,` too, so future trace propagation might need to expand. Today's scope is right.
- **Nit:** `_log.exception("request_failed", ...)` will emit the traceback under `exc_info`. Structlog's `dict_tracebacks` processor (already in the formatter chain) will format it as structured fields. Good — no change needed.
- **Nit:** The conftest's `os.environ.setdefault` doesn't override pre-existing env vars. If a contributor runs tests with `ENVIRONMENT=staging` set in their shell, the test would unexpectedly try real auth. The `setdefault` is intentional (lets contributors override for integration testing) but worth documenting if anyone gets tripped up. Acceptable today.
- **Follow-up worth tracking:** if Week 2 adds parameterized routes (e.g., `/api/v1/connections/<id>`), audit the per-request `path` log to ensure no PII / opaque-ID leakage. Either switch to route templates or scrub specific patterns.

## Risks
- **Zero runtime risk to existing functionality** beyond the intentional log-format change.
- **Operational risk lowered:** every request is now correlatable across access log + handler logs via `request_id`. App Insights ingestion will be unified rather than mixed-format.
- **CI risk: nil.** The post-fix push confirms the test job runs clean.
- **Compat risk:** API consumers expecting verbatim echo of arbitrary X-Request-ID values will see UUIDs instead when they send bad inputs. Acceptable — no consumer should be relying on echo of >64-char IDs.

## Verdict
**LGTM — safe to squash-merge.** Tight bundle: closes both #50 and #51 and addresses both audit findings in the same review, with 12 new tests, 85% backend coverage, clean conventions throughout, and verified E2E behavior recorded in the PR body. Quality engineering of a real audit response.

  "content": "import { useMsal } from '@azure/msal-react';\nimport { createContext, useMemo, type ReactNode } from 'react';\n\nimport { authMode, DEV_USER } from './config';\n\nexport interface CurrentUser {\n  name: string;\n  username: string;\n  homeAccountId: string;\n  isDev: boolean;\n}\n\nexport const CurrentUserContext = createContext<CurrentUser | null>(null);\n\n/**\n * Provides the current user to the tree.\n *\n * - dev_bypass: static dev user.\n * - unconfigured: null (AuthGate shows the banner).\n * - real: subscribes to MSAL accounts via useMsal().\n */\nexport function CurrentUserProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  if (authMode === 'dev_bypass') {\n    return (\n      <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={DEV_USER}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>\n    );\n  }\n  if (authMode === 'real') {\n    return <RealCurrentUserProvider>{children}</RealCurrentUserProvider>;\n  }\n  return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={null}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;\n}\n\nfunction RealCurrentUserProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const { accounts } = useMsal();\n  const value = useMemo<CurrentUser | null>(() => {\n    const account = accounts[0];\n    if (!account) return null;\n    return {\n      name: account.name ?? '(unknown)',\n      username: account.username,\n      homeAccountId: account.homeAccountId,\n      isDev: false,\n    };\n  }, [accounts]);\n  return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { useMsal } from '@azure/msal-react';\nimport { useMemo, type ReactNode } from 'react';\n\nimport { authMode, DEV_USER } from './config';\nimport { CurrentUserContext, type CurrentUser } from './currentUserContext';\n\n/**\n * Provides the current user to the tree.\n *\n * - dev_bypass: static dev user.\n * - unconfigured: null (AuthGate shows the banner).\n * - real: subscribes to MSAL accounts via useMsal().\n */\nexport function CurrentUserProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  if (authMode === 'dev_bypass') {\n    return (\n      <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={DEV_USER}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>\n    );\n  }\n  if (authMode === 'real') {\n    return <RealCurrentUserProvider>{children}</RealCurrentUserProvider>;\n  }\n  return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={null}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;\n}\n\nfunction RealCurrentUserProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const { accounts } = useMsal();\n  const value = useMemo<CurrentUser | null>(() => {\n    const account = accounts[0];\n    if (!account) return null;\n    return {\n      name: account.name ?? '(unknown)',\n      username: account.username,\n      homeAccountId: account.homeAccountId,\n      isDev: false,\n    };\n  }, [accounts]);\n  return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/api/client.ts",
  "content": "import axios, { type InternalAxiosRequestConfig } from 'axios';\n\nimport { authConfig, authMode } from '../auth/config';\nimport { getMsalInstance } from '../auth/msalInstance';\n\n/**\n * Shared axios instance for DataQ API calls.\n *\n * baseURL is relative (/api/v1); vite dev proxy forwards to the FastAPI\n * backend on :8000, and production same-origin deploy needs no CORS.\n *\n * Request interceptor attaches an Azure AD bearer token in real auth mode.\n * In dev_bypass / unconfigured modes the interceptor is a no-op (backend\n * dev-bypass resolves the user without a token).\n */\nexport const api = axios.create({\n  baseURL: '/api/v1',\n});\n\napi.interceptors.request.use(attachBearerToken);\n\nasync function attachBearerToken(\n  config: InternalAxiosRequestConfig,\n): Promise<InternalAxiosRequestConfig> {\n  if (authMode !== 'real') return config;\n  const instance = getMsalInstance();\n  if (!instance) return config;\n  const account = instance.getAllAccounts()[0];\n  if (!account || !authConfig.apiScopeUri) return config;\n\n  const result = await instance.acquireTokenSilent({\n    account,\n    scopes: [authConfig.apiScopeUri],\n  });\n  config.headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${result.accessToken}`);\n  return config;\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { Alert, Card, Descriptions, Spin, Typography } from 'antd';\nimport { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\n\nimport { fetchMe, type MeResponse } from '../api/me';\n\ntype LoadState =\n  | { status: 'loading' }\n  | { status: 'ok'; me: MeResponse }\n  | { status: 'error'; error: string };\n\nexport function Home() {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<LoadState>({ status: 'loading' });\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let cancelled = false;\n    fetchMe()\n      .then((me) => {\n        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', me });\n      })\n      .catch((err: unknown) => {\n        if (!cancelled) {\n          const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n          setState({ status: 'error', error: msg });\n        }\n      });\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true;\n    };\n  }, []);\n\n  if (state.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin tip=\"Loading /api/v1/me…\" size=\"large\" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;\n  }\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return (\n      <Alert\n        type=\"error\"\n        showIcon\n        title=\"Failed to load /api/v1/me\"\n        description={state.error}\n        style={{ margin: 24 }}\n      />\n    );\n  }\n  return (\n    <Card title=\"Authenticated as\">\n      <Descriptions column={1} bordered size=\"small\">\n        <Descriptions.Item label=\"Display name\">\n          {state.me.display_name ?? '—'}\n        </Descriptions.Item>\n        <Descriptions.Item label=\"Email\">{state.me.email}</Descriptions.Item>\n        <Descriptions.Item label=\"AAD object id\">\n          <Typography.Text code copyable>\n            {state.me.aad_object_id}\n          </Typography.Text>\n        </Descriptions.Item>\n        <Descriptions.Item label=\"Last seen\">{state.me.last_seen_at ?? '—'}</Descriptions.Item>\n      </Descriptions>\n    </Card>\n  );\n}\n"
}

| **4a** | Structured JSON logs at startup: `app_startup` info + `auth_dev_bypass_active` warning with the no-prod note | ✅ |
| **5a** | Production build (`pnpm build`) succeeds, dist 689 KB JS + 115 B CSS, single-page shell with crossorigin asset refs | ✅ |
| **6a** | Caller-supplied `X-Request-ID: e2e-correlation-id` propagates verbatim from frontend → vite proxy → backend → response header | ✅ |
| **6b** | When caller omits, backend generates 32-char hex id and echoes it | ✅ |

### One observation (non-blocker)
- `auth_user_resolved` debug log lines from the dev-bypass code path don't surface at INFO level. Expected — `log.debug(...)` in `auth.py:154`. If you want them in dev for debugging, set `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` in `.env`. Not worth filing.

### Verdict
**E2E healthy across the full stack.** Auth flow (dev-bypass mode), UPSERT semantics, error envelope, request-id correlation, vite proxy, production build, and DB schema all behave as designed.

Ready to `/review` + merge PR #63 when you give the green light.

**PR A [#67](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/67) opened.**

## Security audit recap (already done in background)

Two MEDIUM findings worth fixing — **folding into PR E** (observability bundle) since both touch logging / middleware:

1. **PII redactor doesn't cover AAD claim fields.** `auth_user_resolved` logs `aad_oid` and `user_id` at INFO every authenticated request. AAD `oid` is GDPR-identifier-grade. Fix: extend `_PII_KEYS` to `{oid, aad_oid, aad_object_id, upn, preferred_username, user_id, name, display_name}` or hash them.
2. **Caller-supplied `X-Request-ID` is echoed unvalidated.** No length cap, no charset whitelist. 10KB+ values bloat every log line for the request. Fix: validate against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$`; on mismatch, generate fresh UUID.

Otherwise clean: dev-bypass triple gate verified safe, fail-closed enforced, `_upsert_user` UNIQUE constraint correct, lazy AKV import correctly raises rather than silently falls back, error envelope doesn't leak stack traces, MSAL bootstrap fails loud.

Ping when PR #67 CI is green and I'll review + merge, then start PR B (#54 mypy dep consolidation).

> AGENT

**PR B [#68](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/68) opened.**

## What this fixes
- `backend/requirements-typecheck.txt` — single source of truth (one file to update for new runtime imports)
- CI installs `pip install -r backend/requirements-typecheck.txt` in both type-check + test jobs
- `scripts/check-typecheck-deps.py` — diffs the YAML against the txt, exits 1 on drift with clear "only in X / only in Y" message
- Pre-commit `typecheck-deps-sync` local hook runs the script — catches drift locally **and** in CI (via the lint job)
- Verified: positive (sync clean) + negative (added `fake-pkg`, hook correctly failed)

So new contributors update 2 files; if they forget one, the hook stops them before push. **Down from 4 places with no enforcement to 2 places with automated enforcement.**

Ping when CI is green and I'll review + merge, then move to **PR C — #43 CodeQL false-positive config**.

TITLE: chore: PR 2a — docker-compose + Pydantic Settings config

BODY:
## Summary

First slice of **PR 2 — Docker Compose + DB scaffold** (CLAUDE.md §13). Lands the runtime services + 12-factor config layer; later slices add core/logging + errors + FastAPI skeleton (PR 2b) and SQLAlchemy models + Alembic baseline (PR 2c).

- `docker-compose.yml` — `postgres:16-alpine` + `redis:7-alpine`, healthchecks, named volume for postgres data.
- `.env.example` — documents all backend env vars (consumed by both compose and Pydantic Settings).
- `backend/app/core/config.py` — Pydantic Settings (12-factor): `environment`, `log_level`, `database_url`, `redis_url`, optional `applicationinsights_connection_string`. Cached via `lru_cache`.
- `backend/` package skeleton.

## Test plan

- [x] `docker compose config -q` validates
- [x] `docker compose up -d postgres redis` → both healthy (`pg_isready`, `redis-cli ping`)
- [x] `black --check backend/` clean
- [x] `ruff check backend/` clean
- [x] `mypy backend/app/` clean
- [x] `from backend.app.core.config import get_settings; get_settings()` loads with defaults

## Notes

- App Insights middleware is no-op-when-unset per session decision; wiring lands in PR 2b alongside the FastAPI skeleton.
- The `[ -d backend ]` CI guards will become no-ops on this PR (backend/ now exists) and can be removed in a follow-up that has `workflow` scope.

=== PR #40 ===
TITLE: chore: PR 2b — structlog logging, error shape, FastAPI skeleton

BODY:
## Summary

Second slice of **PR 2 — Docker Compose + DB scaffold** (CLAUDE.md §13). Lands the FastAPI app entrypoint with cross-cutting infra that every later endpoint depends on.

### `backend/app/core/logging.py`
- structlog with JSON output, ISO timestamps, log-level injection.
- `request_id` correlation via `ContextVar` (set/reset by middleware).
- Centralised **PII redactor** (working agreement §27) — recursively walks event dicts and replaces values for known PII keys (`password`, `token`, `email`, `phone`, `ssn`, `credit_card`, etc.) with `<redacted>`.
- Optional **App Insights** wiring (working agreement §29 / CLAUDE.md §10) — when `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` is set, attaches `AzureLogHandler` to the root logger; otherwise no-op. Lazy import avoids unnecessary opencensus init at app start.

### `backend/app/core/errors.py`
- Consistent error envelope per working agreement §28:
  ```json
  { "error": { "code": "snake_case_code", "message": "Human-readable", "detail": {} } }
  ```
- `DataQError` base exception (extensible per domain) + handlers for `DataQError`, `HTTPException`, `RequestValidationError`, generic `Exception` (catches unhandled; logs via `logger.exception` → flows to App Insights when configured).
- `register_exception_handlers(app)` attaches all four.

### `backend/app/main.py`
- FastAPI app with **lifespan-managed** logging init.
- Request-ID middleware: extracts `X-Request-ID` or generates one, sets ContextVar, echoes header on response.
- Exception handlers registered.
- `/healthz` probe endpoint.

## Test plan (executed locally)

- [x] `black --check backend/` clean
- [x] `ruff check backend/` clean
- [x] `mypy backend/app/` clean (strict mode)
- [x] `uvicorn backend.app.main:app` boots without errors
- [x] `GET /healthz` → `200 {"status":"ok"}` with `x-request-id` header
- [x] `GET /no-such-route` → `404 {"error":{"code":"http_error","message":"Not Found","detail":{}}}` (envelope shape confirmed)
- [x] Inbound `X-Request-ID: test-rid-123` is propagated and echoed unchanged
- [x] When no header present, server generates a uuid4-hex rid and echoes it

## Notes

- App Insights stays no-op locally (env var unset). The lazy import means we don't pull opencensus into the import graph unless it's actually wired.
- During verification I had to sync the dataq conda env via `conda env update -n dataq -f environment.yml --prune` — the existing env predated this PR's deps. This is a one-time local issue, not a code change.
- Next: PR 2c — SQLAlchemy models + Alembic baseline.

=== PR #41 ===
TITLE: chore: PR 2c — SQLAlchemy models + Alembic baseline migration

BODY:
## Summary

Final slice of **PR 2 — Docker Compose + DB scaffold** (CLAUDE.md §13). Lands the v1 data model and the baseline migration. Closes the PR2 milestone.

### Tables (9)

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `users` | Local mirror of Azure AD identities (synced on first login). `aad_object_id` UNIQUE. |
| `connections` | **Datasources AND orchestration providers** in one table; `type` discriminates (`snowflake`/`adls_gen2`/`s3`/`unity_catalog`/`adf`/`airflow`). |
| `suites` | DQ suite definition (one connection, many checks). |
| `checks` | Individual GX expectations within a suite. |
| `runs` | DQ suite executions (status, started/finished, triggered_by). |
| `results` | Per-check outcomes within a run (observed/expected/sample_failures JSONB). |
| `shares` | Suite-level access (view/edit/admin). |
| `pipeline_runs` | **Orchestrator pipeline/DAG executions — NOT same as `runs`.** Provider-tagged. |
| `trigger_bindings` | Provider-agnostic mapping `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env)` → suite. |

### Design decisions baked in (signed off earlier this session)

- **UUID v4 PKs throughout** — `gen_random_uuid()` server default (PG 13+ core function, no extension).
- **Severity tier columns deferred to Week 3** — baseline ships without; added backward-compatibly per working-agreement §30.
- **Hard delete only** — no `deleted_at`. YAGNI for v1.
- **Local `users` table mirroring AAD** — `aad_object_id` UNIQUE; FK from `shares.user_id`, `connections.created_by`, `suites.created_by`.
- **TEXT + CHECK** for status/type enums (not native PG enums) — easier to evolve via migration.
- **`results.sample_failures_purged_at`** column added now so the W5 Celery sweep doesn't need a follow-up migration. Retention: `SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS=30`.

### Infra

- `backend/app/db/base.py` — `DeclarativeBase` with explicit naming convention (`pk_`/`fk_`/`ix_`/`uq_`/`ck_` prefixes).
- `backend/app/db/models.py` — all 9 tables; relationships only where they matter (e.g. `Suite.checks` cascade).
- `backend/app/db/session.py` — engine + `sessionmaker` (with `pool_pre_ping=True`).
- `backend/alembic.ini` + `env.py` + `script.py.mako` — template uses PEP 604 (`X | Y`) typing to satisfy ruff `UP007`.

TITLE: feat(auth): backend Azure AD bearer-token validation + /api/v1/me (PR 3a)

BODY:
## Summary

PR 3a — first slice of PR 3 (Azure AD SSO end-to-end). Adds backend MSAL bearer-token validation, the \`/api/v1/me\` endpoint, and user upsert on every authenticated request.

Design signed off in the previous conversation turn:
- ✅ Library: \`fastapi-azure-auth\` (5.2.0)
- ✅ Dev strategy: \`.env\` placeholders + \`AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true\` for local dev
- ✅ User upsert: every request (refreshes email / display_name / last_seen_at)
- ✅ Key Vault: deferred to PR 3b (abstraction)

## What lands

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`environment.yml\` | Pin \`fastapi-azure-auth==5.2.0\` |
| \`.pre-commit-config.yaml\` | Add \`fastapi-azure-auth==5.2.0\` to mypy deps |
| \`.env.example\` | New Azure block: \`AZURE_TENANT_ID\`, \`AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID\`, \`AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID\`, \`AZURE_API_SCOPE\`, \`AUTH_DEV_BYPASS\` |
| \`backend/app/core/config.py\` | Settings additions + \`azure_auth_configured\` / \`azure_api_scope_uri\` properties |
| \`backend/app/core/auth.py\` | **New.** Two-mode auth (real / dev-bypass) + user upsert + structured log + \`init_auth()\` |
| \`backend/app/db/session.py\` | Add \`get_db()\` FastAPI dependency generator |
| \`backend/app/api/v1/me.py\` | **New.** \`GET /api/v1/me\` returns the resolved current user |
| \`backend/app/main.py\` | Wire \`init_auth()\` into lifespan; mount router |

## Two operating modes

**Real mode** (production / staging): \`AZURE_TENANT_ID\` + \`AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID\` set → \`fastapi-azure-auth\` validates issuer, audience, signature, expiry, scope. OIDC config loaded once at startup.

**Dev bypass** (local only): \`ENVIRONMENT=dev\` + \`AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true\` + Azure vars empty → no token required; every request resolves to a fixed dev user (\`aad_object_id=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001\`).

**Fail-closed**: any other configuration raises at startup. Verified — booting with \`ENVIRONMENT=staging AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true\` (no Azure config) yields \`RuntimeError: Auth not configured...\` and the app exits.

## Verified locally

- \`pre-commit run --all-files\` clean across all hooks (ruff, black, mypy strict, bandit, gitleaks, etc.).
- \`docker compose up -d postgres redis\` + \`alembic upgrade head\` from a clean DB.
- \`AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true uvicorn ...\` boots, structured log shows \`auth_dev_bypass_active\` warning at startup.
- \`GET /api/v1/me\` (request 1) → \`200\`, creates user row with \`last_seen_at=T1\`.
- \`GET /api/v1/me\` (request 2) → \`200\`, same \`id\`, \`last_seen_at\` advances to \`T2\` (UPSERT working).
- DB check: exactly one row in \`users\`, \`created_at\` unchanged across requests.
- Fail-closed check: \`ENVIRONMENT=staging\` refuses to boot.

## Test plan
- [x] \`pre-commit run --all-files\` clean.
- [x] \`/api/v1/me\` returns dev user in bypass mode.
- [x] UPSERT updates \`last_seen_at\` without creating duplicate rows.
- [x] Fail-closed in non-dev environments.
- [ ] CI green.

## What's NOT in this PR (deferred to 3b / 3c)
- **PR 3b**: \`SecretStore\` abstraction (\`AzureKeyVaultStore\` + \`EnvSecretStore\`). Real Azure Key Vault provisioning defers to Week 7.
- **PR 3c**: Frontend MSAL flow (\`@azure/msal-react\`), \`<AuthGate>\`, axios interceptor, login UI. Folds in #38 (antd-icons version reconcile).

TITLE: feat(secrets): SecretStore abstraction (env + Azure Key Vault) (PR 3b)

BODY:
## Summary

PR 3b — second slice of PR 3. Wires the SecretStore abstraction with two backends, lazy-imports the Azure SDK, and lands the first pytest suite in the repo.

Design signed off earlier:
- ✅ Protocol with \`get(name) -> str\`
- ✅ \`EnvSecretStore\` (local dev) + \`AzureKeyVaultStore\` (prod/staging)
- ✅ \`secret_store\` enum in Settings, \`azure_key_vault_url\` for AKV mode
- ✅ Real Azure provisioning defers to Week 7

## What lands

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`backend/app/core/secrets.py\` | **New.** Protocol, two implementations, lazy Azure SDK import, cached factory, test-reset hook |
| \`backend/app/core/config.py\` | \`secret_store\` Literal + \`azure_key_vault_url\` settings |
| \`.env.example\` | \`SECRET_STORE\`, \`AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL\`, example \`KV_SECRET_*\` pattern |
| \`backend/tests/conftest.py\` | **New.** Autouse fixture clears settings/secret-store caches between tests; \`clean_kv_env\` strips \`KV_SECRET_*\` vars |
| \`backend/tests/core/test_secrets.py\` | **New.** 12 tests covering env-key normalisation, env store happy/missing paths, AKV mocked happy path + SDK-exception wrapping + None-value, factory selection + error path, cache + reset |
| \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` | Pytest deps now include \`pydantic\` / \`pydantic-settings\` / \`structlog\` (required at test import time). Sync requirement comment added |

## Why the abstraction now

The \`connections.secret_ref\` column already exists (PR 2c) holding KV secret names. Once Week 2 datasource CRUD lands, anything reading a connection's credentials needs \`SecretStore.get(connection.secret_ref)\`. By landing the abstraction now, Week 2 work can take a clean dependency rather than pattern-matching on env-var fallbacks.

## Lazy import + cost

\`AzureKeyVaultStore.__init__\` builds nothing. The Azure SDK (\`azure-identity\`, \`azure-keyvault-secrets\`) imports happen inside \`_client_lazy()\` only when \`.get()\` is first called. EnvSecretStore-only deployments never trigger the import — verified by the \`test_akv_store_lazy_client_not_built_on_init\` test.

## Test posture

12 tests, 87% coverage on \`secrets.py\` (the uncovered lines are the actual Azure SDK import, deferred to Week 7 integration tests against a real vault). First pytest suite in the repo — establishes the \`backend/tests/<module-mirror>/test_<module>.py\` convention and the autouse cache-reset fixture pattern.

Per working-agreement principle 6: *Tests are written in the slice they belong to.*

## Verified locally
- [x] \`pytest backend/tests/\` — 12 passing, 0 failing, 87% module coverage.
- [x] \`pre-commit run --all-files\` clean.
- [x] Bandit S105 false-positive on \`secret_store = "env"\` suppressed with explanatory \`noqa\` (mode selector, not a password).

## CI infra sync

CI test deps now include the runtime packages tests transitively import. This is the same drift pattern as #45 / #54 — adding to issue #54 backlog (consolidate type-check + test dep lists into a single source of truth).

## Test plan
- [x] Local pytest green.
- [x] Local pre-commit clean.
- [ ] CI green.

## What's NOT in this PR (deferred to 3c)
- **PR 3c**: Frontend MSAL flow + login UI + axios interceptor. Folds in #38 antd-icons.

## Summary

Bundles in the #38 antd-icons v6 bump since we're touching frontend.

Design signed off earlier:
- ✅ Redirect token flow (loginRedirect / acquireTokenSilent)
- ✅ Dev-bypass mirrors backend
- ✅ Single PR, four commits
- ✅ Relative \`/api/v1\` + vite dev proxy (no CORS)

## Commits

| # | Title | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | \`feat(frontend): React app scaffold\` | First React code in the repo. index.html, main.tsx, App.tsx, styles.css, antd ConfigProvider/App. Plus tsconfig hygiene (composite mode was emitting artifacts; folded into single tsconfig). |
| 2 | \`feat(auth): MSAL provider + AuthGate + dev-bypass mode\` | config.ts (authMode from VITE_*), msalInstance.ts (PublicClientApplication, real-mode-only), MsalProvider / CurrentUserProvider / useCurrentUser split for react-refresh, AuthGate with three paths, async bootstrap in main.tsx per #62. First Vitest in the repo (4 tests). |
| 3 | \`feat(api): axios client + bearer-token interceptor + /me page\` | api/client.ts (acquireTokenSilent → Authorization), api/me.ts (typed fetch), pages/Home.tsx with loading/ok/error state. 3 more tests. |
| 4 | \`chore(frontend): bump @ant-design/icons to ^6.2.3 (#38)\` | Aligns icons with antd v6.4.3. |

## /review — PR 2b (logging + errors + FastAPI skeleton)

**Verdict:** merge-ready. All 10 CI checks green. Smoke-tested locally: healthz, 404 envelope, X-Request-ID inbound propagation, auto-generation when absent — all confirmed.

**Notable design choices that look right:**
- Unhandled exception handler returns generic message — no detail leak.
- PII redactor contract is kwargs-only (matches the working-agreement intent: enforce centrally, callers must use kwargs not f-strings).
- App Insights handler is lazy-imported only when connection string is set — no opencensus in import graph otherwise.
- `assert isinstance` pattern in handlers narrows for mypy; safe because FastAPI dispatches by registered type.

**Minor (non-blocking, defer):**
- PII keys are exact-match (`email` matches, `user_email` doesn't). Substring matching is one keystroke but risks false positives (`secretary` → `secret`). Tune later against real log samples rather than guessing now.
- `dict_tracebacks` ships exception args verbatim; redactor only sees dict keys, not string values. Caller discipline — don't put PII in exception messages.
- CORS middleware not yet wired — out of scope; lands when frontend starts hitting the API.

**Heads-up for PR 2c (next):** SQLAlchemy + Alembic baseline. Schema includes the `pipeline_runs` and `trigger_bindings` tables — make sure ADR 0004's orchestration-abstraction shape is reflected before the migration is locked in.

## Overview
